🏍️ Did You Know?

Burt Munro got faster... 37 years after he died.

His famous 1967 Bonneville run was originally recorded at 183.586 mph.

In 2014, that figure was corrected to 184.087 mph (296.3 km/h), confirming Burt had actually gone even faster than first recorded.

Nearly five decades after setting the record, history finally caught up with the man from Invercargill.

【 逗子アートフェスティバル2026 
オープニングイベント開催！ 】

2022年、コロナ禍の中で開催された
現代アートの祭典『documenta fifteen』。
CINEMA CARAVAN ＋ 栗林隆で招待され、
ドイツ・カッセルで過ごした100日間。
そのとき掲げられたスローガンは
“NO ART MAKE FRIENDS”
物質的な作品を残すこと以上に、
「人との関係性を深くすること」こそがこれからの時代に大切なアートの要素。
それは、僕たちがCINEMA CARAVANや逗子海岸映画祭を通じてずっと表現し続けてきたことそのものでした。
インドネシアの仲間（ルアンルパ）がキュレーターになり声をかけてもらった時、「そのテーマなら日本最高峰かも」と勝手に自画自賛しながら、慣れないアート界に飛び込んだあの経験は、今も僕たちの歴史に深く刻まれています。
そして今回。
あのカッセルでの日々に迫ったドキュメンタリー映像作品を、なんと総勢25人もの音楽家と一緒に上映します。
映像と生演奏が重なり合う、間違いなく圧巻の時間になります。
ぜひ会場へ遊びに来てください！

Special GUEST（第2部）
◾️KOM_I（アーティスト・歌手） 声を主に用いて表現活動を行う。日本の郷土芸能や民俗学、北インドの古典音楽に影響を受けている。 主な音楽作品に、オオルタイチと制作した『YAKUSHIMA TREASURE』や、食品まつりa.k.a foodmanと発表した『FANI MANI』。気候危機について歌った『なんか地球がおかしい』など。

◾️青森うぐいす姉妹 800年の伝統を持つ南部手踊り発祥の地、青森県南部町生まれ。 姉・西塚繭子、妹・西塚淳子ともに3歳から民謡を習い、民謡と南部手踊りの世界で、史上初となる姉妹での全国チャンピオンを成し遂げる。 唄い、踊り、三味線を弾く。 幼い頃から身体に染み込んだ南部の芸を、姉妹ならではの息の合った舞台で届けている。
西塚淳子 第63代青森県民謡王座、第11回南部七踊り全国大会優勝ほか、数々の大会で優勝。 津軽三味線世界大会の唄付けや、南部七踊り全国大会などの本部伴奏を務める。全国200件以上の福祉施設を訪問し、フィリピン公演では4,000人を動員。 民謡、津軽三味線、南部手踊り。それぞれの師匠から受け継いだ技術と精神を忠実に表現しながら、三つの芸を自在に操る、確かな実力を持つ総合芸能者。

西塚繭子 第31代青森県手踊り名人位、第69代青森県民謡王座。南部手踊り全国大会優勝ほか、数々の大会で受賞。 女性として史上初となる「青森県手踊り名人位」と「青森県民謡王座」の二冠を成し遂げる。 活動の拠点を関東に移し、民謡や踊りに興味を持つ全国のミュージシャンやダンサーなどの民謡とは異なるジャンルの表現者にも積極的に指導し、日本の魂を覚醒させている。 伝統とは、革新を続けること 今回のオーケストラと南部民謡の共演は目指す革新そのものです。

プログラム・出演者紹介
『beyond documenta fifteen』（監督：志津野雷） “アートのオリンピック”とも呼ばれる国際芸術祭「documenta fifteen」。全体キュレーターのルアンルパへのインタビューを軸に、CINEMA CARAVAN×栗林隆の実践と「NO ART MAKE FRIENDS」の思想が響き合う姿を、notremusica orchestraの生演奏とともに上映予定。

志津野 雷 写真家・映像作家。世界各地を旅しながら自然、文化、人々の営みを撮影し、写真・映像作品を発表。2010年、逗子を拠点にCINEMA CARAVANを立ち上げる。映画、音楽、食、アートを横断し、地域と世界をつなぐ表現の場を国内外で展開している。

辰田 翔 / notremusica orchestra 作曲、ピアノ、哲学を学ぶ。自身のオーケストラ『NMO』で作曲・指揮・ピアノを担当。ファッション、映画、広告、自治体、芸術祭などへ幅広く音楽・音響作品を提供する。美術分野でも映像、空間、インスタレーション、立体造形、建築など多角的な作品制作を行っている。

いよいよZAF2026オープニングまで2週間を切りました！

今回自分企画で、特に観てもらいたいのが、『beyond documenta fifteen』× 生オーケストラ。

これだけの規模の生オーケストラでこの作品を上映できる機会は、正直なかなか作れません。
次にいつできるかもわからないので、ぜひこの機会に観てもらいたいです！

10月3日（土）、逗子文化プラザ・なぎさホールで開催する、逗子アートフェスティバル2026のオープニングイベント。

第1部では、CINEMA CARAVAN 志津野雷監督の『beyond documenta fifteen』を、notremusica orchestraの生演奏とともに上映します。

ドイツ・カッセルで開催された「documenta fifteen」でのCINEMA CARAVANの活動とルアンルパの思想を記録した作品。地域と地域、人と人がつながり、それぞれの場所で文化や場をつくっていくという、自分たちが大切にしてきたことにもつながる作品です。

第2部は、notremusica orchestraのLIVE。
こちらもこれだけのメンバーが揃って演奏すること自体なかなかない機会です。大編成ならではの生の音を、ぜひホールで体感してください。スペシャルゲストにkom_Iの参加も決まっています。

そして中学生以下は無料！
楽器を習っている子どもたちにも、きっと良い刺激になると思います。ぜひご家族でも。

さらにチケット購入者には、今年のZAFメイン会場「本田邸」の無料入場チケットも付いてきます。

せっかく実現したこの機会、できるだけ多くの人に観てもらいたいです。

いろいろなイベントが重なっている10月3日ですが、ぜひお誘い合わせの上見に来てください。

Burt Munro Challenge ambassador @cormacracing proudly represented us during a television interview with UK broadcaster @tntsportsbikes at the German Grand Prix. 👏🏍️

Cormac thrived at the tight and technical Sachsenring circuit and was on the pace from the outset, finishing P9 in the opening FP1 session and P8 in practice to secure a direct spot in Q2. Even more impressively, his lap times were just 0.3 seconds and 0.1 seconds respectively off the fastest rider.

After recording his best qualifying result of the season in P11 (+0.5), Cormac expertly managed tyre challenges during the race to secure a strong P13 finish and add more valuable Moto3 World Championship points to his tally.

We're proud to see Cormac representing the Burt Munro Challenge on the world stage. 🔥

📸 Manu Tormo

【和歌山旅の記録 8/6 - 8/10】
朝2時に葉山を出発。お昼過ぎに撮影クルーと待ち合わせし岡崎ニットさんで職人の想いに触れた後、夕暮れの潮岬で言葉を失うほど美しいサンセットに巡り合う。夜は那智勝浦に到着し、紹介してもらった佐藤由明君のバーで夕飯がてら素敵な夜を過ごした。
8/7
備長炭職人のヤン君と合流。
本州最南端のサーフポイントを案内してもらう
インドネシアのような透明度の高い青い海と綺麗なグーフィーの波を堪能。夕方は下里で台風の残しうねりを楽しむ。
8/8、ライオンズゲートが最も強まる日に那智大社へ。八咫烏の眠る岩や天照大神の社に挨拶。
遅めのランチ食べて夕方波乗りに。
夜は山奥のヤン君の家で、名スケーターバンド「ワセリンズ」の即興ライブ。寝床のすぐ横が最高のライブスタジオに変貌する贅沢な夜。

8/9は早朝から下里で朝イチサーフィン。残った良い波を堪能した後、すさみ町へ移動。
来年のシネマキャラバンの実現に向けた打ち合わせへ。「場所が人を育てる」という考えのもと、町民も県外から来る人も垣根なく自由に受け入れようとする町長の温かい心構えと深い地域愛に強く共感。来年ここで何か面白いことができそうな熱い予感を抱いて、聖地・高野山へ向かった。
8/10
早朝の奥の院で空海へ朝食を届ける「生身供」に参列。お坊さんたちの祈りを聞きながら、歩き回って体感した立体曼荼羅。
「人間主体」ではなく「自然主体」で生きること。自分を愛し、人を愛することを突き進む決意を宇宙に投げかける、静かで強い時間だった。
〆は3万歩歩いた足疲れを花山温泉の冷泉で癒やして帰路へ。
すべてが完璧に巡った5日間でした
ヤン君、よしあき君ありがとうございました♪

@_photosbyblair | Photographer Showcase Ep. 03 📸

Next up in our Photographer Showcase series is Blair Eastwood.

Based in Wānaka, Blair usually spends his days photographing nature and wildlife. But every now and then, it’s good to trade the mountains for something a little louder.

✨ “Morph was a different kind of wild. Incredible people, great energy, and unreal colour.”

When we asked what brought him to Morph this year, his answer made us smile:

“My amazing sister Stace was shooting Morph and we’ve always wanted to shoot a festival together. I’ve recently moved back to Aotearoa and we finally managed to do one! It was so special walking around sharing tips, lenses and mealtimes together across the weekend.”

There’s something really special about seeing Morph through Blair’s lens. His eye for colour, light and genuine moments brought a fresh perspective to the weekend, capturing both the energy of the festival and the quieter moments in between.

Thank you, Blair, for being part of our very first Morph and for sharing your beautiful work with us 💚

🏁 26 August 1967

On this day, Burt Munro recorded an average speed of 184.087 mph (296.259 km/h) at the Bonneville Salt Flats, setting a world record in the Class S-A 1000cc category aboard his modified 1920 Indian Scout.

It was the achievement of a lifelong pursuit and a moment that would forever connect Southland with the world of motorcycle racing.

Each year on 26 August, riders and motorsport fans pause to remember the day Burt's name was etched into the record books, not simply for the speed he achieved, but for what the achievement represents: the pursuit of a goal, no matter how ambitious.

As we mark this historic anniversary, we also look ahead to another milestone. In February 2027, the Burt Munro Challenge celebrates 20 years, bringing together the people, motorcycles, and stories that continue to keep Burt's legacy alive.

Imagine growing up thinking this was normal:
Your parents dancing until their feet hurt. 
People actually knowing their neighbours. 
Making a new best mate in about four minutes. 
Running around outside all day while a whole bunch of adults are looking out for you.

We think about that a lot when we’re building Morph.
Obviously we want to create an unreal few days. We want incredible music, beautiful spaces, good food, dancing, workshops, ALL of it ✨

But there’s a bigger reason we want kids here too.
We want them to grow up seeing adults play. 
Seeing people help each other. 
Meeting all kinds of humans. 
Feeling like they belong somewhere bigger than their own little family.
And maybe one day they’ll be the ones creating these spaces for us.

That’s a pretty f*cking beautiful thought 💚
For now though, we’ll keep building it for them, and for all of us.

Together we Morph.

【逗子アートフェスティバル関連情報】

10月3日（土）に文化プラザホールで開催される「ZAF2026 OPENING ACT」に、KOM_I（コムアイ）、青森うぐいす姉妹のスペシャルゲストとしての参加が決定しました！

CINEMA CARAVAN/CINEMA AMIGOの長島 源が共同代表を務める『逗子アートフェスティバル(ZAF)』。

ZAF2026の幕開けを彩る、特別な一夜です。 志津野雷による『beyond documenta fifteen』の上映と生演奏に加え、さらにスペシャルゲストを迎えて、オープニングを盛り上げます。
ぜひ会場で、この日限りの時間をお楽しみください。

Special GUEST（第2部）
◾️KOM_I（アーティスト・歌手） 声を主に用いて表現活動を行う。日本の郷土芸能や民俗学、北インドの古典音楽に影響を受けている。 主な音楽作品に、オオルタイチと制作した『YAKUSHIMA TREASURE』や、食品まつりa.k.a foodmanと発表した『FANI MANI』。気候危機について歌った『なんか地球がおかしい』など。
　
◾️青森うぐいす姉妹 800年の伝統を持つ南部手踊り発祥の地、青森県南部町生まれ。 姉・西塚繭子、妹・西塚淳子ともに3歳から民謡を習い、民謡と南部手踊りの世界で、史上初となる姉妹での全国チャンピオンを成し遂げる。 唄い、踊り、三味線を弾く。 幼い頃から身体に染み込んだ南部の芸を、姉妹ならではの息の合った舞台で届けている。

西塚淳子 第63代青森県民謡王座、第11回南部七踊り全国大会優勝ほか、数々の大会で優勝。 津軽三味線世界大会の唄付けや、南部七踊り全国大会などの本部伴奏を務める。全国200件以上の福祉施設を訪問し、フィリピン公演では4,000人を動員。 民謡、津軽三味線、南部手踊り。それぞれの師匠から受け継いだ技術と精神を忠実に表現しながら、三つの芸を自在に操る、確かな実力を持つ総合芸能者。

西塚繭子 第31代青森県手踊り名人位、第69代青森県民謡王座。南部手踊り全国大会優勝ほか、数々の大会で受賞。 女性として史上初となる「青森県手踊り名人位」と「青森県民謡王座」の二冠を成し遂げる。 活動の拠点を関東に移し、民謡や踊りに興味を持つ全国のミュージシャンやダンサーなどの民謡とは異なるジャンルの表現者にも積極的に指導し、日本の魂を覚醒させている。 伝統とは、革新を続けること 今回のオーケストラと南部民謡の共演は目指す革新そのものです。

Bali Spirit Festival is the origin story for so many wellness festivals around the world and it is on this week, 15th - 19th April! 🥳

So we wanted to share our respects by showing some of our favourite moments at the festival over the years 🙌🏽  @balispiritfest have been pioneers in this space for decades now and we take great inspiration from them in everything we do at @morphfest   We call them our sister festival but in reality they are more like a mother 🙏🏽  So if you want to experience the origin of this movement, get your tickets to Bali Spirit Festival 🙌🏽  Use the code MORPHTOBALI to get 20% off 👌🏽  There are lots of the Morph Crew performing this year, so you will see them there!
🏆 Les presentamos a los ganadores de las categorías del día sábado  de la Mandinga Tattoo Expo 🖤🔥

The end made us pretty emotional, actually 🥹

Because underneath all the different answers, everyone kept coming back to the same things.

The people.
The whenua.
The friendships.
The crew.
The feeling of being somewhere you can just be yourself.

And yeah, of course we love the music. We love the stages, the dancing, the ridiculous outfits...

But somewhere in between all of that is the reason we really keep coming back.

It’s the person you meet at 2am who somehow feels like an old friend.
The conversations you didn’t plan on having.
The people you came with, and the people you leave with.

👉🏽That’s a huge part of WHY we built Morph in the first place.

Not because the world needed another festival.

Because we still believe we need places to gather like this.

And hearing people say it back to us in their own words... yeah. That got us 🤍

Here’s to doing it all again in 2027!

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #726 | 24 SEPTEMBER 2026

RDT rules finally passed for NSW but I keep reading misunderstandings about it. As I see it, there will be no change to the testing roadside, just different punishments. If you have a prescription and register you should no longer get into trouble, so long as you are not impaired and no alcohol or other drugs! 

Pathetic really, but never forget this is war and we’re negotiating peace and this is just the first step. Finally you can consume your medical cannabis and drive and no longer be a criminal. You still might have to leave your car for 24 hours, nothing has changed there, but otherwise it’s a win for a lot of people who are happy getting their legal weed in the mail. A big thank you to Legalise Cannabis’ Jeremy Buckingham.

Hopefully now he can focus on the real job at hand which is allowing us to grow our own medicine and how to begin winding back the whole disastrous drug war… I virtually never do edibles, as they call it in weed world. A cookie can take a couple of hours to take full affect and then it can be too much or too little. That’s why the majority of us cannabis users smoke, we can feel when we’ve had enough. The effect is quickly into our bloodstream, then our brain.

It was half-time in the weekly Friday Hemp Hour on NIM-FM and I hadn’t eaten all day and got tempted by a chocolate ‘cookie’. As soon as I tasted it I knew it was strong, but down the hatch and I soon forgot about it. A couple of hours later it hit me like a freight train...

Smoking is in fact the way to self titrate your medical cannabis dose, but it is also the one that activates your saliva for RDT. As the police have said in the past, if you smoke we’ll catch you, if you eat a cookie, maybe we will, but if you swallow a capsule, we can’t detect it. This has encouraged many to not smoke but ingest in other ways which can be less safe, unless you know exactly the amount you need and the strength of the buds.

Love to everyone and keep your sense of humour handy if you can.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #725 | 17 SEPTEMBER 2026
High Headliners! 
I had a win in court on Monday with my old mate and legal wiz John Weller convincing the Magistrate to allow me to keep driving, albeit with a two year good behaviour clause. Coincidentally, the new RDT bill* will hopefully pass in NSW Parliament today, finally getting over the numerous road blocks. It’s a small but significant change I maintain, with no more automatic loss of licence, if you register with transport etcetera. 

This Headlines is full of great stories from Portugal, Switzerland, Holland, South Africa, India and more. The legendary Ed Rosenthal has turned his cannabis law reform radar on India which was forced to join everyone else and make their sacred ganja illegal in 1961. Did I forget they were given 25 years to “clean up their act” so in fact ganja didn’t really became illegal there until 1986. 

So my decade of going back and forth to the land of the Hindus, smoking copious chillums (pipes) with sadhus (spiritual disciples), was all legal times. We certainly never got in any trouble and I remember you could buy legal government grown ganja in some states. It didn't compare to the hash which was coming in from Afghanistan, Pakistan and northern India, by the tonne. 

How’s the AFP Police Commissioner trotting out that same old line blaming drug users for the gang shootings in Sydney? Now if everybody would stop using cocaine and meth all this violence would stop. I feel for the cops who are just going backwards in every way fighting this unwinnable drug war. Their morale is low and their numbers are down, understandably. We’re asking the impossible of the police. Time to start seriously questioning the drug war.
Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #729 | 15 OCTOBER 2026

High Headliners!

...Changing cultural practices is a slow process, but there is no doubt it is happening. Research consistently shows that people who use cannabis decrease their alcohol use and in many cases stop it altogether. When Americans are surveyed, the majority believe cannabis is a much healthier option than alcohol. We seem a long way behind that here.

In the Western Australian Parliament, Dr Brian Walker argued this week that grog poses a greater societal danger than pot and asked the Government to investigate a regulatory framework that treats each according to the evidence and harm. Way too rational for them I suspect.

There was yet another disappointing television show about the dangers of legal weed being unapproved and too high in THC, this time by SBS. Stories from people who have little experience, it sounds like, and doctors who pull out the same closed-minded nonsense. 

Their blindness in only allowing indoor, mostly hydroponic pot to be legal (and then it must be irradiated, but most importantly so little is organic), is a big part of the problem. Powerful chemical fertilisers are growing most of our food as well and I just know it’s not healthy.

Basically the authorities can’t handle that the horse has bolted, when they opened up Telehealth during the pandemic. Has anyone died from cannabis yet? No. Are thousands more getting huge pain relief from it? Yes. Will it lessen the stigma? Yes. They still don’t comprehend we have an Endocannabinoid System, each one of us.

Easily the highlight of my week was reading Lucy Haslam’s freshly penned story of her discovery of cannabis via her son Dan’s cancer treatments. And it’s not over yet, she’s still in the trenches, arguing for us all, trying to get heard by the rule-makers, as determined as ever. The book is available through print on demand via Lucy’s website (https://authorlucyhaslam.com/). It’s an inspiring story, also available on Amazon. A great read.

Love to everyone.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #728 | 8 OCTOBER 2026

High Headliners!

I was hanging out in Colombo at the ancient Buddhist Temple and got to know an old monk who spoke good English. I was telling him how magic mushrooms changed my life and he said, “Do you want to see how Buddha got enlightened?”.
It was an experience to remember.

He led me down into the bowels of the Temple, pulled an ancient key out from under his robe and opened an equally ancient cupboard with it. He pulled out an old book, the pages looking very handmade, which told the story of Buddha’s journey. There were simple drawings in the book, which was helpful, because I couldn’t read any Sanskrit.

He found the page and read it to me. Buddha had reached the end of his search for Truth and sat down under the Bodhi Tree and fasted for thirty days. He was determined to sit there until he attained awakening. Figs were falling from the tree and lay scattered around him on the ground. Birds were eating the fermented ones and getting drunk, falling over and so on. Buddha ate some and was enlightened and that was it! When I think about it, after fasting for so long, the alcoholic figs would have done the job. However, not all Buddhist’s I tell that story to like it! 

Four Corners on the ABC wasted a show this week, I thought, on a few companies ripping off the DVA by prescribing huge amounts of weed to Veterans, just like the NDIS rip offs. The real story for me is doctors who have no cannabis experience, being the prescribers. They’re so fortunate no one can die from using cannabis as they have no idea about it, a lot of them, and everybody is different. Experience is the real teacher.

I like that PlantMed wont prescribe THC without CBD as well. Just imagine if they let the hippies, who’ve used weed for decades, sell medicine from dispensaries, as well as cuttings of cultivars, suited to your needs, that you could grow at home. That’s the dream and I’m sticking to it! 

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #718 | 30 JULY 2026
High Headliners!
I’m still so naive, I’m shocked by dishonesty. Prohibition has been good at teaching people to lie, but some just do it as part of their job, it seems. I mean, we all care about road safety I imagine, so why not be transparent about the saliva testing results, as we all try and work out if and how it can work? Why not be honest and open?

It is because they’re using road safety as an arm of the drug war, Dr Michael White from the University of Adelaide tells us. And there’s been nothing as effective as RDT in stopping cannabis use. Just the fact we’re not told our saliva test results is a problem for a start. If we were, it would quickly become apparent the results are all over the place and hold little relevance to safety on the roads. My saliva tested at 1200ng and the copper agreed I didn't look impaired, and I wasn’t.

Now I read how they did trials at Swinburne, five years ago and buried the results because they clearly showed how hopeless the spit tests are at detecting THC. The unpublished experiment involved 40 subjects who used their normal dose of THC medicine and were tested 1, 2, 4 and 6 hours after use. The non-detection rate was 40% after 1 hour; 65% after 2 hours: 70% after 4 hours and 77% after 6 hours. Police say they will, “inevitably catch cannabis use in drivers for up to 24 hours after use”. Bald-face lying they can justify, to themselves at least, because this is a war.

Drug use is not bad, we’ve just been told that. It’s actually awesome and important, if you do it right which is not so easy, with a war going on against you. It’s almost forgotten that it’s been a normal part of human behaviour forever until a hundred years ago, when the ‘Reefer Madness’ propaganda campaign began.

The truth will set us free, we just need to be open to it, in this fast changing, exciting and amazing time on Earth.

Love to everyone!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #719 | 6 AUGUST 2026
High Headliners!
I’ve been on the road for the last week, just loving the natural Aussie bush, native trees with very few weeds. Anxious cannabis users driving around outback Queensland, tensing up every time we see a cop car, a cop shop. Where do we smoke a joint? In the middle of nowhere. We met a good country woman in an op shop who had the shakes, early Parkinson’s. “Have you thought about trying cannabis?”, I asked. “I hear it’s a problem driving”.

Shame on the bullies running the State... blindly doubling the punishment for drug driving offences in Queensland, including mandatory imprisonment for repeat offenders! A new war against cannabis users. Please spread the word about the 25 August RDT Protest at Parliament House in Brisbane (see details below). I’m looking for a lift so I don’t have to drive, like everyone else!

South of the border in New South Wales the new Bill to let medical cannabis patients drive passed the Legislative Assembly. The Bill now goes to the Upper House for debate. The Transport Minister assured parliament info they want from us will not link to automatic number plate recognition. One thing we importantly need is for anyone’s saliva who is tested to be given the results and interstate drivers with a prescription have an escape clause. Jeremy will be trying to pass amendments but the new system is a solid step forward. We’ll have to work on it when they review it. It will be a big relief to be able to drive knowing they can test me twice and I can have any amount of nanograms of pot in my saliva and not lose my licence. 

Sometimes I want to put a sign on the outskirts of the village… “Welcome to Nimbin—May contain traces of nuts”... We try hard to deal with any mental health episodes ourselves rather than call police so I was really happy to see the announcement NSW is getting a new statewide mental health emergency response model, which will see more appropriate people attending those incidents rather than police, unless they’re really necessary. It’s been shaped by the English, ‘Right Care Right Person’ Program, which makes good sense.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #721 | 20 AUGUST 2026
I’ve been thinking about the story from New York in last week’s Headlines about the all-in-one permit that allows a small operator to cultivate, manufacture and sell weed at Farmers Markets and the like. “Small craft cannabis cultivators”, sounds like the dream to me.

In most of the world if you don’t work you don’t eat. Family becomes huge just to look after each other. Survival isn’t an issue here, there is always food somewhere. I can vouch for the skips behind the supermarkets in affluent Canberra. 

Wandering the planet showed me how little money has to do with happiness and how hard in fact it is to be rich, with so many choices like we have here. We would grow tired of rice and dahl every night, but for most, so long as the bowl is full, they are happy and grateful. Happier than us, generally, I think.

So I come back to cannabis and how many people would just love it if they could earn a living from growing their favourite vegetable, instead of letting Big Cannabis take over the market.

“Regulated cannabis has proven to be an economic engine for New York”, they’re saying and it could be the same here, I reckon. Thousands of Aussie tokers would love a small licence, say between 20-50 square metres, or even much smaller. It could just be your six home grown plants, but you could sell them at the market. 

Thousands of people would go off the dole or the pension. Thousands would love their job, many of whom have been learning it covertly for decades. Thousands would have a meaningful and purposeful life, which is not easy to find in this world right now. I'll keep dreaming.

Meanwhile it’s encouraging to read that global cannabis use is up forty percent as we follow, “a continuum of gradual normalisation towards cannabis use”. There’s hope for us yet!

Love to all!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #727 | 1 OCTOBER 2026
I’ve been visiting the massive brand new Tweed Hospital nearby, built in the middle of prime farmland. My old mate James Kingsbury, otherwise known to many of you as Heathen Lovechild, is who I’m visiting, and he’s very sick. As is Jim Moylan, who is going through an experimental new chemo trial, while choofing as much as he can which the doctors are of course fascinated by.

The Legalise Cannabis Party would not exist without the years of work put in by those two, so this mention is in deep appreciation. Some of the road trip campaigns I’ve been on with Jim are legendary while hermit Heathen kept the HEMP Party running from a little tin shed in the middle of the bush for years.

As a result of their decades of work, NSW MP Jeremy Buckingham was in parliament this week questioning when will we honestly tackle the current gang wars in Sydney, fighting over the massive profits to be made from coke and meth. Prohibition doesn’t work—drug use is a health issue—humans have always used drugs—they like them! The message is no different to thirty years ago, but meanwhile, thousands of lives are being trashed each week by the unwinnable drug war. It has to end sometime.

This year marks the 25th anniversary of Portugal decriminalising personal possession of all drugs. They’ve developed an integrated system of health and social services without making abstinence a precondition for getting help. Simply treat drugs as a health issue as we’ve been saying for years.

Alcohol is so popular in Australia and ingrained in our lifestyle and culture with mainstream advertising and promotions everywhere. Still, more and more people are discovering and loving cannabis, and hence drinking less. It’ll make us smarter and healthier, I reckon. A huge percentage of daily cannabis users I know don’t drink alcohol at all. It’s a significant change. Think don’t just drink!

Michael Balderstone
HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #722 | 27 AUGUST 2026
High Headliners!
It was like the old days, protesting outside Parliament House in Brisbane on Tuesday about RDT. A great crowd of about a hundred people and lots of faces I haven't seen in years. True blue campaigners who’ve been at it for decades. Lots of women, mothers with children who were helped by weed. Life changing weed! Just imagine having a child with hundreds of seizures every day then with a tiny bit of cannabis they stop overnight. 

The fact that it took stopping epileptic children’s seizures to make the bastards accept that maybe it does have some medical value is disgusting. However, it shows how hard it is to change peoples minds and get them to actually question stuff and think for themselves. Not these mothers who risk their children being taken off them for using illegal plant medicine, they’re genuine heroes.

Former magistrate, David Heilpern, who spoke at the Rally is another hero. He had to quit his job because it literally sickened him having to repeatedly take away driving licences from innocent people for the mere presence of THC. He can’t believe the Queensland Government is now talking about jail for repeat drug driving offenders, and the proposed fines have skyrocketed to thousands of dollars that no poor people can ever pay.

The Australian Institute of Health and Welfare’s National Drug Strategy household survey found 3% of Australians had used cannabis for medical purposes in the last year, equating to about 700,000 people. You could safely treble that, I reckon. Not sure about you, but when I’m asked if I’m a criminal, I don’t really feel inclined to tick the yes box on that one.

Canada shipped 20 tonnes less weed to Oz last year, down to about 50. While Thailand went from one tonne to 21, a quarter of the total! Germany in comparison imported over 200 tonnes. We grew, in Oz, 55 tonnes of legal and exported seven. I just want to grow my own, and it still feels as far away as ever.

Good luck to Dr Craig Buchanan running in the Secret Harbour By-election in WA this weekend. He says pre-poll has been overrun by an orange tsunami!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #723 | 3 SEPTEMBER 2026
High Headliners!

I’m picking oranges every morning for juice and we just had a week of glorious sunshine, which makes heaven even more obvious. No doubt it’ll be hot soon enough and I read that it was the mildest winter in 150 years, so look out for a hot, hot summer. Speaking of climate change, Nepal changed my life fifty odd years ago.

It was the lifestyle of the people and their laughter. I’m six months out of the London stockbroker suit and wandering through the mountains out of Pokhara. I slept and ate with the locals in the villages and wondered at how happy these people were. The women would head off in the morning together, chatting and laughing to collect huge bundles of sticks they’d carry home on their backs.

The men worked together building or planting, or whatever, as they did everything themselves. The villages and countryside were beatifically maintained, with little whitewashed huts dotted amongst the gardens, it looked like paradise to me. Hashish was legal then and sold everywhere, cheap as chips, from plants growing wild alongside hillsides of rhododendrons. 

That was 1973, just before America and the UN pressured Nepal to make weed illegal, which totally disrupted their economy. I was in Nepal eight years ago and it was extremely hard to find hash. I was told by locals the King said it was bad and his word is gospel.

I love the story analysing the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics covering 20 million people between 1990 and 2025. In States that decriminalised mediweed (which only started in 1996 in California, remember) health related work absences dropped by about 7%. Health services saw a 32% drop, manual workers 39%. These are huge figures related to treating chronic pain, muscle conditions and mental stress. Interestingly, the largest absenteeism reductions, at 36%, were amongst the less educated and experienced.

Love to everyone!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #724 | 10 SEPTEMBER 2026

If you’d like to donate to Nepal, Helen Simpson goes back and forth regularly, between working in the Nimbin Hospital. She’s a beauty and we trust she will spend any money donated wisely (see below).

There was a story in last week’s Headlines about how Albo promised $600 million to help Pacific nations stop international drug trafficking. I guess the profits are so massive even if only a percentage of the craft get through there’s still a fortune to be made. By the time it gets to Nimbin, after being cut any number of times, coke is $300 a gram. Every day there’s a gangland shooting in Sydney, fighting over the profits. 

Most of the coke is from Colombia and the meth from Mexico. The question is when does this end? They will never stop the illegal drug trade, they admit that, yet there is no discussion about ending the war creating it. How about we regulate these drugs with quality control and prescriptions through a doctor like they’ve done with cannabis?

NSW police have been at it again with their RAID, ‘Remove All Impaired Drivers’, last weekend. They conducted 6,420 drug tests with 774 positive. They don’t tell us how many were for cannabis but I bet the majority are and those people will most likely pay the $704 fine when it arrives in the mail, unaware it’s an admission of guilt and a week or two later they’ll get a letter saying they've lost their licence for three months. 

It’s sickening the way they keep saying these numbers represent “potential lives saved”. The same old propaganda cut and pasted over and over again. No wonder they’re struggling to get new recruits. Respect for the force is at an all time low and bad laws are a big part of it. Why do they refuse to accept presence does not mean impairment? Are they just bullies, or is this about money, like most things?

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #720 | 13 AUGUST 2026
High Headliners!
There have been some terrific speeches in Victoria’s parliament by our Legalise Cannabis MP’s in the last week or so. Tall David and Rachel are absolutely giving their all down there as the curtain draws closer on their term batting for us all. 

The rules changed there this week with the Government and Opposition voting out the Group Voting Tickets (GVTs), which pretty much spells the end of any chance of minor parties getting elected again in Victoria. It sounds like it will be Labor, Liberals, One Nation and Greens and no one else after 28 November. You need 16.7 % of the vote to get a spot in the Upper House, making it extremely hard, without a lot of backing.

Rachel and David had one shot left and called for a non binding plebiscite on legalising personal use, which in no time got voted down 27 to 8, despite their own parliamentary inquiry recommending it. Interestingly the polls in the papers are showing around 80% of people would support it, but the politicians clearly know better, they reckon!

I watched the debate in the New South Wales Legislative Council last week on the RDT Bill, which passed the Lower House. Jeremy has bent over backwards to try and get the smallest of changes, and it was extremely painful to watch one after another Coalition opponent use up their twenty minute time allocation, until there was no time for a vote. A filibuster it’s called! Now we wait for another month, before we can pick up the threads again, with not much time left in NSW before they shut down for the March 2027 Election.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

At Tangi, creating murals is only one part of the experience🌱

We believe that understanding the local culture and community is just as important as painting in a public space. That’s why we dedicated a day for our participating artists to slow down, learn, and connect with Bali beyond the walls.

The journey began at Gunung Kawi in Tampaksiring, an 11th century temple complex known for its monumental rock carved shrines and rich historical significance. Guided by our curator and cultural advisor @susantadwitanaya from @guratinstitute, the artists were introduced to stories, history, and cultural perspectives that offer a deeper understanding of the island 💫

We then visited the exhibition at @rad_ruangartaderau , where we were warmly welcomed by Bu Puti, Agung, and the team. The visit became an opportunity to exchange ideas, share experiences of making art in Bali, and have open conversations about artistic practice, culture, and everything in between.

For us, meaningful cultural exchange happens not only through murals, but also through listening, learning, and spending time together❤️

Video produced by @es4satria and @fajarmahendra_ 💥

#tangistreetartfestival #streetartbali #tangisaf2026

Four years of Tangi.

What started as a small idea has grown into a festival that brings artists, communities, friends, and new faces together through walls, workshops, music, and shared experiences.

Every year has brought something different. New places, new artists, new collaborations, new challenges, and a lot of good memories along the way.

This year, we spent a week in Glagalinggah, Kintamani, painting walls, meeting people, making things, dancing, laughing, and simply enjoying being together.

Looking back, it’s not only the walls that make us proud. It’s everything that happens around them.

Four years in, Tangi is still growing. And we’re very happy to see where it takes us next. 🌞

Thank you to all artists, partners, supporters, volunteers, team and everyone who has been part of the journey.

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #710 | 4 JUNE 2026
...Finally the long promised NSW RDT news arrived today, like getting blood out of a stone, rather than saliva from a stoner. At least it’s a start and no longer will you automatically lose your licence here, if you have a valid prescription and are registered on a new ‘mediweed’ database.

Not sure how that registering will go, not sure if people have enough trust to do that, be interesting to see how many do. It’s a ‘world-first’, of course, we love to be different from everywhere else, like we know better, is it?

Also, they plan to lift the acceptable level of THC in your saliva from 10ng to 50ng. I’m not sure if I don’t wake up with more than 50ng! First time I got RDT busted I naively plead not guilty, but it meant I got my reading back from the lab, 1200ng. My mate Andrew did the same and his reading was 1500ng. The police both times said we didn’t appear impaired.

The people drawing up these rules have likely never ever used cannabis. They don’t really get it. How could they? The only mind altering substance they’ve probably experienced is alcohol, which has an entirely different effect to cannabis.

The words drug and driving together terrify them it seems, yet about ten million Australians take Big Pharma pills each day, three million take opiates. Rules are you are only allowed to feel good using their pills, or alcohol.

Cannabis actually calms my emotions, my PTSD, my whatever-you-wanna-call-it. It chills my child and sits him in the corner, enabling me to focus and be a better driver. They don’t understand that.

RDT was never really about safety on the roads so much as an arm of the war against the plants they don’t understand, that make us feel good, or ‘God’, depending on who you’re talking to. They don’t want us having our own direct connection with natural medicine, there’s no profit for anyone in that.

Anyway, hats off to our MP Jeremy who’s nagged Premier Chris Minns every chance he got since he was elected, about RDT. At least it’s a start and they promise to review it all in twelve months.

Love to everyone. Patience is wisdom really.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

We are excited to congratulate Georgia Boseley (Central and Eastern Arrernte) for winning the award for Best Emerging Indigenous Artist at Melbourne Fringe for their solo show, ‘Weaving the Everywhen’, currently on show here at KHT!

Georgia’s sculptural work asks audiences to reflect on their relationship with their natural environment and consider a future shaped by Indigenous systems of reciprocity, relation and care for Country. Unsettling our linear understandings of time, the work draws on Indigenous deep history in order to imagine an Indigenous deep future. 

KHT is proud to host this deeply resonant exhibition in the Birraung Building. Come and experience this award-winning exhibition before it closes on 22 November.

—

Installation view of Georgia Boseley (Central and Eastern Arrernte), ‘Weaving the Everywhen’, Koorie Heritage Trust, 29 September – 22 November 2026. Image courtesy of Koorie Heritage Trust. Photo by Christian Capurro, 2026.

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #711 | 11 JUNE 2026
...NSW Premier Chris Minns announcement of his proposed RDT changes have been swirling around all week with lot’s of angst and disappointment and we still haven’t even got all the details. Leaving people beside the road is an issue, especially for us country folk, and registering is also upsetting many. 

As someone said to me today, the police have been hunting me for fifty years how can I trust them not to target my car when they know I’m on the medical cannabis register? And 50 ng is not much… fifty parts of one billion! I registered 1200ng about two hours after smoking a joint, gives you some idea... 

In New Zealand, it’s a terrific and sensible change for hemp farmers, which I wish we would copy. From now on, no permits are needed, but anyone wanting to plant hemp has to register with police and the Department of Agriculture. They also lifted the THC content allowed to one percent.

Our lives are increasingly being run by control freaks with more and more rules. There’s little trust and I notice zero trust with tech who asks me to prove who I am constantly. No blame, just what is happening with the new world order! So we better get used to registering if we use the ‘killer weed’ in any way—same as a gun registry. 

That’s how deep the reefer madness propaganda has gone with a plant that has never killed anyone in ten thousand years of recorded history. Meanwhile the ‘mother plant’ England is stirring, as nine MPs from across the political spectrum have signed a parliamentary motion demanding the Government scrap the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.

“It actively hurts our communities, jeopardising the health and wellbeing of future generations, whilst fuelling increasingly resourceful and violent organised crime”.

No one should be in jail for drugs, it’s a health issue. Love to everyone.
Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #707 | 14 MAY 2026

Still raining here and the nights are cooling fast, making the fire our best friend in the damp forest. Nearly finished cleaning up after MardiGrass, which it seems everybody enjoyed. I must credit the Police with their sensible approach to the big crowd, many of course who had ‘legal’ weed.

On the road was another matter, no let up on busting drivers who had a skerrick of cannabis in their system, legal or otherwise. They busted 55 over the MardiGrass weekend and quite a few more on the Monday as people were leaving.

But that pales compared to the 708 busted in Operation RAID, “Remove All Impaired Drivers”, from 8,400 roadside drug tests. At least they’ve learnt the word “impaired”, which should be the issue for road safety, whether drivers are affected by old age, fear or fury, as well as drugs. The current primitive tests have increased anxiety on the roads.

Unless you actually were impaired, I recommend anyone busted driving with cannabis in their system, go to court and plead your case instead of paying the $700 fine which will see you get a letter from the Police a few weeks later telling you your licence is suspended for three months, in NSW anyway. Very sneaky failing the pub test behaviour as I see it. I guess paying the fine is an admittance of guilt, to them.

Interesting story on the Leafie website about a single dose of psilocybin changing the human brain structure! Twenty-eight healthy volunteers with no previous experience of magic mushrooms were wired up and monitored. All but one said it was the “single most unusual conscious state of their entire lives”. Mushroom use is booming in Oz like never before, because of saliva testing. 

Another study released by the American Medical Association talks about how many older Americans are turning to ‘mediweed’ and dropping pharmaceuticals. I hear healing stories every week like this, people in pain or unable to sleep finally try cannabis and find relief. Often it’s after years of struggling with various pharma’.

It’s hard to swim against the stream and hard to accept doctors aren’t always right! Trust your self!

Michael Balderstone
HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #717 | 23 JULY 2026
High Headliners!
I hadn’t realised more than half of California doesn’t sell legal cannabis... So there is a booming illegal black market which the authorities are fighting, in an increasingly expensive and endless lost battle.

First it was mostly poor Mexicans but now the Chinese and other Asian crime syndicates have taken control of the black market. They buy or lease poor, cheap land and use highly toxic banned fertilisers and pesticides which some say are causing serious health issues including psychosis. Perhaps even worse, the horrific chemicals are left behind which is a serious issue, especially in National Parks.

The California Governor’s office has destroyed 841,000 pounds (381,472 kg) of illicit weed, including 1.3 million plants, in the last three years. The catch is, 53% of cities and counties in California do not allow any type of cannabis business, and that’s just in California. The same problem exists all across America, with half the States legal and half not, leaving massive openings for black market operators...

The Legalise Cannabis Party has no Federal MP’s and although the Greens have a great weed policy, they're too busy with other stuff to give the issue much attention, which is why we formed a political party specifically for the job in the first place. Perhaps we need a lobbyist pacing the corridors of the Big House?

I’ve been reading for years cannabis can help people with Alzheimer’s and other dementia based illnesses and now there’s some extremely positive trials going on with patients and the end of life agitation which often comes with dementia. Nearly 90% of patients found it highly effective. There’s that word again!

If you’re in Western Australia, Legalise Cannabis has selected Dr Craig Buchanan as their candidate in the Secret Harbour By-election, coming up soon, on 8 August. Craig has been Dr Brian Walker’s offsider for years and is a perfect candidate. 

The annual and infamous Nimbin Cannabis Cup was held last weekend and the quality just gets better and better (see below). Number 30 won, an Hybrid Indica cultivar called Crikey!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #713 | 25 JUNE 2026
High Headliners!

Raining again now, makes the few sunny days we just had very precious. We picked some of the hemp crop just in time and the rest will have to wait. The few males we missed early made some of it quite seedy but soaking it in organic olive oil should lure stacks of the little fat soluble cannabinoids to melt into it. So in my thinking it’s CBDA on salads and CBD if it’s used in the frypan!

The NSW Government has a new Hemp Industry Development Plan and is finally backing hemp seriously as a new regional growth industry, they say. It looks like two $10 million dollar grants to get Australia's first large scale hemp processing plants built.

Our Jeremy was instrumental in forming the Hemp Industry Taskforce and his commitment to growing the hemp industry has finally hit some gold. He’s a busy man down there in the Big Smoke with the Ivan Milat Inquiry and RDT changes all happening at once. I’m full of admiration for his effort, wearing a suit every day for us, as I see it.

Still plenty of discussion on the proposed RDT changes for NSW with the biggest worry for people being left beside the road, and not trusting putting their name on a register. We are being corralled into a corner where you must have a current prescription for the legal, mostly hydro ‘mediweed’ and register on a database of users to get any benefit from the proposed changes.

I figure any crumbs off the table are good if you’re starving and let’s hope the review, in twelve months, alleviates the ignorant fears transport cops and the NRMA have about us. No ones seems to be sure about any changes to the roadside testing, but I suspect they’re continuing the same as now, just changing the punishments, if you do what they want. Otherwise you drive with the same stress and anxiety about being tested we all have now. So I guess I’ll play the game, having been busted twice already.

Don’t lose your sense of humour whatever happens, with no experience, they have no idea how cannabis affects us. Patience is wisdom.

Love to everyone!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #714 | 2 JULY 2026
High Headliners!
EOFY talk is everywhere at the moment and the weed story in Forbes caught my eye. The American States that have legalised recreational pot have collected more than $28 billion in tax revenue over the past twelve years, which is about $40 billion in Aussie dollars.

That’s only twenty-four US States and in 2025 alone they collected nearly US$5 billion. Not only has the new industry created about 430,000 jobs, as well as all the tax, at the same time it has spared hundreds of thousands from arrest and incarceration.

Compare that to here. Australia spends about $17 billion a year on police and another $10 billion on jails and courts, which gives some idea of just how much economically it might help if we legalised, regulated and taxed our weed sales. 

On the jobs side of things, a study of twenty million working adults found the medical cannabis laws are associated with a notable reduction in health related workplace absences, like about 7%! Less pain, less stress, less days off—is there anywhere that legalising cannabis has done harm?

The RDT football is being kicked from end to end again this week with Queensland over-reacting and going in the opposite direction to the proposals in New South Wales, vowing to dramatically increase fines and even jail “drug drivers”, who they say are causing more accidents than drink drivers, now. I noticed that just as in NSW, the enemy kept quoting 60% of traffic fatalities have cannabis in their system. What are they talking about? 

Such a distortion. Reading carefully, 60% of deemed drug driving fatalities have cannabis in their system, they say. Illegal drugs—they mean—of course; MDMA, coke, meth and pot. As for blood tests, pot is uniquely fat soluble and unlike all the other water soluble drugs it stays in our bodies for months while the others are gone in a couple of days. Very convenient for twisting the statistics, or are they just that ignorant?

Don’t let that sense of humour stray too far. Love to everyone!
Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #716 | 16 JULY 2026

High Headliners!

It’s big news coming out of Victoria that the Premier looks like abolishing the GVT’s (Group Voting Tickets) for the next State Election in a few months. This will almost certainly end the time in parliament of Legalise Cannabis MP’s David Ettershank and Rachel Payne who would now need to acquire 16.7% of the vote to get re-elected.

Not just ours but all minors parties will likely be dumped, with only Labor, Lib’s, Greens and One Nation candidates getting elected. Very sad for our campaign in Victoria to change the weed laws, the Greens will have to step up, one hopes. No doubt David and Rachel have put cannabis on the map in Victoria in a whole new significant and respected way. They’ve both been terrific representatives for the plant and the people who love it.

My mate Andrew has been telling me for years the police are responsible for hugely affecting drug trends. Cannabis has always been by far the easiest bust, being bulky and smelly and most people who use the herb smoke it, usually a big give away anywhere in public. A big reason why many of us used to smoke in cars while driving around, or we stayed at home.

If you can be in Brisbane at midday on the 25th of August, do come to Parliament House for a protest rally, highlighting the ridiculous new roadside drug testing Queensland is proposing. Mark it in your diary now. Queensland is considering doubling its already huge fines and suggesting anyone with illegal drugs in their blood, who seriously injures someone in a crash, could go to jail for 25 years. Remembering pot stays in your blood for months this is plain ridiculous. 

RDT is the one big weapon left against cannabis users and the Sunshine State looks like using it big time, doing the opposite to New South Wales out of pure ignorance, or is it spite? Just as Germany releases research following the booming medical cannabis expansion over there, showing several regions “actually resulted in unexpected declines or stagnation in traffic fatalities”.

Love to everyone!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #712 | 18 JUNE 2026
High Headliners!
...The dust has settled a little on the NSW Premier’s new Roadside Drug Testing ideas, which caused quite a stir, including some very unfair finger pointing at our Jeremy and Alex Greenwich, who were not included in designing any of it. As far as I can tell, it was all done by Police and Transport, and even Minns himself seems confused about the level of ng we will be tested for and how it will happen beside the road. We’ll find out soon enough.

...I’ve met dozens of police in the last fifty years and most of them good people who didn’t join to be front line in a drug war... Fact is, for years, nearly all who would speak to me agree cannabis should be legal and some even congratulated the HEMP Embassy when medical got the green light. Many of them have smoked pot in the past... Quite a few ex-cops buy it here now for their PTSD, preferring the home grown bush weed to the super strong imported chemical stuff...

More than half police work these days is related to the war on drugs... Cannabis is by far the easiest bust, it’s bulky and smelly to carry and of course when you smoke it everyone nearby knows. Swallowing a tiny pill is incomparable and powders are easily hidden as well. The RDT saliva testing has done the same. Whatever is not tested is now popular, but not as safe as pot! People aren’t idiots, they work out ways around bad laws there is no respect for. There are multiple substances that can change your state of mind not just pot, cocaine, MDMA and meth, the only four tested.

Cannabis however is the safest and the most passive. It used to be a popular reason to bust peaceful hippies who never had guns but those days have changed with a cocktail of drugs mixed up in the black market now. Our police have become Big Pharma’s army. I just wish they could see it themselves, but they’ve been fed so much propaganda, and no doubt most of them are locked in with mortgages. Meanwhile, Canada earned $2.5 billion from adult use cannabis sales last year. When will we wake up? 

Love to everyone and it’s worth writing to your local MP about how RDT affects you!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #715 | 9 JULY 2026

High Headliners!

Finally the cold arrived, along with drizzly rain that reminds me of childhood Warrnambool weather. Winds fresh off the Antarctic and frozen mornings riding around lambing ewes at first light before the crows picked their eyes out. Raw and real stuff city folk rarely experience. I was fortunate growing up in the country, but glad I moved to the subtropical Nimbin zone to find like-minded souls!

The Queensland prison report, 54% more in prison than ten years ago, is shocking. If about half of our prisoners end up back in jail within a year or two you’d reckon it was time we changed tack somewhere... 

What really is of interest, is that over half the people in our prisons have a history of mental health issues and over 70% have used ‘illicit drugs’ in the last year. We have to get past the idea that the drugs we’ve made illegal are bad. How can people trying to get mental or physical pain relief be ‘bad’?

Sometimes I see Nimbin as an outdoor, free-range hospital. People like myself, who discovered the wonderful relief cannabis gave, have been attracted to live around Nimbin for over fifty years now, because we get understood and accepted, not judged. Your neighbours won’t dob you in here and in fact what has made this community so close is that most of us are criminals, even if we know we aren’t, really!

Our community has characters with all sorts of drug habits and over the decades we’ve come to realise it is better not to judge, but rather be grateful we are not one of them. It’s all about pain relief, trying to have a good day, trying to enjoy our lives. Surely the purpose of life, no?

Honestly, when it’s all boiled down, no one should be in jail for drugs. For forty years I’ve watched members of our community go back and forth to jail, or as we call it, criminal university. Prohibition has created this mess all by itself, trying to control how people enjoy their lives. Give it fifty years and we’ll look back in shame at how we’ve treated the most hurt and traumatised in our society.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

These are our forests.

Two weeks ago, here in Les Gavarres, 2,300 of the massif’s nearly 29,000 hectares burned. It hurts — but the forest is still standing.

And it’s not just here. Europe has spent weeks trapped under an omega block: a dome of hot air locked between two low-pressure systems, shaped like the Greek letter Ω. The atmosphere can’t renew itself. Heat builds. From Portugal to Greece, forests are burning.

But heat alone doesn’t explain it. For centuries, farming, herds and firewood kept these forests in balance. When that life left, the fuel stayed. The forest doesn’t need to be left alone. It needs to be lived in.

To the firefighters, the military emergency unit, civil protection and every neighbour who stayed to defend their home: thank you. You held the line.

Cork oaks are built for fire. They sprout again from their own bark — the same bark that still gives cork in Les Gavarres today. They will return. So will we.

The future of our forests belongs to everyone who loves them, rides them, lives them. In Girona, in Europe, anywhere in the world where there’s a trail you care about.

We’ll keep coming back. And we’ll watch them grow again, season by season.

🔥 Platinum Sponsor Spotlight: Banya 5 🔥

Long before the sauna revival swept the PNW, @banya5urbanspa was already setting the standard for thermal wellness and contrast therapy in Seattle. Founder John Goodfellow, inspired by the legendary 10th Street Baths in Manhattan, dreamed of bringing that same NY-style banya experience to the Northwest.

After extensive research trips through Brooklyn and Manhattan, Banya 5 opened its doors in 2004, introducing Seattle to a new kind of rejuvenation — one rooted in heat, cold, and connection.

For 21 years, Banya 5 has offered a powerful mix of tradition and restoration: a 220° dry sauna, 45° cold plunge, 88° salt tub, and eucalyptus steam room, alongside scrubs, wraps, and massage treatments.

What began as a pioneer in a then-industrial South Lake Union neighborhood is now a Seattle institution — a sanctuary where wellness, culture, and community converge.

💧 Experience the original. Experience Banya 5 — proud Platinum Sponsor of the Seattle Sauna Festival.

Come chat with the Banya 5 team at the Seattle Sauna Festival Nov 1 & 2 at the National @nordicmuseum 

#SeattleSaunaFestival #Banya5 #SaunaCulture #PNWWelness #ContrastTherapy #SeattleSpa #SaunaLife

🌊 Floating Sauna Futures: Inspiration, Innovation & Impact
 Join David, founder of @vonsauna —the PNW’s first floating sauna and one of our *Gold Sponsors* of the festival— plus founders from @wildhauspnw for a conversation on what’s next in floating sauna design, culture, and community. Moderated by festival co-founder Ryan Davis. Sunday at 12pm. 
💧🔥 Fireside Chats (2 PM & 4 PM both days) The Fire & Ice Formula: 5 Ways to Get the Most out of Your Contrast Therapy Sessions with @redwoodoutdoorsco :

• Delaney Paullus — Adventurous visual storyteller whose first sauna memory traces back to a small German town with Oma & Opa; rooted in nature, guided by curiosity, and shaped by a background in Outdoor Behavioral Health, Education, and Forest Regeneration research.

• Michelle Mayther — Michelle’s contrast therapy journey began as a way to recover from the stress and anxiety caused by spending over a decade in corporate marketing. Now, she leads the Marketing Team at Redwood Outdoors and is able to speak about and spread her passion for sauna lifestyle.

🍯 Saturday 12–7 PM: @hierophantmeadery Tastings on Fisherman’s Terrace (Beverage Garden).
 Mead — the world’s oldest fermented beverage — has deep roots in Nordic culture, where it was often shared after sauna sessions and celebrations as a drink of renewal and connection. Made from honey, water, and botanicals, mead embodies the same balance of earth, fire, and craftsmanship that defines the sauna tradition itself.

Gracias a Fundación Líneas Romero y Líneas Romero, este viaje se convirtió en mucho más que un recorrido cruzando "El Río", hicimos de éste, una experiencia para descubrir nuestro territorio desde otra mirada y con banda sonora sobre el mar. Junto a Geoparque Mundial UNESCO de Lanzarote y Archipiélago Chinijo, conocimos la historia geológica de este entorno único, mientras Ale Acostase encargaba de hacernos bailar con sesión muy especial.

Al atracar en Caleta del Sebo, Los Blody llenaron el escenario de energía en un concierto inolvidable demostrando porqué han sido una de las bandas ganadoras del @sonoralaspalmasgc. DIRECTAZO 🎸⚡ De forma paralela,  chinij@s y mayores participaron en la creación colectiva de una sombrera graciosera elaborada a partir de residuos plásticos recogidos y otros materiales reutilizados. Un taller de reutilización de residuos impulsado por la Fundación Líneas Romero realizado de la mano de Álvaro Guzmán (@alvardelmar) demostrando que la cultura y la sostenibilidad siempre pueden ir de la mano.

Gracias a todas las personas que formaron parte de este Belingueo tan especial. Nos llevamos momentos que, como este aftermovie, merecen volver a vivirse una y otra vez. 💙

OPEN 13:00〜
年齢や国籍、肩書きといった境界をいったんほどき、
ただ一人の人として出会い、言葉を交わす。
平等でも序列でもない、関係が混ざり合いながら立ち上がる“scramble”な状態へ。
逗子から都心、そして世界へとつながる30代が掲げるテーマは、
「偏愛で生きる実験場」。
まだ人生の途中にいる私たちが、
効率や正しさではなく、どうしても惹かれてしまうものや、抑えきれない衝動を大切にする。
広く浅くではなく、狭く深く。
それぞれの偏愛が交差し、小さな関係が生まれていく。
海辺にひらく、一日限りの実験場です。

✴️ OKAY IT’S NOT FUNNY ANYMORE, I WANT SUMMER BACK ✴️

La música en directo está llena de momentos mágicos, pero también de situaciones inesperadas que nos recuerdan que, por encima de todo, están las personas.

Como ya saben, nos hemos visto obligados a realizar un cambio en la programación de esta edición. Desde aquí queremos enviar nuevamente todo nuestro cariño y apoyo a Ginebras. Esperamos de corazón poder encontrarnos con ellas muy pronto.

Al mismo tiempo, queremos agradecer profundamente la comprensión que nos han compartido tras el comunicado. En pocas horas hemos trabajo sin descanso para encontrar una alternativa a la altura de una ocasión tan especial.

Y ya podemos anunciar, con enorme ilusión, que 𝐑𝐮𝐟𝐮𝐬 𝐓. 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐟𝐥𝐲 se incorpora al cartel de Sonidos Líquidos para el 6 de junio.
Una de las bandas más personales, sorprendentes y admiradas del panorama nacional.

Con un directo hipnótico, elegante y emocionante, @rufustefirefly lleva años construyendo un universo propio donde el rock psicodélico, la sensibilidad pop y la experimentación conviven de forma natural.

Queremos dar las gracias a la banda por decir que sí cuando más lo necesitábamos. Con muy poco margen y un concierto en Murcia que ofrecerán la noche anterior, no era precisamente el plan más cómodo. Por ello, queremos expresar nuestro más sincero agradecimiento a todos sus integrantes y su equipo humano por su compromiso, su generosidad y su disposición para formar parte de esta aventura.

Ya queda muy poquito para vernos el sábado en La Geria para compartir 𝑡𝑜𝑑𝑎𝑠 𝑙𝑎𝑠 𝑐𝑜𝑠𝑎𝑠 𝑏𝑢𝑒𝑛𝑎𝑠 que solo suceden cuando artistas y público caminan en la misma dirección y se dan cita en un lugar único en el mundo.

Gracias por la comprensión 🙏🏻

Be dazzled by these miniature forms on a monumental scale... Unfortunately named but astonishingly beautiful, slime moulds (myxomycetes) are some of the strangest organisms on Earth. Neither plant nor fungus, these ancient amoebae appear like jewels, coral, lacework and alien architecture across decaying logs, forest litter and damp woodland floors.

This exhibition is a partnership between Beaker Steet and Rosny Farm. 

Open Saturday and Sunday 11am - 4pm

CORE REMAINS

Inspired by Mulat Sarira, this mural reflects the balance between adaptation and identity. The chaotic layers, sharp movements, and shifting forms represent the pressure of constantly changing environments, cultures, and experiences.

At the center of the composition, the figure continues to transform—absorbing its surroundings while holding onto its core. Beneath the noise, distortion, and movement, something essential remains intact.

Core Remains is about resilience through awareness: evolving with your environment without losing the spirit that defines who you are.

🎬✨ ¡YA ESTÁ EN MARCHA UN FIN DE SEMANA DE SONIDOS LÍQUIDOS QUE SERÁ ESPECTACULAR!

Y como ya es tradición, arrancamos con uno de esos maridajes que se convirtieron en un clásico y nunca fallan: cine y música en directo. 🍷🎶🎥

La Sala Buñuel de El Almacén acogió esta noche una nueva colaboración entre Sonidos Líquidos y el Festival Internacional de Cine de Lanzarote (@festivalcinelanzarote), convirtiéndose en el escenario de una experiencia irrepetible.

🚕 En esta ocasión viajamos al Nueva York más oscuro, hipnótico e inolvidable de Taxi Driver, la obra maestra de Martin Scorsese que marcó para siempre la historia del cine. Una película icónica, protagonizada por un inmenso Robert De Niro, que sigue fascinando cinco décadas después por su intensidad, su estética y su retrato de la soledad urbana. 

🔥 Y para hacerla aún más especial, la banda sonora cobró nueva vida gracias a la interpretación en directo de @zabala.music, que acompañó cada escena envolviendo al público en una atmósfera única, emocionante y profundamente cinematográfica.

🎂 Y qué mejor manera de celebrar estos 50 años que como más nos gusta: uniendo películas de culto y música en directo. Un comienzo perfecto para todo lo que está por venir.

🎟️ Mientras disfrutábamos de esta noche de cine y música, también arrancó la recogida de pulseras cashless en la sala anexa al Multicines Atlántida, el primer paso para vivir al máximo el gran día en La Geria.

🔜Mañana tenemos mucho más

Hoy el festival se vivió de una forma más íntima, más cercana, casi como si la música nos hubiera hablado al oído.

La Sala Buñuel de El Almacén se convirtió en ese refugio especial donde descubrimos a artistas emergentes con muchísimo que contar. Y en esta ocasión nos acompañó @soyangelaglez, una de las voces jóvenes más prometedoras de la escena nacional. Con letras honestas y un pop de autor fresco que abraza desde el primer acorde, la cantautora malagueña nos regaló canciones que emocionaron y se quedarán con nosotros mucho después del directo.

Ángela nos ofreció un concierto auténtico, divertido, con desparpajo, con esa calidez que se genera cuando artista y público de verdad crean complicidad.

Antes, seguimos calentando motores: en El Charco de San Ginés la entrega de pulseras cashless (en la sala anexa a Multicines Atlántida) reunió a gran parte del publico que invitamos con una caña Mahou para ir calentando motores y sumar los primeros brindis de un fin de semana que promete ser GRANDE.

✨ Recordamos que quienes aún no han retirado su pulsera podrán hacerlo mañana, de 10:00 a 13:00 en @pm.proshop donde también podrán comprar nuestro merchan; y en la entrada del recinto presentando su QR. Dentro podrán recargarlas en los puntos habilitados.

Las ganas van ‘in crescendo’ para vivir intensamente las 10 horas de música en directo que llenarán el escenario utópico de La Geria de momentos inolvidables.

Si tienes dudas, en la web y en las historias seguiremos ofreciendo toda la info útil.

¿Preparad@? Tic… tac… tic… tac… ✨

Dear Folks,

It is with heavy hearts that we share the passing of Michael Sollis. Michael has been part of the Festival staff team since mid-2023 when he was appointed Co-artistic Director alongside Chris and Holly. Together they have shaped the past three festivals (2024-26). Michael battled cancer tirelessly since his diagnosis in 2021 and continued to pour his energy and time into creative pursuits, his family, and his community right until the end.

Beyond the Festival, Michael led a rich life full of music, community, and creativity. He contributed significantly to the fabric of his beloved home of Canberra on Ngunnawal Country, and Australia more broadly through his compositions, curation, creative programming and visionary leadership.

Michael passed away peacefully last night, proud and happy knowing that the folk community had an absolute ball at the Festival this year. He was right there amongst it all; dancing with his children, scooting around the site taking it all in, and sharing many special moments with his wife Kiri, extended family, colleagues, friends and the folk community.

Chris and Holly are honoured to have shared over 12 years working with Michael on creative projects including the National Folk Festival, and are grateful to have been gifted Michael’s vision and hopes for the Festival as they look ahead and continue as Co-artistic Directors. Festival Director Anne and Volunteer Manager Demelza have also worked closely with Michael over the past three years, and we will all miss his passion, enthusiasm, creative and quirky ideas, and advocacy for those most in need of it.

The National Folk Festival extends our heartfelt condolences to Michael’s family, and to all who knew him or were touched by his work.

Yours in Folk,

The National Folk Festival Staff Team
Anne, Demelza, Chris and Holly

The final days of painting always bring a different kind of energy.

As deadlines get closer, the walls become busier, ideas become bolder, and something unexpected always happens. At Tangi, artists don’t simply finish their murals. They keep responding to the place around them.

Sometimes that means adding more details than originally planned. Sometimes it means starting spontaneous walls that weren’t part of the schedule at all. When inspiration comes, it’s hard to stop.

This is what we love most about the festival. Every wall grows through curiosity, conversations, and the atmosphere shared between artists, the village, and the people who pass by every day.

Not every mural was planned. Some simply happened because Bali inspired them ❤️💫💥

Archer Archer Archer.  First connected at Bello Winter Music July 2018, where I first did not know what to make of him whilst he chatted to @briannankervis on the couch and recited spoken words pieces like ‘Bring us your old people’. 

Then he sung ! Crooned. 
Like an Old Time Sing song man.
He awoke something in my cells. Memories of my grandparents and their music. I wished my Mum were there to hear these tunes and this man. 
I couldn’t wait to take the CDs home to her

Fast forward to July 2019 and Mum and I go and see Archer play at the much loved (and still missed) cosy Lismore venue @dustyatticmusiclounge 
Mum swoons. She loves him. Buys his book. 
We all have some good chats.

8 November 2024 Mum got to see him perform again. This time at @elthamhotelnsw . More hugs. Gosh she adored Archer and his words and ways.

There was no way we could have imagined this would be Mum’s second to last night out with Live Music
Her final was again at The Eltham seeing William Crighton and Jeff Lang. 

Hearing Archer last weekend was mind blowing. A full band and him commanding the role of lead vocals like a pro. I stood in awe and thought wow here is this man in all his potential. Just WAIT to you see/hear the band @kangarooswithmachineguns (more coming)

Ran into Archer in the streets of Mullum. He remembered Mum at the Eltham. I told him she was sadly no longer with us. We had a hug. A moment of acknowledgment. 

I’m soooo glad I found out Kangaroos 🦘 with Machine guns was his band or I may have well missed them. 

Oh and his handle on Insta just happens to be @oldtimesingsongman 

Thanks @mullumrootsfestival

🎪 Thank you for making the 2026 National Folk Festival an amazing gathering of folk spirit and community!

From the Smoking Ceremony right through to the final note played in the Session Bar, it's been a very special Festival. We’ve been reading messages from you all and again and again people have described a sense of joyful participation that carried right across the program. These photos from our fabulous volunteer photography team capture just some of the beautiful moments!

For many, the experience was shared across generations and communities: “The National Folk Festival really is a family event, the musician family, dance family, craft family … I love you all, see you next time!” The breadth of the program also stood out too. “The range of acts, workshops and sessions was phenomenal and I had an absolute blast… I had so many incredible collaboration opportunities… particularly wonderful moments in the Session Bar… late night/insanely early morning serenades…”

Running through it all was something harder to define, but widely felt. As 19-Twenty reflected “It felt like a little world away from all the noise… it felt like HOME" They went on to describe what makes the Festival distinct: “complete acceptance… all ages, all backgrounds, all genres… The Nash is more than a festival, it’s a family gathering.” Fred Smith summed it up simply: “National Folk Festival is always a smorgasbord for the soul, but last weekend was one of the best.” 

Thank you for your music, your dancing, your conversations, your presence, and your support for this very special event. Follow us online, and make sure you're signed up to our newsletter to hear all about next year. Save the date 25 - 29th March 2027!

National Reconciliation Week offers an opportunity to reflect on how we continue to learn, listen and walk forward together. 

One particularly musical way to get involved is through Voices for Reconciliation, where choirs, community groups and friends across Australia are invited to learn and share a song each year. 🏆✨ Award‑winning news! ✨🏆

Last month at the 2026 Melbourne International Flower & Garden Show, @jakemikoda, was awarded First Prize for his stunning bronze sculpture featuring two platypuses, “The Way We Move Together.”

This marks the fifth year Jake’s work has received awards and recognition at this major exhibition - an achievement he’s incredibly grateful for.

‘As a long-standing stallholder at Salamanca Market, Salamanca has always been a special place for me to connect with collectors and visitors,’ he says.

“The Way We Move Together” captures a quiet moment between two platypuses as they drift and play in the gentle pull of the river. There is no leader and no rush, just an easy rhythm shaped by water and familiarity. The sculpture reflects how connection often grows in nature, not through intention but through shared movement.'

'Cast in bronze, the work turns a brief moment of closeness into something lasting.'

Jake’s work is truly breathtaking, and we couldn’t be prouder to have his sculptures at our market - and to see his talent recognised on such a major stage.💚

I recently Watched 30 Years of Australian Story on ABC and was reminded how damn good @alexlloydofficial was at @mullumrootsfestival back in July. 
Despite LOVING his early albums Black the Sun (1999) and Watching Angels Mend (2001) this was the first time I’d had the pleasure of catching Alex live. 

I’d also had a chat to him on @bayfm99.9 a week or so before the festival and he’d mentioned he felt his shows had never been better. So i was ok with having waited so long. 

He released an album in 2016 called Acoustica which I’ve been listening to a lot. Stripped back acoustic versions of his hits and it includes a cover of Hallelujah which he performed in Mullum too. 

Absolutely sensational sets. I went both nights. First at the Civic Hall and second at the Top Pub. 
Got to say a quick hello and thanks 🙏🏽 

He also mentioned not liking to stay still TOO long so keep an eye on his tour dates because he sure does get around !

He’s got shows coming up at @brassmonkeycronulla 
@soundlounge Gold Coast and back in the Northern Rivers at @brunswickpicturehousensw on Saturday October 17th and so many more places. 

So glad i finally got to be in a live audience. It was SO good to hear those old songs brought back to life … and I don’t just mean the big hit Amazing. 
Ive fallen in love all over again with Bus Ride, Green, Everybody’s Laughing 🩵

Let’s talk about last night...

Trad Rave at the @nationalfolkfestival is where the “folk” genre gets completely flipped on its head.

This isn’t your typical sit-down-and-listen folk music, but a full-volume, red-lining the mixer, subs cranked, late-night, no-holding-back kind of folk.

From the second @eliasalexanderrr stepped on stage, the already electric atmosphere shifted up another notch. Relentless energy, massive sound, and one of those sets where the whole room just clicks. You look around and absolutely everyone, young and old, is completely dialled in, on beat, and the dance floor turns into a sea of flailing limbs.

It’s loud, it’s immersive, and it pulls you in whether you planned on it or not. 

This is the side of the Folkie that catches people off guard, and usually ends up being one of their favourite parts!

#NationalFolkFestival #Folkie #VisitCanberra #Photox #folkfestival

A DECADE OF HISTORY IN 200+ PAGES.

Introducing Flying in Blind, a new book celebrating 10 years of Long Beach walls.

What once started as an email musing has grown into one of the biggest wall art festivals in the world. After 10 years of history and over 150 painted murals and counting, Long Beach Walls is publishing “Flying in Blind,” a new book capturing the first decade that transformed a small-scale show into an indispensable part of the Long Beach identity and community.

Created in collaboration with MAEKAN, Studio Bangu, Intertrend Communication, and Creative Class Collective, it features over 200 pages that include interviews with artists and organizers including, James Jean, Lauren Young-Smith, Julia Huang, and Jasper Wong; photos of murals from each festival year; and rare ephemera spanning a decade of Long Beach Walls memories.

Tangi Street Art Festival 2026 Artist Lineup

Introducing our fifth artist for Tangi SAF 2026: Francisco Bosoletti @bosoletti 

Born and raised in a small village in Santa Fe, Argentina, Bosoletti is known for his poetic and introspective murals that explore themes of life, nature, and human existence. His work often blends classical sensibilities with contemporary street art, creating images that feel both timeless and deeply personal.

Through subtle details and layered compositions, his paintings reveal hidden meanings, inviting viewers to slow down and see beyond what is immediately visible. His murals often respond to the memory of a place and its people, creating a quiet dialogue between the artwork, the environment, and those who encounter it.

Bosoletti’s work encourages a different way of seeing, one that is more sensitive, reflective, and aware of the fleeting nature of life.

Tangi Street Art Festival 2026 Artist Lineup

Introducing our third artist for Tangi SAF 2026: @pinokibooo_ .

Pinokibo is a street artist and illustrator from Cilacap, Central Java, known for his dark, shadowy, semi-realistic, and edgy character style. His work often explores living forms such as humans, animals, and nature, combined with imagination, fictional figures, and strong atmospheric patterns.

Active in street art since 2012, he started with brush and paint before expanding his practice by combining it with spray cans. His works can be found across various urban surfaces, from rolling doors and skateboards to trucks, electrical boxes, and street walls.

Through his visuals, Pinokibo expresses stories, emotions, and messages that are not always easy to say directly, resulting in works that feel intense, personal, and full of character.
