🎵Extra Artist Announced! 🎹

Don't miss this rare opportunity to learn from melodica specialist, Anne Denzer in her Festival workshop 'Reeds of Renewal: Melodica as Living Cultural Practice'.

Led by Festival Director Anne Denzer, this workshop returns to the melodica as a site of deep listening, breath, and shared cultural practice. In an act that is both healing and celebratory, Anne reconnects with her roots as a melodica player, inviting participants into a space of reflection, renewal and collective sound. 

Participants explore tone, phrasing and ensemble awareness while engaging in a participatory process grounded in connection, inclusion and community-led music-making. Through simple, accessible material, the session invites players to locate themselves within a collective sound world and contribute to a living, evolving tradition shaped through listening, response and shared experience. 

Open to all levels. All instruments welcome. 11 - 11:50 pm on the Village Green, Sunday.

Learn more at folkfestival.org.au/program

Applications are now open for Manor Made 2026.

Manor Made in Winchelsea is a one-day makers market and arts festival set across the grounds of the historic Barwon Park Mansion, part of the Surf Coast Arts Trail Festival 2026.

We’re inviting ceramicists, textile artists, jewellers, sculptors, printmakers, illustrators and object designers to apply for a place at the Manor Made Makers Market — a curated selection of contemporary craft and handmade work across the mansion grounds.

Across the lawns and courtyard, the market unfolds outdoors for the day— ceramics, textiles, jewellery, sculpture, printmaking, illustration and object design set against sandstone and open sky.

Inside the stables, the Quiet Riot National Annual Small Works Art Prize (@quietriot.prize) will be exhibited, bringing together small works from artists across the country.

Within the mansion, Wayngurrla, Wayngurrla (Wadawurrung language for “To Make Good”) presents a First Nations exhibition reflecting on place, story and ongoing cultural connection, featuring Aunty Marlene Gilson OAM alongside her children and grandchildren.

A full day of work, made things and conversation, spread across a site that holds its own pace.

THE ENORMOUS RADIO/

PRESENTED BY THE SUBSTATION, CHAMBER MADE & MELBOURNE FRINGE

30 September – 10 October
12 – 9pm
Hourly sessions, final session at 8pm

Chamber Made's The Enormous Radio is a new large-scale immersive audio experience by artists Roslyn Oades and Bob Scott with collaborators. A ring of old radios replete with glowing dials, crackling speakers and twitchy antennas fill The Substation Main Space. This strange hive has been hacked, revived and repurposed to operate as an interconnected machine-medium capable of seeking, receiving, translating and transmitting uncanny messages from the animal world.

Drawing on Australian wildlife field-recordings, spatialised composition, translation software, and techno-spiritualism, the installation conjures haunted transmissions that speculate on the possibility of interspecies communication. As acoustic ecologists make breakthroughs in deciphering animal languages, this work asks: what if we could tune into the non-human, the endangered, and the wild? What might they say?

In the time of human-made climate emergency, The Enormous Radio stokes our longing to connect and tune into the unknown and the wild.

Tickets are on sale now for this limited two-week season, visit our link in bio.

Like stumbling upon a pot of gold (but way tastier), this Irish Stout has returned just in time for the cooler days ahead. Rich, full-bodied, and seriously satisfying, Folk Stout delivers bold coffee and chocolate flavours balanced with just the right hint of hop bitterness.

Brewed with roasted barley, this stout pours deep and dark with robust coffee and chocolate characters, complemented by a smooth, full-bodied mouthfeel and a medium hop bitterness that keeps everything perfectly balanced.

It’s the kind of beer made for cool, crisp autumn days - the perfect excuse to slow down, settle in, and enjoy a proper stout.

Brewed each year for the National Folk Festival in Canberra, this year to celebrate the 60th year of the Festival we are releasing a limited amount of Folk Stout in cans!

🎶 We're excited for didgeridoo player Mark Atkins' Festival appearances, including collaboration with British-Australian composer and improvising musician Keyna Wilkins, and a special performance with the Canberra Youth Orchestra. Together they present Celestial Emu (Dhinawan), a didgeridoo concerto inspired by the Gamilaroi “Emu in the Sky” constellation, bringing young orchestral musicians together with First Nations performance and storytelling.

We also look forward to Suara Dance sharing Indonesian traditions through movement, song and percussion. Featuring Acehnese dances such as Rapai Geleng and Ratoh Duek alongside West Sumatran talempong and Randai, Suara will collaborate with the Woden Valley Youth Choir in the Opening Concert.

Founded in 1969, the Woden Valley Youth Choir has supported generations of young singers, with performances ranging from national ceremonies to major festivals.

These projects bring visiting artists and local youth ensembles together on our Festival stages.

[ID] Final wall for Tangi Intervention Program #3

@rubseight adalah seorang tattoo artist, ilustrator, pelukis, dan graffiti writer asal Yogyakarta, yang kini berbasis di Bali. Ia telah aktif di jalanan sejak tahun 2008.

Untuk mural ini, ia menghadirkan interpretasi visualnya tentang konflik sejarah antara Kerajaan Buleleng di Bali Utara dan Kerajaan Badung di Bali Selatan. Keduanya merupakan kerajaan besar dengan pengaruh kuat terhadap wilayah, jalur perdagangan, dan aliansi politik. Ketegangan di antara keduanya memicu pertempuran di beberapa wilayah, termasuk daerah yang kini dikenal sebagai Peguyangan.

Berdasarkan berbagai catatan sejarah yang ia pelajari, peristiwa tersebut menjadi bagian dari lapisan cerita mengenai asal usul nama Peguyangan. Kawasan ini menyimpan ingatan tentang pergerakan, pertarungan, dan pergeseran kekuasaan, yang kemudian ia terjemahkan ke dalam bentuk visual melalui figur simbolik dan komposisi.

Ia juga menambahkan tipografi “Rahayu”, sebuah kata yang ia anggap sebagai salah satu bentuk doa terbaik. Kata ini kerap diucapkan sebagai harapan tulus untuk keselamatan, kedamaian, dan kebaikan dalam pertemanan serta kehidupan sosial.

Some of the best moments (planned or unplanned) at the Festival happen in the Session Bar, where all are welcome to join in. Dust off your instrument and bring it along!

Start the day with Slow Sessions where tunes are shared at an easy pace, perfect for those who are new to jamming to play together and build confidence. Led by West End Bluegrass, Comhaltas Sydney, The Nykelharpa Society and Laura Targett, these sessions offer a taste of different traditions. 

At the Bush Traditions Sessions, Ray Mulligan leads tunes collected from Colonial-style musicians exploring a living archive of Australian folk tradition. Or head to the series of 'Bangers The Kids Play These Days' sessions hosted by some of the younger trad players on the folk scene. 

In the evening, the Terrace is the place for singing sessions, hosted by Windborne, Shanty Club and more, with open singing sessions going late into the night. 

Bring your enthusiasm, voice and instrument and join in!

The National Folk Festival’s Community Arts program is a vibrant hands-on hub where folks of all ages can explore traditional and contemporary craft. 

Across the weekend, artists and makers lead workshops in all sorts of crafts including traditional hat making (to complete your ball outfit), tatreez embroidery, folk art painting, puppet-making, and jewellery making. Create a leather wristband or mask (again, outfit sorted!), decorate folk art designs, sketch the Festival in motion, or blend your own signature perfume.

The Community Arts area also hosts ongoing drop-in projects including the Festival Mural, lantern making for the Festival Parades, knitting and crochet, and collaborative banner-making. Whether you want to learn a new skill, contribute to a shared artwork, or spend time alongside other makers, Community Arts is a place to connect through creativity.

Tangi Street Art Festival 2026 Artist Lineup

We’re excited to introduce our first artist for Tangi SAF 2026: Darbotz.

An Indonesian artist known for his bold monochromatic style and his iconic “Cumi” character, Darbotz has spent the past two decades exploring themes of urban chaos, resilience, and survival. His intricate, monster-like forms reflect the intensity of city life while celebrating individuality and persistence.

Moving between urban art and contemporary contexts, his work has gained recognition both locally and internationally, connecting with audiences through its raw energy and distinct visual language.

We look forward to seeing his work come to life at Tangi 2026.

🌿 Los festivales están transformando progresivamente la forma en que gestionan su sostenibilidad y su impacto en el entorno.

Neftalí Acosta, director de @sonidos_liquidos, nos comparte su opinión, en la que destaca que los cambios son reales, principalmente, debido a la presión de las administraciones públicas para acceder a ayudas, pero también tras la demanda del propio público, que busca formar parte de un tejido de festivales comprometidos con el medioambiente. 👀

👉 En esta conversación resalta el papel del público en el desarrollo de estos cambios y en la inclusión de prácticas más sostenibles, impulsando así un cambio en el sector.

🎤More Folk Legends Join the Lineup!

We’re delighted to welcome these fabulous folks whose work helps us look back at the Festival’s past, examine it with care, tell stories that haven’t always been heard, and be inspired as we move forward. 

Special guest Judy Small AM joins the Festival for panels, conversations and special events reflecting on social issues, protest songs and the queer history of folk. We also welcome Dale Dengate, with friends Kerith Power and “Molly” Jane Ellis for a special session of 'Songs We Sang in the Sixties'. Paul Mortimer & Friends explore the history of the Sydney Folk scene in a special event, plus Bruce Watson will present 'Immortal', his video tribute to Australian folk legends featuring archival content from the Festival.

Still more to come, learn more here: folkfestival.org.au/artists

There is so much to share after a weekend of amazing music and stories, but I’ll start with this one because it’s my favourite. 

This fella was busking old time banjo songs on the street in between the venues and I stopped and watched and listened to him and then asked him if he’d ever written any songs. He said that he didn’t because he thought they always sounded weird whenever he attempted to. Of course, as a song writer, I told him they always sounded weird when they first come out and you just have to push through…

Anyway, the next morning he approached me telling me that he’d written his very first song that night and asked if he could play it for me. So he sat down right there and then and played me this song. I didn’t weep or anything (not)! 

I love this story because it’s EXACTLY why I created this music festival. To promote and encourage original music. His name is Martin Thornton, he lives locally and you’ll be seeing more of him…if I have it my way!  #mullumrootsfestival

Sonidos Líquidos 2026 arrancó hoy con un concierto absolutamente mágico en la Casa Museo del Campesino, y no podíamos haber imaginado un comienzo mejor.

La increíble @natalialacunza fue la encargada de inaugurar esta 16ª edición con un directo que había generado muchísimas expectativas entre nuestro público… ¡y se cumplieron desde que se subió al escenario con su banda!  La cantante y compositora nos hizo llegar sus canciones de una forma tan personal, auténtica y emocionante que transformó la tarde del domingo en un encuentro verdaderamente inolvidable.

Además, su actuación fue un marco perfecto para conmemorar el Día de la Mujer, poniendo en valor, a través de la música, el papel imprescindible que las mujeres desempeñan en nuestra sociedad 💜

Queremos agradecer a los Centros de Arte, Cultura y Turismo de Lanzarote por el patrocinio de este concierto y por permitirnos traer a una artista tan especial a uno de los espacios más queridos de nuestra isla. La Casa Museo del Campesino representa como pocos lugares el esfuerzo del pueblo de Lanzarote, su vínculo con el campo y sus raíces, algo que se respira en cada rincón de este lugar tan icónico.

Y, por supuesto, gracias enormes al público que nos acompañó con tantas ganas a vivir este arranque y compartir tanta buena energía. Esto nos confirma que nuestra 16ª edición promete muchos momentos para disfrutar a través de la música, la cultura y los vinos de la isla. 🥂

Big thanks to our Waste & Recycling team for setting up all the bins and systems to look after our Festival Village this long weekend. Here are some tips from the crew:

There are four bins, each with clear signage to help you correctly dispose of your recycling and waste.
 
The majority of what you buy from food stalls will be compostable; these items go in the maroon-lidded bin. Recycling can be placed in the yellow-lidded bins. Aluminium cans and plastic drink bottles with the Container Deposit 10c Levy should be placed in the purple-lidded bins. All other waste can be disposed in the bright red lidded bins.

Plus, don't miss the waste-related workshops over the weekend with waste experts Martyn Royds and Gerry Gillespie all about recycling with a focus on food!

🎶🍷 Hace unas horas vivimos el primer Belingueo de Sonidos Líquidos en la Casa Museo del Campesino… ¡y qué conciertazo!

@sarria_musica y su banda llenaron el mediodía de energía con un directo intenso y elegante, mezclando rock, blues, guiños andaluces y atmósferas psicodélicas que conquistaron al público desde el primer acorde.

Además, fuimos muy afortunad@s: la borrasca Therese apenas se hizo notar y nos permitió vivir plenamente una jornada que contó con todos los ingredientes que hacen de cada Belingueo una experiencia única ✨

Los @vinosdelanzarote fueron los protagonistas de los 3 maridajes que deleitaron al público combinando a la perfección con los platos elaborados por la cocina de los Centros de Arte, Cultura y Turismo poniendo en valor el producto local.

Come at any hour, bring a friend or a sandwich, smile at a stranger across the glimmering flames.

[ID] Colour Connect: Yodokabe Festival, Osaka ✨
Awal bulan Oktober ini kami membawa sedikit kehangatan Bali ke Osaka lewat workshop melukis topeng untuk anak-anak bersama Kids Craft Jiso Osaka. Ruangan penuh dengan tawa dan rasa penasaran saat anak-anak memilih topeng favorit mereka dan mulai mewarnainya dengan warna-warna cerah yang ekspresif.

Para orang tua dengan antusias ikut menyaksikan, beberapa datang dengan sepeda membawa anak-anak mereka. Tim kami juga berbagi cerita di balik topeng Bali dan memandu anak-anak dalam setiap sapuan kuas. Melihat semangat di mata mereka mengingatkan kami bagaimana seni bisa menyatukan lintas budaya dan generasi.

Terima kasih Ms. Akaza, @yodokabe dan @wallshare team atas sambutan yang hangat 💛

[EN] Colour Connect: Yodokabe Festival, Osaka ✨
Early this month we brought a piece of Bali to Osaka through a kids workshop on Balinese mask painting with Kids Craft Jiso Osaka. The space quickly filled with laughter and curiosity as children picked their favorite masks and learned how to paint them with bright, expressive colors.

Parents eagerly watched, some arriving on bicycles with their little ones, as our team shared stories behind the masks and guided the kids through each brushstroke. Seeing the excitement in their eyes reminded us how art connects across cultures and generations.

Thank you Ms. Akaza, @yodokabe and @wallshare team for welcoming us with such warmth 💛

Moment captured by @jeremyangusf_ 📸

In 2026 the National Folk Festival marks sixty years and we're looking back at the artists and communities who have shaped us, and forward to how folk traditions continue to evolve. As part of this milestone, we’re proud to announce the 2026 Lifetime Achievement Award recipients:

Martyn Wyndham-Read is recognised for his extensive career, performing and championing Australian folk music alongside songs from England, his homeland. Involved in the early planning of the first Festival in 1967, he has spent more than six decades carrying Australian folk to audiences around the world.

We also honour Rob and Olya Willis, whose decades of fieldwork have created an extraordinary archive of Australian folklore. Their collection holds 3,000 hours of recordings, photos and documents capturing stories and lived experience from every state and territory.

Join us in celebrating them at the Festival!

🌱 Young Folk Large Ensembles Announced!

Our Young Folk program features up-and-coming solo artists, alongside large ensembles where young musicians come together to share collective music making, and where fun, learning, tradition and collaboration coincide.

This year, Con Folk, the Sydney Conservatorium of Music Folk Ensemble, share much-loved tunes and songs from the British Isles, led by folklorist and cultural historian Dr Kathryn Roberts Parker. Music for Canberra, who are also celebrating 60 years, continues its long tradition of nurturing young musicians through its flagship group Canberra Youth Orchestra. Meanwhile, the Queensland Youth Folk Orchestra brings together young string players exploring Australian, English, Celtic and Scandinavian folk traditions.

We can't wait to host these ensembles who highlight the depth, energy and future of folk music, and the power of young people making music side by side.

Quiet Riot Art Prize is now open for 2026.

A nation-wide open call for wall-based artworks up to 30 × 30cm. Nothing oversized. Nothing loud by default. Just focused, compressed work that has to earn its space.

This is an exhibition built from limitation: hundreds of works, one constraint, no exceptions.

Installed inside the stables of Barwon Park Mansion during @manormade.festival, the exhibition creates a quiet tension— between the historic and the contemporary, the restrained and the disruptive, the delicate and the forceful.

This is a national prize that takes the values built at Rose St., independence, craft, direct support for artists, and applies them to a curated annual exhibition in a setting worthy of the work.

Apply now via quietriot.au. Find further details on our website.

We’re sending our love and support to Grace Petrie, who has postponed her Australian tour due to a family bereavement. Grace is a treasured part of our Festival community, and we look forward to welcoming her back to the National Folk Festival very soon.

We’re very grateful that Irish Mythen will step in at this year’s Festival. Irish joined us last year, showed deep commitment to the Festival and our community, and left a powerful impression on us all. We’re honoured to welcome them back.

A JUNO-nominated Irish-born Canadian singer-songwriter based in Prince Edward Island, Irish has built an international reputation through fearless songwriting and formidable live performance. From Glastonbury to the Sydney Opera House, their shows balance warmth, wit and extraordinary vocal power, forging deep connection with audiences.

Speaking about stepping in, Irish shared:
“My thoughts are with Grace as she navigates such a difficult time at home. It’s my absolute honour to step in for her on these Australian dates. There’s only one Grace Petrie - but I promise I’ll give my all to have you laughing, crying, waving angry fists at the establishment and everything in between. It’s truly an honour to step in for my pal Grace. We’re all thinking of you, friend.”

All performances will proceed as scheduled. Full program here: folkfestival.org.au/program (link in bio)

From May 2026, the National Folk Festival will no longer request or use Spotify accounts, links or statistics in artist submissions, assessment processes, or marketing. 

Spotify has become the dominant global music streaming platform, shaping how artists distribute, and audiences discover and consume music. With that dominance comes responsibility. We believe Spotify has consistently failed to meet that responsibility. 

This decision is not about putting more pressure on artists, rather about putting choice back in their hands. We are choosing to carry this decision at an institutional level to support artists’ freedom of choice to share their music however they wish, without pressure or penalty.

We encourage our fellow folks, festivals, venues, and presenters to join us in rethinking your reliance on platforms you perceive to be exploitative or unethical.

To read the full statement, visit our website www.folkfestival.org.au/ethos and scroll down.

FROM THE STREETS OF MULLUMBIMBY TO THE MULLUM ROOTS STAGE.

Last year I met a young busker at Mullum Roots Festival.

We got talking about songwriting. That night he went home and wrote a new song.

The following day he tracked me down at the festival and played it for me. This is the moment I recorded.

I made him a promise: write 10 songs before the next festival and I’ll give you a spot on the lineup.

Well, he did it.

And this July, he’ll be performing at Mullum Roots Festival 2027.

Sometimes the best things happen when you least expect them.

This is what Mullum Roots is all about. ❤️

A little sanctuary in the middle of the chaos 🌿✨This year’s @cubadupa  just got even better…

@vicuniwgtn is transforming its architecture and design school into something pretty special called - Whanga—The Cove.

Right in the heart of the festival, you’ll find an immersive indoor forest filled with art, sound, light and creativity. Think sculptural installations, ambient soundscapes, poetry, short films, hands-on activities… and even the chance to sit down and ask a real-life philosopher anything.

It’s designed as a place to pause - a calm, creative escape from the buzz of Cuba Street. Wander through living trees, discover hidden artworks, make your own zine, or just sit and soak it all in. Even better, it's free entry!

You can expect a living pathway winds through the space (constructed from real trees and foliage), an interactive scale model of the city, delicate 3D‑printed vines hanging overhead, a soundscape of Aotearoa’s native birds, a showcase of student-made films, animations, and visual effects, DIY zine zone, free temporary tattoos, and a self-service photobooth. 📸

We love this kind of collaboration - students, artists, and the wider Wellington community coming together to create something playful, thoughtful, and a little bit magical.

And it doesn’t stop there - the Vic Uni Glover Park Stage will be showcasing incredible local talent all weekend long 🎶

If you need a breather, a moment of wonder, or just something a bit different… the cove is calling.

See you there 🌿

En la gala A Greener Festival Awards celebrada en Londres, nuestro festival fue reconocido con el Pied Piper Award (Greener Communications) 🏆♻️

Este galardón nos premia por nuestra comunicación sobre sostenibilidad más allá del propio evento; y por el compromiso con la sensibilización en torno a la protección del medio ambiente y la biodiversidad del geoparque en el que se celebra el festival. Un reconocimiento enmarcado en una gala muy especial en la que han participado festivales de todo el mundo —Reino Unido, Noruega, India, Colombia, Países Bajos y muchos más—, demostrando que la música puede ser un motor global de transformación.

Y por si fuera poco… ¡renovamos nuestra tercera estrella A Greener Festival! ⭐⭐⭐
Una confirmación de la apuesta firme, coherente y consciente que mantenemos con el cuidado y el respeto del delicado entorno donde celebramos cada edición como es La Geria.

Este reconocimiento también es de ustedes. Del público, colaboradores, empresas y compañer@s que entienden, respetan, se implican y que son un pilar fundamental de nuestras medidas sostenibles. Gracias de corazón 💚 Porque sin su colaboración y actitud ejemplar, nada de esto sería posible.

🫂No podemos ocultar que estamos muy emocionad@s y felices por este bonito camino que continuamos andando junt@s en Sonidos Líquidos

Seguimos sonando. Seguimos cuidando. Seguimos creyendo que la música también puede cambiar el mundo. 🌍✨

Hay lugares que no se pisan, se escuchan. Vinos que cuentan una historia épica que nació de la tierra volcánica, sabores que llevan a ese territorio que no se parece a ningún otro (al menos en este mundo) y música que se funde con el paisaje creando emociones IRREPETIBLES.

Así se vive Sonidos Líquidos: una experiencia donde Lanzarote no es solo el escenario, es el alma. Un festival cultivado con el mismo cariño que nuestros viticultores cuidan nuestras viñas y racimos, sostenible y profundamente ligado al patrimonio isleño, donde el público no viene solo a disfrutar, sino a formar parte, a respetar y a valorar lo que nos hace únicos.

Este año compartimos en FITUR este vídeo que nos invita a brindar por los grandísimos recuerdos que hemos creado junt@s, llevando la esencia de la isla más allá del Atlántico.

Confirmamos algo que nos llena de orgullo: Sonidos Líquidos conquista fuera de las fronteras y es un gran atractivo para el público que busca experiencias auténticas, conscientes y memorables.

Opening day (Fri 24th) starts at 3:00 PM.

With the concept “Play with the Earth,” the traveling creative collective CINEMA CARAVAN brings a special space to life on the sandy shores of Zushi during Golden Week.

As a platform where people and culture come together in nature, this normally quiet beach transforms through a collaboration between CINEMA CARAVAN, the communities they’ve encountered around the world, and the local Zushi community.

In the ever-changing natural environment by the sea, engage all five senses, experience with your whole body, feel the Earth, and play with it.

Come and enjoy the warm, welcoming space created through local connections and global cultural exchange—an expression of the CINEMA CARAVAN spirit.

🇦🇺 🇧🇪 3 DAYS LEFT TO APPLY FOR THE BRUSSELS COMIC ARTIST RESIDENCY PROGRAM 🇧🇪 🇦🇺

The Perth Comic Arts Festival, in association with the Musée de la Bande Dessinée @comicartmuseumbxl, is very proud to present the first comics-artist residency in Brussels available to Western Australian artists.
Between October and December 2026, for three weeks, the Museum is hosting Belgian and international comic artists in Brussels for an artistic residency. This residency, with the support of PCAF, is available to a Western Australian comics-maker. The residency will bring together artists to share, explore, and inspire one another.

The Museum undertakes to organize the residency with the Artist to enable them to work optimally on their project, following the Artist for the duration of the residency and doing its best to:
🗯️ Provide help and advice on their work
🗯️ Share professional contacts and facilitate meetings
🗯️ Invite the Artist to public or networking events that would happen during its stay
🗯️ Include the Artist in the Museum activities, if the programming allows it
🗯️ The Museum will also provide the artist with 50€ per diem for up to 21 days

PCAF will support the artist by:
🗯️ Assisting the artist with finding accommodation in Brussels for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $3000 AUD towards accommodation costs for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $2000 AUD towards return flight costs to Brussels from Perth

WHO CAN APPLY?
Comic artists meeting all of the following criteria:
🗯️ A practicing comics artist based in Western Australia with a graphic novel or long-form comic currently in process
🗯️ An Australian citizen or Permanent Resident with an up-to-date passport
🗯️ At least 18 years of age

Please head to pcaf.org.au/2026-brussels-residency for full details on the residency and the application guidelines!

IMPORTANT DATES
🗯️ Applications open: 26th of July, 2026
🗯️ Applications close: 14th of August, 2026
🗯️ Applicants notified: 31st of August, 2026
🗯️ Residency Period: 3 continuous weeks, between the 10th of October and 15th of December (to be decided in consultation with PCAF and the Museum).

🇦🇺 🇧🇪 BRUSSELS COMIC ARTIST RESIDENCY PROGRAM APPLICATIONS CLOSE TONIGHT 🇧🇪 🇦🇺

The Perth Comic Arts Festival, in association with the Musée de la Bande Dessinée @comicartmuseumbxl, is very proud to present the first comics-artist residency in Brussels available to Western Australian artists.
Between October and December 2026, for three weeks, the Museum is hosting Belgian and international comic artists in Brussels for an artistic residency. This residency, with the support of PCAF, is available to a Western Australian comics-maker. The residency will bring together artists to share, explore, and inspire one another.

The Museum undertakes to organize the residency with the Artist to enable them to work optimally on their project, following the Artist for the duration of the residency and doing its best to:
🗯️ Provide help and advice on their work
🗯️ Share professional contacts and facilitate meetings
🗯️ Invite the Artist to public or networking events that would happen during its stay
🗯️ Include the Artist in the Museum activities, if the programming allows it
🗯️ The Museum will also provide the artist with 50€ per diem for up to 21 days

PCAF will support the artist by:
🗯️ Assisting the artist with finding accommodation in Brussels for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $3000 AUD towards accommodation costs for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $2000 AUD towards return flight costs to Brussels from Perth

WHO CAN APPLY?
Comic artists meeting all of the following criteria:
🗯️ A practicing comics artist based in Western Australia with a graphic novel or long-form comic currently in process
🗯️ An Australian citizen or Permanent Resident with an up-to-date passport
🗯️ At least 18 years of age

Please head to pcaf.org.au/2026-brussels-residency for full details on the residency and the application guidelines!

IMPORTANT DATES
🗯️ Applications open: 26th of July, 2026
🗯️ Applications close: 14th of August, 2026
🗯️ Applicants notified: 31st of August, 2026
🗯️ Residency Period: 3 continuous weeks, between the 10th of October and 15th of December (to be decided in consultation with PCAF and the Museum).

High Headliners!

Week after week of cloudless blue skies and a week before MardiGrass the rain starts—and doesn't stop. Oh well, ‘MuddiGrass’ again! The scene is set, last tents went up today and the last stage is almost finished. The little Village is quite excited about our Annual Protest Weekend and we’ve sold a lot more tickets online than ever before. I’m guessing there’s a lot of new cannabis users interested now that it’s ‘legal’.

Tourist attractions don’t always last, I’ve noticed, and possibly Nimbin is one of them. The colourful hippy town attracted lots of visitors not long ago, but not so anymore. We are not the novelty we once were. Many of our day trippers were motivated by buying some weed and now it’s available at your local chemist, at half the price!

Change is everywhere. I know I have carried on before about weed drinks replacing alcohol, but the trend is gathering momentum. This is the new and healthy way to relax and unwind, with no hangovers, less calories…and less aggression!

Meanwhile, Down Under, use of meth has doubled in a decade according to wastewater reports. Cocaine, MDMA and heroin, up by a record percentage, just in this last year. Use of everything is way up! So how is the ‘war’ going, coppers? 

They never, ever, ever seem to support change, which I guess makes sense because their jobs are on the line, or so they think. Don’t ask the army about stopping wars! Honestly, in the last year meth use went up 23%, cocaine 20% and everything else that is illicit, up over 20%, yet we keep doing the same thing over and over.

We need a ‘Drug Summit’ in Canberra to seriously look at the whole ‘drug war’ and what we should do about it, because what we’re doing now is going backwards, fast. Prohibition created this nightmare and only ending prohibition and changing society’s attitude to ‘drug’ use will fix it.

Love to everyone and Happy MardiGrass!

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

The National Folk School is back in 2027!

Spend three days before the Festival learning directly from some of the world’s leading folk artists and tradition bearers. Go deeper than the one-hour workshop or Festival Ensemble: learn by ear, build your technique and repertoire, explore a tradition, and make music and dance with fellow folkies.

Your 2027 Folk School tutors are:
👞 Nic Gareiss (USA) — Percussive Dance
🎸 Jenn Butterworth (Scotland) — Traditional Guitar
🪗 Will Pound (England) — Harmonica & Melodeon
🎻 Sami Braman (USA) — Old-Time Fiddle
🪕 Allison de Groot (Canada) — Clawhammer Banjo
🎸 Quinn Bachand (Canada) — Guitar

And when the Folk School finishes, the music keeps going: all six tutors are also performing at the National Folk Festival in duo and trio combos. What you learn over those three days travels with you into the sessions, dances, ensembles and music-making of the Festival itself.

Returning after a long hiatus, the Folk School continues a National Folk Festival tradition stretching back more than 25 years, presented in partnership with the ANU School of Music.

Come early. Learn deeply. Then join in.

Long before social media and digital cameras, racing in Southland thrived on the same passion, creativity, and sense of adventure that still drives riders today. We’re celebrating that timeless spirit by sharing the incredible story of Barrie Neilson, a man who lived through the golden era of motorcycling in Invercargill and remains deeply connected to the Burt Munro Challenge.

Barrie didn’t just race for five years at Teretonga and on Oreti Beach. He was also interviewed for the original documentary that inspired the Burt Munro movie. He was there, at that historic moment when Burt’s era met a new generation of riders.

So, what were those days really like?

- When Barrie switched from British bikes to Japanese ones, he needed practice. But how do you train when the track is covered in sheep droppings? Simple: he and his mate Neil loaded the race bike and two brooms onto a trailer and swept the track clean before riding. (No fences, no Armco barriers back then!)

- And what about this? During a race on Oreti Beach, the pilot of a commercial plane arriving in Invercargill saw the action below. What did he do? He flew low over the beach so his passengers could watch the bikes racing, turned over Riverton, and came back low again so the other side of the plane could enjoy the view. He even showed the landing gear before heading to the runway! 

- Barrie also remembers the Invercargill Centennial Parade, riding on the Southland Motorcycle Club float alongside Burt Munro and other members. Burt, he says, looked frustrated...why? Because he wanted to work on his Velocette, which had broken down at a Teretonga event.

📸 Historic Photos:
- The Southland Motorcycle Club float in the Centennial Parade, with classic bikes and the checkered flag.
- Barrie and Geordy Read on Oreti Beach after winning their classes (500cc and Production). Their prize? A tin of Duckhams oil each. That photo even appeared on the cover of Duckhams Oil magazine in the UK!

【BALI CULTURE DAY】
映画： #アルナとその好物

「バリ・カルチャー・デー 2026」では、食、映画、そしてコミュニティを通じて、インドネシア文化を体験する特別なひとときをお届けします。バリの伝統的な習慣である「Mebat（ムバット）」にインスピレーションを得たこのプログラムは、共に料理を作る喜びを分かち合うものです。
会場内では、インドネシア各地の美食を巡る旅を追いかけた特別映画の上映をはじめ、シアター・テントでのバリの若手映画制作者による短編作品の公開、さらにはワークショップやインドネシア人アーティストによるライブ・エンターテインメントをお楽しみいただけます。また、お土産が揃う「トコ・オレ・オレ（Toko Oleh-Oleh）」を探索したり、レストランで本場のバリ料理を堪能したりと、インドネシアの魅力を存分に体感できるイベントとなっています。

Concept：
メバットはバリ島に伝わる共同調理の伝統で、バンジャール（村落共同体）の人々が集まり、儀式​​や地域社会の大きな行事のために料理を準備します。テンポが速く、実践的で、活気に満ちています。食材を切ったり混ぜたり、ラワールやサテなどの料理を作ったりと、誰もが役割を担います。単なる作業というよりは、人々が一体となって動き、話し、協力し合う、共有された流れのように感じられます。
メバットは単なる食卓の場ではなく、人との繋がりを象徴するものです。物語や技術、伝統が、参加するだけで自然に受け継がれていきます。その過程には強い一体感が生まれ、単なる文化的な慣習にとどまらず、コミュニティの精神を生き生きと保つ社会的な体験にもなっています。
イベントを通して、バリ島とインドネシアの文化を体験することができます。料理、物語の語り、そして日々の儀式が、フェスティバルの雰囲気の中で皆で共に繰り広げられるでしょう。

🗞️NEWS! Real, relates to Kiwiburn, NEWS, from us to you. Turns out, rewriting a constitution takes a bit more than one spicy Facebook thread, so we’re officially moving into Phase Two of Kiwiburn’s constitutional reform process.
Here’s what happens over the next few months (good things take time). 
🕥From now: Jump into the dedicated Discord channel (handily called ‘Constitutional reform suggestions’) to suggest ideas, raise concerns, and argue passionately about governance structures.
📆July: We’ll hold a hui to discuss the ideas that come through.
✍🏻August: The first draft of the updated constitution will be presented.
🎙️September & October: Another hui, more feedback, and revisions to make sure we land somewhere as agreeable as possible. 
🗳️November: We’ll hold a Special General Meeting (SGM) where members (that’s you!) can vote on the final constitution.
This is the part where general vibes get turned into actual words which will actually be written down and enacted, which means your input matters now more than ever.

If you’ve got thoughts on how Kiwiburn should be structured, governed, or protected for the future, get involved! This is our community, we want as many voices as possible contributing to the final result. 
Democracy: Is messy, occasionally bordering on tedious, but ultimately our best bet for a happy community.

If this doesn’t work, we have a Plan B that just reads: “All disputes shall be settled through combative fire dancing.” 😉

💚Theme: Moss & Microchips💠

The Meaning: Imagine a future where advanced technology leads to the unravelling of society. We can see the path to this through technology encouraging isolating individualism over values of community and nature. We can’t avoid the growing role of technology in our lives, so let’s explore how we want to exist in accordance with this and choose how we wish to balance it with our place in the natural world. 🌱 We’re proud to welcome Waking Life in Portugal to the Ecosystem Restoration Communities network.

Located in central Portugal, this community-led initiative is restoring degraded land through reforestation, water retention, soil regeneration and collective stewardship.

Through art, culture, education and shared learning, the project is exploring how communities can rebuild deeper relationships with the land while creating more resilient and regenerative ways of living together.

Their work combines:
🌳 Ecosystem restoration
💧 Water retention and landscape resilience
🛠️ Hands-on regenerative skills
🎨 Creativity and cultural exchange
🤝 Community participation and learning

caption:
In Covas do Barroso, the European Union has made a sinister choice. Under the banner of the “green transition”, the EU has granted “strategic” status to a lithium mine that threatens to devastate ancient farming lands recognised by the UN as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System.

The calculation is brutal. Bureaucrats and investors fast-track permits, dismiss water contamination risks, and label local opposition as an obstacle to progress. But let’s call this what it is: bright green colonialism. The real green transition would mean walkable cities, massive public transport investment, and smaller, more efficient vehicles, not ripping open the Portuguese mountains to sustain our addiction to private electric SUVs.

This fight is no longer just about a mine in Trás-os-Montes. Residents have taken the European Commission to court, challenging the very legality of labeling extraction as “sustainability”. If they lose, it signals that any community, anywhere in Europe, can be bulldozed for “strategic” supply chains.

Covas do Barroso is a moment of truth. If your climate solution requires destroying ecosystems and torching farmland to dig up minerals, it’s a fraud. A fake green future that simply swaps carbon emissions for cratered landscapes and poisoned water is more like a bad trip.

Follow @udcovasdobarroso

🐏This is a gentle plea and earnest request for a little h.e.l.p at Black Sheep Ranger HQ. You’ve all seen the news: ‘Kiwiburn needs vols’, ‘do it year-round, you’ll be better for it’ etc.
Well, have we got the compromise for you: The Rangers need an experienced Ranger (well, ideally a flock of them) to keep everything working throughout the Burn, this would title you as our Support Ranger/s. We’re not asking for year-round support, we’ve got that covered. 
🐑What we’d like is someone(s) to step up a little to help support the training sessions at the beginning of the Burn, support the Rangers throughout the Burn, and just generally help the Rangers Range. It’s like an operations manager role, without the management part. It’s like being a Ranger shift lead or on-call expert a few times throughout the Burn, to help educate and keep everything flowing. Good news, there’s (probably) no admin tasks involved. 
Basically, we’d like someone with a pretty good idea of how Rangering works to make themselves a little more available to ensure the Ranger leads can deliver training and maaaaaybe get a little time to enjoy the Burn themselves.
🌾You will be perfect for this role if you are an experienced Ranger and:
Have been looking for a relatively low-commitment way to commit just a little more
OR
Have an increasingly unignorable feeling that it maybe just might be time to do a little more for some of these critical Burn functions, coupled with the realisation that if it’s not for you, some poor soul will spend yet another Burn lingering near-ish to Rangers HQ for the majority of their time
OR
Wanna give it a go.
Wanna give it a go and be a Support Ranger?
Contact blacksheep@kiwiburn.com for more information

Our previous edition of the EFP included a survey on setting the AGM date and sourcing an alternative to Facebook. For the AGM survey and attendance we mentioned you would need to be a member of Kiwiburn Inc. We received a couple of queries about how to become members.
Membership in this case means you are either a KB25 member or a KB26 member (or both).
You are a KB25 member if you:
were the final purchaser of a ticket for KB25 (whether you attended or not does not matter),
were accepted for direct membership in 2025
Your KB25 membership expiry in either of the above two cases is extended until the date of the 2025 AGM whenever it is held – either on Paddock in January or online in February (have your say in the survey).
Alternatively you will be a KB26 member if you:
are the final purchaser of a ticket for KB26
were accepted for direct membership for 2026
If you are a current financial KB26 member under either of the above options then you are entitled to attend the AGM covering 2025 activities.
If you have not yet purchased a KB26 ticket but are scheduled to be offered a ticket to purchase for KB26 then once that ticket is paid then you become a member that way.  All KB26 tickets will have been paid for before the event starts and therefore also before the AGM. 
For information on membership and how to become a member please refer to the Kiwiburn Membership page.

🔥We’ve talked before about fire restrictions at Kiwiburn, and we know it’s something many of you are thinking about – especially given how the weather’s been this summer. 👀
At the time of writing, Hunterville is in a Low Fire Danger rating with an Open Fire Season. That means fire is currently allowed within Kiwiburn’s usual rules. However – and this is the important part – fire season status can change, sometimes quickly.
BIt’s not just about the weather. Dryness, wind, and heat all matter. But there’s another big factor that’s just as important – fire response in this area relies on volunteer crews, and those volunteers are currently stretched thin. If local crews are tired, over-committed, or don’t have the capacity to safely respond, fire restrictions can be increased – even if the weather still looks okay.
If we move to a Restricted Fire Season, fire performance and FAST-approved braziers would still be allowed.
If we move to a Prohibited Fire Season, neither fire performance nor braziers would be allowed.
Either way, in anything other than an Open Fire Season, the burning of the Effigy and Temple would be very unlikely.
Fire rules aren’t just guidelines, they’re about real people and real risk. Adhering to fire restrictions (not ignoring or bending them) ensures:
The safety of participants, volunteers, neighbours, landowners, and the environment
No additional pressure is applied to already-stretched emergency services
Our ongoing ability to run future Kiwiburn events
We maintain our relationship of trust with the local community, emergency services and volunteer groups
We know that’s what everyone wants and reflects our Principles of Civic Duty, Communal Effort, and Leave No Trace.
If anything changes, we’ll let you know as soon as we can and be clear about what’s allowed and what isn’t.
Thanks for being thoughtful, responsible humans.

“Para mim, é uma honra ser jurado na Tattoo Week, pois, desde o início da Tattoo Week Rio, eu vinha participando. No primeiro ano, fui de curioso e, desde então, era meu sonho subir no palco e levantar o tão sonhado troféu da maior convenção do mundo.

E agora, mais um ano junto nessa missão de avaliar trabalhos de outros artistas e sempre levar minha experiência para os artistas que estão presentes na convenção”, disse @gustavo.tattoo .

🌈Wow – what a ride. While most of us wandered off into the sunset a week ago (muddy, happy, and slightly feral), a heroic handful of humans were still out there lovingly packing down the very last bits of on-site infrastructure. And now, at long last, we can officially say Kiwiburn 2026: A Work of HeArt has wrapped. Deep breaths. Group hug. What the heck just happened?!

🎨33 Art Installations, 66 Theme Camps, many rainbows, some even double! This year’s Burn has earned the name RainbowBurn! Yes, we had some rain – not nearly as much as MudBurn – and you can’t have rainbows without some rain. Spirits were high and the puddle stomping game was strong. Bananas were dancing, fruit was stolen (accidentally), and then returned! Stickers were collected, Art was created, friendships were made, and boogies were had. 

If you’re reading this, remember when sharing pics to our Instagram and tag the Kiwiburn account with your uploads. While we’re on the subject, a gentle reminder to please only upload photos with people in them if they have expressly consented to it. Some people may consent to a photo but not the upload on social media. Online life and offline life are very separate for some members of the community and want to keep it that way so please be mindful of photos. If you blur people or crop, please blur or crop full bodies so people are not recognisable. 

We hope you had as magical a time as we did. And now that you’re (hopefully) mostly recovered and back among the civilians, why not channel all that fresh inspiration into your next big idea? Kiwiburn 2027 is calling. Dream up an Art piece, start or join a Theme Camp, or take the plunge into a year-round volunteer role (trust us – it’s the best way to keep the magic alive all year). Until then… bring on Kiwiburn 2027! Love you!

🎟️Did you score a ticket in the lottery? Lucky you! It was drawn on Sunday the 14th, but if you missed out – don’t be afraid! All names have been moved into the STEP queue in the order of when you signed up.
That queue can move fast so keep your eyes on your portal and on your emails.
➡️A few things to note:
If you ‘won’ a ticket in the lottery, you don’t have too long to purchase it – so do this asap! Check the deadline for the ticket purchase in your portal.
If you don’t wish to purchase said ticket for whatever reason, please decline this asap so the next person in the queue can purchase it.
If you’re in the queue but don’t need a ticket, please remove yourself from STEP so that it can move to the next person.
Didn’t get a ticket? There are still plenty of opportunities to get yourself on the Paddock. In this EFP you will find several volunteering roles that want you with even more still available on the website.
You never know what experiences you’ll have and friends you’ll make when you take a chance and take that step. Traffic management, site team, perimeter, sanitation, just to name a few. So have a read!
Only 37 days till the Paddock opens and 45 days till the Effigy burns, the excitement is building! Do you know where your booty shorts and tutus are?

🎛️Do you love Kiwiburn, enjoy a good spreadsheet, and find yourself mysteriously drawn to the phrase “strategic decision-making”? Then you might be our next Services Facilitator! We’re looking for a calm-in-the-chaos human who can support the powerhouse teams behind Depot, Gate, Greeters, Ticketing, and Town Hall. This is a year-round role (with a bit more action as Burn season approaches) where you’ll help keep communication flowing, timelines on track, teams supported, and ExCom caffeinated and informed. It’s big-picture leadership mixed with practical project wrangling—and plenty of opportunities to make a real difference for the Kiwiburn community.

🧠If you’re organised, collaborative, love working with passionate volunteers, and don’t mind the occasional flurry of emails, we’d love to hear from you. Prior leadership is a bonus, but enthusiasm, good humour, and a willingness to dive in are just as valuable. Join us in shaping the future of Kiwiburn—one policy, timeline, and well-supported team at a time!

For more information about this role, check out our website.
To apply for this role and to see the other year round volunteer roles available, peep the link in our bio 🔗

Building skills. Building community. Building with nature.

Earth Architecture Academy - Erasmus Youth training at Waking Life

Join us at build-up, from 6th to 15th of May, for an 8 day program on natural building. 

A learning opportunity into natural building techniques - from wattle & daub to carpentry and the restoration of existing sculpted and woven structures.

Guided by @cru.atelier @thomas0tt @miorouge_ we’ll shift between theory and practice, exchanging grounded skills & knowledge around the lake, getting our hands dirty and learning what it means to create with Pachamomma’s materials :)

This is an open call for folks residing in Portugal, Spain, Italy, Greece, Georgia, Belgium, France and Kosovo. The training is funded by Erasmus+ and includes accommodation and travel costs.

Apply by March 16th.

🧳Before you start playing boot-Tetris, a quick PSA: pack smart, not heavy. That hill on the way out is real, and an over-loaded car can turn your exit into a slow slide in the wrong direction. Bring what you need – just don’t bring everything you own. 🙈

One of the 10 Principles is Radical Self-Reliance, so it’s worth checking out the official What to Bring guide at our link in bio before you start packing.

Think water, food, and containers you can actually carry and refill. Add solid shelter, warm bedding, and shade for daytime survival. The Paddock can serve up scorching sun, freezing nights, hectic wind, and, as we saw a couple of years ago, a ridiculous amount of rain and mud, so it’s best to be prepared for anything.

When night falls, lights matter. Headlamps, LEDs, fairy lights – they keep you visible, upright, and help you find your way home, plus they look pretty and who doesn’t like looking at the pretty things?!

Don’t forget the fun: costumes, instruments, and playful offerings that help turn a paddock into THE Paddock. Just keep it MOOP-free – no glitter, feathers, sequins, or anything else that can easily fall off into the grass.

Pack with intention, care, and a little creative flair.

💦A friendly reminder for all Paddock-bound humans – there is onsite drinking water available so there’s no need to load yourself up with heavy water containers before you arrive.

Bringing less weight means lower transport emissions, which in turn helps us all leave less trace. Using the onsite water supply is a small choice that makes a meaningful difference with a bonus – fresh, filtered rain water is way tastier that anything you’ll get from a city!

All you need to do is:

Bring a sturdy, reusable bottle/jerry can/ container of some sort
Make sure it has a secure lid so you can safely transport water back to your camp (if you’ve got large containers, or many of them, a little cart/trolley helps with transport!)
While we’re on the topic of caring for the land, this is also a great moment to pause and consider what else you’re bringing with you. Please avoid packing products like shampoo, soap, etc. These can cause long-lasting harm to the Paddock and can’t be used in the river. Let’s all be filthy hippies together. 💧

Rock Away🏆 “優勝トロフィー”はこのダルマ。

賞金に加えて、「Rock Away」の優勝者に贈られるのは、ただのトロフィーではありません。

今年も、ACRAFT / @a.craft86 が手がける、世界にひとつだけのデニムだるまが勝者へ贈られます。

お気に入りのモノに”手を施す”ことで、新たな命を宿す。

それがACRAFTのものづくりの原点。

履き込まれたデニムからインスピレーションを受け、日本の伝統文化である「だるま」と融合させた作品には、**“温故創新”**という想いが込められています。

廃棄されるはずだったデニムに新たな価値を吹き込み、一体一体すべて異なる表情を持つこの作品。

スタイルを貫き、自分らしさを表現したライダーだけが手にすることのできる、Rock Awayの象徴です。

今年、この特別なトロフィーを手にするのは誰なのか。

#tbt☀️ especial de 2015 quando tive o prazer de participar do festival @miaufanzara festival de street art numa cidadezinha no interior da Espanha com menos de 2000 pessoas.
Memória que não dá pra esquecer
Gracias amigos, te echo de menos 🫶🏾

“El perro hace guau… y el gato hace MIAU!” 🐶🐈💬 @miaufanzara • X edición • 10 x 8,5

Un festival nacido para cuidar el entorno a través del arte. 🏞️

Fue un gusto participar en esta edición. Gracias a todo el equipo por invitarme y a todo el pueblo por el recibimiento. En especial a María José y su familia por confiarme la fachada de su casa, darme via libre.. y no dejar que me faltara de nada. También agradecer a Pilar y Linares por acogernos como a uno más de la familia. 🫶

Gracias @lamaryposafotografia por los disparos!

Este mural me ha dado más de un quebradero de cabeza 😅. El reto era conseguir que las ventanas sumaran al diseño en vez de estorbar. Al final salió este homenaje al universo de Tom & Jerry, siguiendo en mi linea de glitch, pixel art, cartoon y ya sabes..graffiti..
Recién la he bautizado como que “Digital Nostalgia”. Dime que no mola el concepto..😌

Además, me tocó presentar la obra delante de toda la gente que vino al festival. No os voy a engañar, hablar en público sigue dándome respeto, pero moló mucho poder contar de dónde sale todo este universo y cómo ha ido creciendo desde mis comienzos..

Me vuelvo con un mural de mis fav hasta la fecha, algunos baños refrescantes en el río, muchas risas y un montón de buenos momentos compartidos con artistas y colegas a los que admiro.

Si todavía no habéis estado en MIAU Fanzara, os animo a visitarlo.🙌

Thanks 4 all! 🤍

📜You may or may not know that Kiwiburn is an incorporated society, and as such, the Kiwiburn organisation follows a set constitution.
Due to a change in legislation, Kiwiburn needs to re-register as a society. This means reviewing the constitution to ensure it meets the new legislation, and if not, it needs to be amended. All Societies have to re-register and file their Constitution with amendments, or without if they think existing rules meet all the new requirements, before April next year. The Societies Registrar will then review them and either accept or decline re-registration.
Any review of Kiwiburn’s governance structure and operations is an entirely separate matter and is not, and should not, be tied to reregistering by April next year.  It requires engagement with the entire community and widespread discussion and debate,  Then based on the outcome of that process Constitutional changes may need to be proposed and voted on. That will be a lengthy and fully inclusive process.

➡️ExCom wishes to advise the community that they have determined there should be two separate processes:
1: Simple registration with minimal amendments
2: A separate full community discussion/review on structure and any changes needed to the constitution that arise from those community wide discussions.
This is just a quick message to inform the community that both reregistration and proposed governance and operational reviews are well underway.

caption:
Over 10 days, 30 peeps banded together to co-create and care for each other and the land, as part of our autumn Erasmus youth exchange program. 

Kimchi fermentation and sourdough bread workshops opened our appetite for exploring ways of food-making. Further in the field, The Egg is now nesting in fresh lines of various trees, bushes and veggies as we dove into growing syntropic agroforestry systems & learned about seed collection, cooperation, propagation and new ways of approaching web-of-life interactions. 

Conversations around the concept of resilient communities wove throughout our days, with both the notions of resilience & community evolving, as we held more complexity & greater understanding of interdependence. 

Obrigada to all the participants for contributing with nourishing and creative explorations, mapping the land, documenting different fauna and flora, cyanotype impressions, building natural structures from acacias, body activations and facilitating the sweetest afternoon of crochet & cakes with the grannies of the sewing club of Monte da Pedra.

🎒Alright humans, it’s time. Kiwiburn is moving off Facebook. It’s time to stop feeding the algorithm. Unless you’ve had your head in the sand for the past few years (and we wouldn’t blame you for that), you’ll know that Facebook has become a bit of a cesspit. And not the fun ‘hippie-soup’ kind of cesspit you’ll sometimes find on the Paddock. No, the worst kind of cesspit, one that’s decidedly anti-Burner!. 
We could be here all day detailing reasons why Facebook is just not the go anymore, but we’re certain you already know why. Instead, we’ll leave you with a few of the main ones: 😒
* Facebook doesn’t align with Burner principles (far from it)
* The algorithm controls all, if it decides not to show you something, good luck seeing it
* Group admin control means less now than ever – the algorithm now blocks posts it doesn’t like automatically. Even mundane ones that it decides don’t align with their community standards. Usually us admins don’t even get to see them at all, Facebook just yeets them into the ether, yet it comes across as us censoring posts (which we have not been doing)
* Other events are also moving away from Facebook (even Burning Man doesn’t have an official group)
* META. ‘Nuff said.
* The list goes on…

caption:
This essay has been in the making for a long while, stitched from many late night and early morning conravesations.  

It is not a doctrine for festival puritanism or a manifesto for competitive karma-olympics.. The critique is born from love, from the visceral memory of a track, a beat and a groove that realigned your brain stem, of eye contact in a crowd that felt like a religious experience, of a dawn that broke in an indescribably and painfully beautiful way. It is a defence of the rebellious, the weird, the psychedelic, the exhausting rave timewarp.. those rare, deeply affecting moments where art and communion fuse into a reason for being. 

These are not trivial pleasures; they are among the sweetest pursuits that give texture and meaning to a life. The argument is not in creating an unattainable golden standard, but instead for allegiance, to that sacred frequency against its corporate simulacrum.

We all participate in numerous industrial-complexes, and our lives are twisted in dark, delirious ways, so the story is far from simple. We navigate a world that contorts us with pressures we did not ask for and bends us into shapes we did not choose. This is an eruption of thought, that itself welcomes critique and dialogue, but simply refuses to submit to apathy or conformity.

Rêve on ;)

💻TLDR: Kiwiburn IS moving off Facebook and we ARE listening to you – your feedback will help us decide what comes next. ⏭️
You may have heard the loudish whispers – and the Propaganda is true (we have told you that we only share the truth…) We have announced our intention for Kiwiburn to GTF off Facebook. There are a bunch of very valid reasons for this move, including:
* FB is a commercial enterprise – it simply doesn’t align with Burner Principles, no matter how you spin it
* The algorithms are a nightmare. Posts are queued, hidden, or removed without moderator input. Our FB Admin Team has no control or visibility over these actions, but still they cop the backlash from accusations of censorship or bias – which is categorically untrue but happens more and more often (especially when posts get traction)
* The group is just too big. It’s no longer representative of the community who actually participate in or engage with Kiwiburn. While overseas membership keeps growing, overall engagement has dropped significantly – by around 38% year on year
* The vibe just isn’t vibing. Many people no longer feel comfortable commenting or sharing views due to the tone of some conversations. The group has become a soapbox for a few rather than a balanced dialogue for many. This isn’t about silencing criticism – we want and we welcome constructive feedback – but we do want a space that’s kind, respectful, and genuinely welcoming.

Music is a siren, and history is a shipwreck. But from the wreckage we uncover stories of pain, love, rebellion, freedom, sin and sorrow.. anthems and dancefloors that built families and toppled empires.

This essay makes no claim to totality. The seismic musical map is necessarily incomplete, drawn in some broad, politically significant strokes. Countless titans remain unnamed, the dissident punk of Soviet bloc bands, the reinventions of Madonna, the shameless edges of Prince, ... To catalogue every insurrectionary chord would require an encyclopedia, not a musico-historical snapshot. 

Our purpose is not archival exhaustiveness, but the articulation of a clear and urgent thesis: that music’s history is a history of political force, and its future sites of gathering, from the squatted basement to the corporatized festival grounds, are where the battle for that force’s meaning is eternally waged. 

What is on offer is not the definitive history, but a critical lens. The rest is just a song waiting to be sung.

caption:
Right now, we’re sitting amongst half-packed containers, wet marquees, aching bodies and VERY full hearts ❤️

Six months ago, Morph was just a vision.
Then it became a team.
Then a crew.
Then a family.

On Monday, we arrived on site and spent three days building this whole world from scratch. By Wednesday night, we thought we were ready to open 🚀

Then Thursday morning, the storm hit.
Within hours, most of what we had built was gone.

We had to make the hardest call: 
delay opening, and somehow rebuild everything in 24 hours.

So our crew, volunteers, artists, vendors and community stood in the rain and rebuilt it all:
the stages, the schedule, the spaces, the hope 💪🏽

Then Friday morning, the sun came out.
And at 2pm, the gates finally opened.

And what happened after that… we’ll never forget.

The hugs.
The dancing.
The kids running free.
The strangers becoming friends.

After everything, you still showed up with so much love and trust 🥹

You reminded us that MORPH was never about perfect plans.
It was always about community.

We’re still packing down, drying things out and slowly bringing this world back down to earth.

Exhausted. Emotional. SO DEEPLY GRATEFUL.

To everyone who came, helped, danced, performed, carried, cooked, cleaned and believed in this with us:

THANK YOU.

We will never forget the people who were part of the very first Morph.

This was only the beginning ✨

With so much love and gratitude,
The whole MORPH Crew ❤️

#togetherwemorph

@itsleahluna Friday night at Lunar Stage 🔥

Could not have been a more perfect fit.

After the severe weather and the decision to delay opening for safety, we had to completely rethink Friday night.

So we did something we never planned to do…

We turned Lunar Stage into our main stage.

We rigged the sound.
The lights.
The smoke.
The bubbles.

And somehow, under that giant moon in the centre, it became something even more special than we could have imagined 🥹

A fully immersive, 360 experience.
People dancing all around.
On the stage.
Around the stage.

And honestly… it made us realise something.

Maybe Lunar Stage needs to become even bigger next year 👀

What do you think- should we expand it and make it even more immersive? Comment below ❤️

@mariaotal_ceramic

El trabajo de María como ceramista está profundamente influenciado por la estética oriental y por la observación de la naturaleza. Le atraen las formas sencillas y orgánicas, las superficies serenas y los ritmos visuales creados mediante relieves repetitivos. También encuentra una importante fuente de inspiración en la pintura sumi-e, donde un gesto aparentemente simple es capaz de transmitir una gran expresividad.

Durante el festival trabajará directamente con el barro en el torno, creando piezas únicas que posteriormente decoraré cuando aún se encuentren en estado de cuero. Mediante técnicas de transferencia, pinceladas inspiradas en la caligrafía oriental y delicados bajorrelieves, irán apareciendo texturas y motivos que dialogan con la forma de cada pieza.

Su intención es mostrar al público un proceso creativo donde la espontaneidad del gesto, la huella de la mano y la belleza de la materia se unen para dar vida a una cerámica contemporánea de inspiración oriental.

Y además María es vecina de Fanzara !!!

@sr_donpez

Sr. Don Pez es el alter ego de un artista que participó en el festival de Fanzara hace unos años. El proyecto que presenta nace de un momento de crisis y bloqueo creativo. Inconscientemente inició un proceso terapéutico a través de recorridos urbanos, paseos azarosos sin objetivo concreto por la ciudad. A partir de esos recorridos , se convierte en un flaneur urbano, observando en primer término la ciudad a un nivel mas general, en su arquitectura, calles y distribución, para después fijar y concretar su mirada en las personas, las problemáticas de la ciudad y sus cambios. Sr Don Pez revierte su mirada en un proceso transformador, de intervención en las paredes, materializando una realidad urbana en piezas vegetales, que articula como jardines urbanos en las intersecciones y recovecos de las fachadas, en las grietas.

 “Empecé a caminar cuando mi cabeza se llenó de ruido. Pensaba que el ruido se calmaría pronto y volvería a trabajar en un proyecto tras otro como antes. Han pasado seis años.  Al principio iba descubriendo calles y barrios que no había visto. La ciudad en la que vivía me era desconocida. Luego miré a la gente.  me metí en los parques y empecé a mirar  la naturaleza. Sus tiempos, sus procesos , sus formas. Y empecé a reproducirla. A veces encontraba unos frutos en un árbol que un poco más pequeños me parecían ideales. Tenía que esperar un año. Entonces volvía. Conozco cada parque, cada árbol, cada jardinera que hay en mi ciudad y siempre descubro una forma nueva. Un día empecé a pegar algunas en mis paseos . Muy sutiles, casi imperceptibles. Los niños las ven, por eso las pego a su altura….”

Y dentro de pocos días un vecino más de Fanzara !!!

Maya ya ha estado con nosotros y viene ha acabar el proyecto que comenzó en 2022 , titulado ...

@interferencias_project es un proyecto multimedia procesual que aborda los distintos temas de la sociedad actual. Este proyecto se adentra en el tejido de la sociedad y apoya la interacción entre el observador y el participante, estableciendo una relación activa entre el artista y el espectador. El proyecto desarrolla cada nuevo tema a través de un enfoque integral, en el cual los ciudadanos, mediante sus declaraciones documentadas, forman el eje central del proceso. La obra se basa en la experiencia de vida genuina de cada individuo.

INTERFERENCIAS EL/LA aborda el tema de la igualdad de género contando con una importante dosis de trabajo documental. El proyecto está basado en la investigación de la legislación actual y en la cultura popular, profundamente arraigada en nuestras memorias.

Maya-Marja Janković Cvetanović es doctora en Nuevos Medios, artista multimedia y curadora. Su trayectoria profesional se sitúa en la intersección entre arte, tecnología y sociedad. En sus investigaciones artísticas explora las relaciones entre individuo y sociedad, abordando temas de memoria colectiva, identidad y transformación social.

Hola a tod@s, hoy terminamos de presentar de los invitados que nos acompañaran en esta X edición del festival @miaufanzara 2026.

Y lo hacemos de una forma muy especial, consolidando una alianza que comenzó el año pasado.

Este año, volvemos a unir fuerzas y a colaborar estrechamente con la @unrwa_es ( Agencia de Naciones Unidas para los refugiados de Palestina ). Creemos firmemente en el poder del arte urbano como herramienta de transformación, visibilidad y solidaridad.

El sábado 4 de julio tendremos un stand informativo de Unrwa en la plaza de la iglesia, será un punto de encuentro para conocer de cerca su labor humanitaria.

Además a las 11.30h tendra lugar una conferencia titulada :

"Cuando el arte ayuda a construir la paz", con la participación de @iris_serrano_ilustracion y Almuden Albert (UNRWA - Agencia de las Naciones Unidas para la población refugiada de Palestina).

En UNRWA utilizan el arte como una herramienta de educación para la ciudadanía global, la sensibilización y la promoción de los derechos humanos. No consiste únicamente en organizar actividades culturales, sino en emplear distintas expresiones artísticas para generar reflexión, diálogo y participación ciudadana en torno a la situación de la población refugiada de Palestina.

Ofrecen materiales didácticos que combinan metodologías artísticas con actividades pedagógicas, como guías para trabajar la paz en el aula, muralismo, cómics, teatro, danza, música y recursos audiovisuales. Las propuestas, en su mayoría, utilizan el lenguaje artístico para acercar historias de personas refugiadas de Palestina y favorecer el diálogo con el público. 

Con este anuncio cerramos el cartel de nuestro aniversario, pese a las dificultades seguimos apostando por un proyecto vital para Fanzara.

¡Gracias a todos los artistas y colaboradores por hacerlo posible!

Nos vemos muy pronto por las calles de Fanzara.

¡No os lo perdáis!

En Fanzara, un pequeño pueblo de Castellón de apenas 300 habitantes, sus vecinos llegaron a dejar de hablarse por un proyecto de vertedero de residuos tóxicos.

El vertedero nunca se construyó… pero la división permaneció.

Hasta que alguien tuvo una idea aparentemente imposible: llenar el pueblo de arte y convertir las paredes en puntos de encuentro.

Así nació en 2014 el MIAU, Museo Inacabado de Arte Urbano. 🧱🎨

Artistas de todo el mundo comenzaron a pintar sus fachadas, pero con una condición especial: convivir con los vecinos, escuchar sus historias y dejar que esa convivencia inspirara las obras.

Hoy, más de un centenar de paredes forman un museo al aire libre con artistas como Escif, Hyuro, Sam3, Deih, Elías Taño o David de Limón.

Y lo más increíble no son solo los murales.

👵 Vecinos mayores conversando con grafiteros.
🏠 Casas abiertas a los artistas.
🤝 Un proyecto construido desde la autogestión.
🌱 Un pueblo que convirtió un conflicto en una forma de recuperar comunidad, memoria y orgullo.

El MIAU demuestra que el arte no siempre sirve para decorar. A veces también puede servir para reconstruir lo que una comunidad había perdido.
📍 Fanzara, Castellón
🎨 MIAU — Museo Inacabado de Arte Urbano

Presentamos el espacio MIAU SOCIAL, con la proyección del documental ...

“NO HABRÁ PAZ SIN LA MUJERES PALESTINAS 2014-2024”

INTRODUCCIÓN: 

El Gobierno del Principado de Asturias impulsó en 2014 la campaña No habrá sin paz sin las mujeres, cuya finalidad era recoger el testimonio de mujeres palestinas e israelís comprometidas con la paz. El documental, producido por aquel entonces por Patricia Simón y Alex Zapico, aborda la situación de las mujeres palestinas y su resistencia en medio de la ocupación y el conflicto. De la mano de sus creadores, el documental "No habrá paz sin las mujeres. Palestina" es una iniciativa que busca generar conciencia sobre la importancia de la participación femenina en la construcción de la paz. 

SINOPSIS:

Ante la prohibición de Israel a la prensa internacional de entrar a la Franja de Gaza, viajamos a Cisjordania y a Jerusalén Este para reencontrarnos con las mujeres a las que visitamos hace 10 años. A través de nuevas entrevistas, se documentan de nuevo las fórmulas que han desarrollado para sobrevivir física y psicológicamente, -indispensable para construir puentes de entendimiento- y hacerse oír entre la opinión pública internacional. 

El documental se podrá ver el viernes 3 de julio a las 22:30h en la plaza de la Iglesia y el sábado 4 de julio a las 19:00h en el edificio sociocultural.

El documental sera presentado por @loraabuaita

Lora Abuaita es doctoranda en el Programa de Doctorado “Estudios de las Mujeres, Discursos y Prácticas de Género” de la Universidad de Granada e investigadora feminista especializada en movimientos sociales en Palestina. Su tesis examina el impacto de la ONGización del movimiento de mujeres palestinas, analizando sus causas y consecuencias desde una perspectiva decolonial. Ha realizado trabajo de campo en Palestina y Jordania con organizaciones de mujeres y lideresas del movimiento feminista.

Es miembro del Movimiento de Mujeres Palestinas Alkarama.

⚡️Stage One: Alternate Channels Residency⚡️⁠
⁠
Inaugural recipient Mara Schwerdtfeger @mara.mara.mara recently completed Stage One of the Alternate Channels Residency with Brand X at the City of Sydney Creative Studios. ⁠
⁠
Alongside a choir of collaborators, Mara spent five-days at the studios exploring the early stages of her project ‘Tectonics’, a choral work that considers the tensions and resonances created by seismic energy. The team spent time in harmony, and disharmony, playing with auto-tune and vocal arrangements which were created through the mapping of the tectonic plates themselves. ⁠
⁠
The week culminated in an intimate showing as Mara presented her early-stage discoveries, laying the groundwork for Stage Two of her residency which will take place at Soft Centre @soft_centre allowing for further development and future presentation. ⁠
⁠
Collectively, the room was captivated by Mara’s fascinating work, and we can’t wait to watch ‘Tectonics’ continue to develop and evolve all the way to Stage Three of the Alternate Channels Residency which will be hosted by Performance Space @performancespace. ⁠
⁠
Collaborators:⁠
Melisa Bester @headaches.cure⁠
Sophia Carey @sofifififif⁠
Elise Nolte @elisenolte ⁠
⁠
Images by Jones King @joneskingphotography ⁠
⁠
Alternate Channels is supported by the NSW Government through @creatensw in partnership with Soft Centre, Performance Space and Brand X

We’re delighted to welcome Mara Schwerdtfeger @mara.mara.mara as the inaugural recipient of the Alternate Channels Residency.

Mara is a composer and curator, working across live performance, film, dance and exhibition contexts, she cultivates an intuitive approach to sound-making, uncovering emotional depth in the details of everyday sound.

Alternate Channels Residency is a new partnership between Brand X, SOFT CENTRE @soft_centre and Performance Space @performancespace that invests in an ambitious experimental live artwork through a multi-stage development pathway.

Mara will develop Tectonics, a new choral work that considers the tensions and resonances caused by seismic energy. Fifteen voices, one for each tectonic plate, slide through intervals and push against Auto-Tune to create constant movement and slipping harmony.

During the Brand X residency, Mara and collaborators will workshop different arrangements for using Auto-Tune in a choir setting and practise different techniques to create specific vocal effects that simulate tectonic movement.	
 
Alternate Channels is supported by the NSW Government through Create NSW, in partnership with Soft Centre, Performance Space and Brand X.

Time to Shred. @ranxogravel by @thetraka 

Some places feed the world quietly. Lleida is one of them. While the world moves toward cities, here the land still belongs to those who work it. Families who have spent generations shaping a landscape that we only have the privilege of riding through.

Ranxo isn’t an event name. It’s a 150-year-old tradition where every Carnival the people of Ponts light 70 cauldrons in the street and feed everyone who shows up. And that’s what this is named after.

The gravel here is good because the land is good. The seventh edition returns to the place that watched this event grow up, with locals who care for every detail and roads that challenge you, surprise you and leave a mark.

Fifth event of the Gravel Earth Series. Third event By The Traka. Three distances. Ponts, Lleida.

Portland Zine Symposium is less than 2 weeks away!! We are so excited to see you and share zines!!! 

PZS will take place on Saturday, November 8, and Sunday, November 9 from 11am-5pm both days. It will be held at the Smith Memorial Student Union Ballroom at Portland State University. 

The event is free, all ages, and open to the public. 
We ask that you wear a mask while at the symposium. We will have masks for free at check in as well as in tabler kits. 

NEW THIS YEAR: 
BYO Screenprinting!!!  Bring your spare t-shirts, hoodies, hankies, onesies, patches and more - we'll print an official PZS design on it! $5-10 suggested donation - NOTAFLOF <3 
Kids Room: Some fun zine-ish activities, like make a 1-page-zine! Make a button! Drawing materials! Stamps!

Quiet Room: Need a place to chill for a few? We’ll have a quiet reading room with some selections from our Zine Library available for tablers and visitors near the ballroom space. 

Rose Haven Clothing Drive: We’ll have a donation bin for Rose Haven, a day shelter and community center serving women, children and gender non-conforming folks. Please bring unopened toiletries, tents, tarps, umbrellas, hand warmers, new underwear and socks, new leggings, and other warm weather supplies.
