We all arrived here carrying a story behind us.
And it is these stories that make us different.
The stories that give shape and meaning to everything that happened.

But today, we wanted to remember four people who did something different.
Something special, unique and difficult for us to forget.

Because yes, you are all winners.
And you are all an important part of every edition.

Congratulations and thank you for your effort.
Very soon… 2027.

Next stop: @ranxogravel

For a few days, we create our own little world. ❤️

🎟️ 𝗣𝗿𝗲-𝘀𝗮𝗹𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗰𝗹𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝟵𝗽𝗺 𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁!

Who's joining us in 2027? 🧚

This has exceeded all our expectations.
Years ago, when we decided to create this monster, we could never have imagined getting this far.

Today, we say goodbye with the most special edition we’ve ever created.
5,000 riders. 15,000 supporters. 450 staff members.
But numbers have never been our thing.

What truly matters to us is the blood, the heart, and the people.
Because behind every person, there’s a story.
And this Traka is the one that has given us the most positive stories we’ve ever experienced.

So, thank you. Thank you to everyone who made this possible.
We feel lucky to be able to work for all of you.

You made history.

⸻

Això ha superat totes les nostres expectatives.
Fa anys, quan vam decidir crear aquest monstre, mai hauríem imaginat arribar fins aquí.

Avui ens acomiadem amb l’edició més especial que hem fet mai.
5.000 participants. 15.000 acompanyants. 450 persones d’staff.
Però les dades mai han sigut lo nostre.

Lo nostre sempre ha sigut la sang, el cor i les persones.
Perquè darrere de cada persona hi ha una història.
I aquesta Traka és la que més històries positives ens ha regalat mai.

Així que, thank you i gràcies a tots els que ho heu fet possible.
Ens sentim afortunats de poder treballar per tots vosaltres.

Heu fet història.

🎶 The program is here! 🎶

We’re getting very close to a pretty special Sunday — and now you can start planning your day at The Channon Craft Market’s 50th Celebrations.

From our Welcome to Country and Smoking Ceremony with Uncle Gilbert through to live music, stories, official speeches and a few familiar faces, we’ve got plenty happening throughout the day.

On the program you’ll find Lismore Flood Water Revival, Kevin Newton, Michelle Bell, Tobi and Friends, Monkey and the Fish and Luke Vassella.

And there’s more happening around the Market too: including the Chai Tent, decorations by Benny Zable, the Bubble Girls and RiverFest BioBlitz activities.

📅 Sunday 11 October 
📍 The Channon Craft Market, The Channon

Have a look through the program, pick out what you don’t want to miss, and come spend part (or all)of this very special market day with us.

And when the Market day wraps up, the celebrations don’t have to! You can keep the evening going at the Chai Tent and Drumming Circle, or if that’s more your style, head on down to The Channon Tavern and settle in for the rest of the evening.

50 years of people, art, music, craft and community. We reckon that’s worth celebrating. ❤️

Proudly supported by Lismore City Council.

#TheChannonCraftMarket #TheChannon #50Years #VisitLismore #NorthernRivers #MakeItBakeItGrowIt

🎪 **STALLHOLDERS — COME BE PART OF OUR 50TH!** 🎪

On Sunday 11 October, The Channon Craft Market turns **50**, and we want to fill the Market with an incredible mix of makers, bakers, growers, artists and creators to help us celebrate.

**New stallholders. Current stallholders. Past stallholders. We want you here.**

If you've always thought about having a stall at The Channon, this is a pretty special Market to make your first.

If you've been part of the Market before, we'd love to welcome you back.

And if you've moved on to other things but still have some of your old creations tucked away in storage... dust them off! This could be the perfect excuse for one more Market day under the trees.

For 50 years, the stalls and the people behind them have made The Channon Craft Market what it is. Now we're bringing everyone together to celebrate where we've come from — and what's still to come.

📅 **Sunday 11 October 2026** 
⏰ **9am–3pm** 
📍 **The Channon**

 Join us on June 11 for a hybrid lecture, listening session, and production-demonstration workshop tracing Budots from its roots in Davao City to its evolving life as a hyperlocal, internet-native, and globally resonant electronic music form.  Led by @djlove_sherwintuna, one of the pioneering figures behind Budots and co-founder of the Camusboyz Budots dance group, the first chapter of the workshop grounds participants in the genre’s lived history: its movement culture, community context, early circulation, sonic markers, and production language. The second chapter, led by @obese.dogma777 extends Budots into the idea of Post-Budots: a framework for respectfully mutating, reimagining, and evolving hyperlocal club forms.   The session will focus on demonstration and shared listening. Participants receive a Budots sample pack / resource kit after the session to continue experimenting independently. Open to researchers, curators, club music fans, and anyone interested in Southeast Asian electronic music, Filipino music, internet culture, regional genres, and experimental dance music. No advanced production experience required.

@asemnavarro

ASEM Navarro es un artista urbano de Madrid, que combina su destreza como escritor de Graffiti con su carrera como ilustrador, buscando una confluencia entre la audacia del arte callejero y el encanto del arte académico, creando trabajos llenos de energía que transmiten personalidad y emoción.

Activo en el Graffiti desde finales de los 90, su arte ha evolucionado constantemente a través del estudio del arte, sin perder la esencia de sus orígenes, trabajando su singular estilo urbano. Su evolución ha sido autodidacta, dibujando siempre en su cuaderno, hasta que en 2020 se graduó en la escuela de arte Artediez, donde desarrolló sus conocimientos y técnicas artísticas en un entorno más profesional.

La diversidad e intensidad de la ciudad han influido en todas sus obras, impregnando de carácter cada trazo, creando una revelación mágica y poderosa, una sinergia de estilo urbano y visión reflexiva, llena de simbolismo e impacto.

@soen_bravo

César de Fernando Bravo, alias SOEN BRAVO, nació en Madrid en 1987.

A partir del año 2000 comienza a pintar graffiti, el cual le proporciona experiencia en la técnica de la pintura spray y amplía el campo de la creación artística. Sus estudios artísticos formales son sus dos años de Bachillerato Artístico en la Escuela de Arte número 3 de Madrid.

Desde entonces, son numerosos los trabajos artísticos que ha hecho de pequeño y gran formato, en Madrid, resto de España y otros países.

Paralelamente, ha desarrollando un estilo personal de pintura caracterizado por la mezcla de la descomposición de elementos figurativos, con formas y letras superpuestas de su estilo de graffiti, uniendo todo esto con formas inacabadas y algunas pinceladas desenfadadas.

Cesar se considera versátil en cuanto a las temáticas de sus obras. En algunas, pretende transmitir un mensaje de denuncia social, política y económica tratando de crear un debate entre lo legal y lo moral. En otras, ciertos rasgos de ternura, por vivencias personales e, incluso, toca temas de carácter histórico y costumbrista.

@victorpuchalski

Víctor Puchalski (Catarroja, 1986) desarrolla sus primeros trabajos dentro de la autoedición y la escena independiente del cómic, participando en publicaciones colectivas y construyendo un imaginario propio entre el fanzine y la novela gráfica. En esta etapa crea a KANN, personaje central de buena parte de su obra y protagonista de Enter the Kann (2016). 

Un año más tarde publica La balada de Jolene Blackcountry, consolidando una línea narrativa marcada por la estética oscura, el western, el manga y el simbolismo, que culmina en KNEEL!!, su última obra publicada hasta la fecha.
Con el paso de los años, su interés creativo se desplaza progresivamente del papel al muro.

Retoma entonces la pintura y comienza a trabajar en producciones de gran formato como asistente de producción junto a Lluïsa Penella i Pons, iniciando una nueva etapa centrada en la pintura mural y la relación entre imagen, arquitectura y espacio público.

@dantearcade

Dante Arcade es un artista visual español afincado en Barcelona, cuya práctica se origina en la cultura del graffiti de los años noventa, desarrollada inicialmente de forma autodidacta, y evoluciona hacia un lenguaje contemporáneo vinculado al glitch, el retrofuturismo y la memoria digital. Su obra investiga la intersección entre cultura pop, tecnología, nostalgia y consumo, articulando un universo visual que conecta el imaginario arcade con la sociedad hiperconectada actual. Mediante el uso del error digital, la pixelación, los códigos de internet y la fragmentación visual, desarrolla una poética crítica en torno a la falibilidad de la memoria contemporánea, la obsolescencia de los medios y la experiencia del realismo en entornos cibernéticos.

Su trabajo dialoga con subculturas retro y vintage, el cómic, los videojuegos y la estética vectorial de los años noventa, reinterpretados desde una perspectiva post-internet y desde una investigación sostenida sobre los lenguajes visuales de la era digital. Especializado en murales de gran formato y en la producción de obra de estudio, produce piezas con una sólida calidad objetual y conceptual. Su práctica híbrida transita entre el espacio público y el espacio expositivo, generando narrativas simbólicas y alegóricas que exploran las relaciones entre individuos, comunidades, memoria y sistemas tecnológicos.
 
Nacido en el Mar Menor (Murcia) y residente en Barcelona, inició su trayectoria influenciado por la cultura urbana, el rap y el skate, integrando desde sus inicios el imaginario de la ciencia ficción, el cómic y el graffiti. Desde entonces, su obra se configura como un proceso continuo de arqueología visual, donde lo clásico y lo futurista, lo analógico y lo digital, coexisten en tensión crítica. Ha participado en proyectos y exposiciones en Europa y América, colaborando con instituciones culturales y marcas globales. Actualmente desarrolla nuevas series para galerías, proyectos curatoriales y programas de arte público a escala internacional.

@taqi_spateen 

Taqi Spateen es un artista y muralista palestino contemporáneo que integra con fluidez las bellas artes y la cultura urbana global. Graduado en Bellas Artes por la Academia Internacional de Arte (IAA) de Ramallah, Palestina. Taqi comenzó a pintar en segundo grado. Al finalizar sus estudios secundarios, ya realizaba encargos y murales en las paredes de la escuela y otros espacios públicos. Esto lo impulsó a solicitar el ingreso a la Licenciatura en Bellas Artes en la IAA de Ramallah. Tras completar sus estudios, compitió con reconocidos contratistas internacionales y ganó una licitación arquitectónica para la renovación de un antiguo palacio.
Su trabajo abarca desde murales públicos de gran escala —notablemente en el muro de separación de Cisjordania— hasta pinturas de paisajes realistas y altamente reflectivas, en las que explora temas como la memoria, el medio ambiente y la resistencia cultural.
El trabajo de Taqi continúa llegando a audiencias internacionales y ha aparecido en medios de comunicación locales, regionales y globales. Taqi fue invitado a colaborar con la marca "The North Face" y creó un mural como parte de la campaña " Walls are made for climbing" (Los muros están hechos para escalar ). También fue finalista en el concurso internacional "UN Sustainable Development Goals (ODS) Global Festival of Action" (Festival Mundial de Acción) por su mural centrado en el Objetivo de Desarrollo Estratégico 16 de la ONU, que promueve la justicia. A finales de 2021, Taqi fue invitado por el alcalde de la ciudad de Cergy/Ville de Cergy en Francia a formar parte de una residencia artística con Art Osons, donde también creó un mural durante el festival de arte callejero "CAPS" en Cergy.
Taqi también fue seleccionado por un comité para recibir una beca y participar en un programa de residencia artística de cuatro meses que finalizó a finales de febrero de 2022 en la Cité Internationale des Arts de París , Francia.

RAINBOW SPIRIT FESTIVAL! 🌈 

It’s taken me time to unwind and reflect on months of work behind the scenes to deliver what was a very successful return for Rainbow.

Moving sites along with 7 years of heartache was not easy as we continue to hopefully end up back at our spiritual home one day at Lexton, but I’ve been saying that any Rainbow is better than no Rainbow. People were worried we wouldn’t be able to recreate the magic of Lexton and although Lexton holds a very special place in our hearts, I could feel the magic of Rainbow as soon as everyone arrived. Having the band back together in any kind of Rainbow format outdoors was always going to be special and it was a very magical weekend. 

The music was absolutely top notch all weekend on all 3 stages from the get go and I’d like to take the time to thank our curation team Corey, Ozzy and I couldn’t be any prouder myself having the opportunity to curate the Horizon stage. I’ve only ever wanted what’s best for Rainbow and everyone that knows me knows I’m a pioneer for pushing the Aussie scene first and foremost. Being tasked with this was a lot of pressure and expectation after such a hiatus but everyone brought their A game and I cant thank you all enough. 

This is why we do what we do and I cant wait for the next one. 

No Doofsticks, no phones, no egos, no bullshit, amazing crowd and going back to our roots feels the most organic and best way forward and we will continue on this path as we grow again. 

Special thanks to all the team, Frank, Loretta, Thad, Danielle, Timmy and Marty and all the rest of the crew that put your blood sweat and tears into this to make it the best event possible. You all know who you are. 

My full set will be available soon

I hope you enjoyed the return of the big dance as much as we enjoyed putting it together.

Till the next one

Love,
Kasey ❤️

We’ve commissioned a new short film by the terminally online Sydney via Saigon via Melbourne visual artist, VJ, director and animator Passive Kneeling alongside a curated program of shorts from near and far for the @sydneyoperahouse 

A fixture of Australia’s underground music scene and a familiar face at Soft Centre, Passive Kneeling has built dystopian yet hypnotic visual worlds for the live shows of Bag Raiders, Roza Terenzi, Ninajirachi and many more. Echo Sleep marks a new chapter: a film exploring the loss of consent in the media we absorb every day and the subtle neurological rewiring inflicted by algorthimically fed content. Built through 3D environments, TouchDesigner and creative coding, it follows the repetition of daily routine as it gradually slips into imagined spaces formed out of boredom and mental drift. The surrounding program asks what it feels like to be a body inside the current media moment — neural media, memetic warfare, the infinite scroll as an opening into treacherous new psychocosms 🧠

Join us for a night of schizzo, deep-fried, high-stim new media art at the Playhouse Theatre on May 28th for @vividsydney

SOFT CENTRE is evolving 🌬️

Today, we’re excited to publicly announce our transition to a 𝗡𝗼𝘁-𝗙𝗼𝗿-𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁. This new entity will power our year-round programs, interdisciplinary commissions, international collaborations, and annual festival in Sydney/Eora. Y comenzamos con los artistas muralistas :

@alexsenna 

ALEX SENNA  Orlândia,  Sao Paulo ( Brasil )

Nacido en Orlândia, Alex Senna es un artista callejero brasileño que plasma vívidamente el amor, el romance y las relaciones humanas a través de ilustraciones juveniles en blanco y negro. Combinando el lenguaje de la ilustración, el cómic y el grafiti de los años noventa, Alex construye una narrativa lúdica, casi poética, que confiere a sus obras un gran atractivo popular.

Sus murales, que observan las relaciones humanas cargadas de carga emocional y entrelazadas con la sátira, han dado en los últimos años un aspecto caricaturesco a las calles de São Paulo ( y muchas otras). Utilizando símbolos extraídos de la imaginación infantil —corazones, notas musicales, globos, pájaros— Alex añade «color» a su arte, que es marcadamente incoloro.

Daltónico, Alex empleó un solo color en sus dibujos y cuadernos de bocetos, que posteriormente plasmaron en los muros de las ciudades, dejando una huella visual sencilla y vívida.

Al trasladar sus bocetos a las paredes de ciudades de todo el mundo, infunde en los entornos urbanos sentimientos de amor y felicidad, exponiendo al espectador a la vida íntima de sus personajes. Los tonos en blanco y negro de su arte transmiten sus mensajes de forma sencilla, clara y sincera.

Con exposiciones individuales en São Paulo, Londres, Chicago, Turín, Taipéi y Seúl, y su participación en exposiciones colectivas en todo el mundo, Alex Senna ha alcanzado el reconocimiento internacional.

Wellfest. WOWfest.

Someone came up to us after this dance and said they felt healed.

After one dance.

Healing doesn’t always have to be heavy.
Sometimes healing happens on the dance floor.

In a room full of strangers and friends.
Bare feet on the earth.
Bodies moving to the beat.

When we drop out of our heads and into our bodies…
something shifts.

We move.
We breathe.
We let the music move through us.

The creative pulse.
Shakti.
Life force.

After this particular dance at @wellfestnz a woman shared that when @sarah.menlove guided everyone to drop awareness down to the base of the spine, she felt a huge energetic blockage release in her lower body.

Our bodies hold so much.

Tension. 
Old stories. 
Limiting beliefs.

And sometimes when we surrender to the rhythm and let the body lead…those patterns begin to soften.

New movement.
New space.
New pathways.

Healing doesn’t always look like sitting in a therapy room.
Sometimes it looks like dancing. ✨

David Moreno Terrón: escultura y renovación fallera

David Moreno es un escultor valenciano con una práctica artística diversa, aunque la mayor parte de su carrera ha girado en torno a la construcción de fallas. Entre sus trabajos destacan dos de las comisiones más emblemáticas de Valencia: Convento Jerusalén y Nou Campanar.

En 2011 creó "Proyecte Ences" con el objetivo de impulsar un lenguaje estético diferente dentro de la tradición fallera. La iniciativa reúne exposiciones, intervenciones artísticas y espacios de debate que conectan las Fallas con el arte contemporáneo.

El giro experimental en su trayectoria llegó en 2013 con "Se está librando una batalla aunque no lo sepas", su primera falla grande realizada junto a Miguel Arraiz. Ese proyecto marcó el inicio de una línea de trabajo más innovadora que continuó en 2015 con "Ekklesia", levantada para Pediatra Jorge Comin - Serra Calderona bajo el colectivo "Pink Intruder". El impacto de la obra traspasó fronteras y llevó a los organizadores de Burning Man a proponerles una colaboración. Así nació "Renaiximent" (2016), una pieza instalada en el desierto de Nevada y posteriormente montada en el Centro del Carmen de Valencia antes de su cremá en 2017. Todo el proceso quedó documentado en "I’m burning", de Andreu Signes.
Su actividad se ha extendido más allá de las Fallas: ha participado en MIAU Fanzara, FITUR, la Capitalidad Mundial de la Alimentación Sostenible 2017, el Fuorisalone de la Semana del Diseño de Milán y ha vuelto a Burning Man en 2022.

David Moreno está considerado una de las figuras clave en la transformación de las Fallas infantiles. Su estilo rompe con la estética tradicional, poniendo el acento en la escultura, el equilibrio compositivo y el valor del vacío. Sus obras tienen un registro poético y conceptual, con una lectura abierta que apela sobre todo a una sensibilidad joven y creativa.

Y la siguiente artista invitada es....

AMANDA AURRO-TEA @mandioh

Amanda Arrou-tea es una artista donostiarra. Se graduó en Bellas Artes por la Universidad del País Vasco en 2013. En 2015 cursó un máster en Gestión Cultural en la Universidad Modelo de México y en 2016 completó un máster en Gestión de Galerías en la Universidad de Barcelona. 

Su trayectoria dio un giro en México, donde descubrió su pasión por el mar y las sirenas, convirtiéndolas en su lenguaje personal. Posteriormente se mudo a Berlín, donde a lo largo de 8 años se introdujo de lleno en el mundo del Street Art, aprendiendo de los artistas más reconocidos a nivel mundial.

Amanda se dedica al muralismo y la pintura. Con sus pinturas e ilustraciones fotorrealistas, crea mundos maravillosos sobre diferentes superficies. Ha participado en numerosas exposiciones internacionales, donde colabora en diversos proyectos artísticos y culturales.

Amanda crea su obra de estudio en Valencia donde reside actualmente, la cual se expone en galerías y ferias de EEUU, Europa y México. Como muralista, compagina encargos con su proyecto «Mermaids», viajando por numerosos países para ilustrar paredes mientras educa sobre feminismo y cambio climático.

Amanda transforma espacios y conciencias a traves del arte, arte con conciencia ambiental y perspectiva de género.

Our values guide how Rainbow Spirit is created and experienced - from site design and programming to how we care for one another on and off the dancefloor. They reflect the culture built over decades and the shared responsibility that makes this gathering possible.

Behaviour that makes others feel unsafe, unwelcome or disrespected has no place at Rainbow. We each carry responsibility for how we show up, helping create a festival that feels open, inclusive and safe for all.

We are so excited to have these wonderful artists and performers joining us this weekend:

✨The Amber Temple is an original music and contemporary dance collaboration between singer-songwriter Julian Temple and contemporary dancer Amber Gabrielle Stephens. Using theatrical elements, costume and face paint, they create an immersive and visceral environment. A powerful duo articulating beautiful and strange vignettes in harmony and synchronicity.

✨CATA – Patagonian-born musician who has spent five years traveling through Mexico, the U.S., Australia and New Zealand. Creating acoustic psychedelic medicine music rooted in tribal traditions and vibrational healing. An intimate, sensual and honest inward journey.

✨Fiordland – Originating from South East England and now based in New Zealand’s South Island, a devotee of deep electronica blending global influences. 2024 marked a breakout year with releases on Seven Villas Music, Nordic Voyage and Krafted Records.

✨Taylor Blaze (Victoria Balsamo) – Artist, dancer and performer from Uruguay, now based in NZ. Passionate about expression, heels dance and aerials.

✨Mik Dass – Downtempo rhythms woven with the teachings of Ram Dass to create a meditative dance floor inviting presence and embodiment.

✨Dorothy Ella – UK singer-songwriter blending disco-soul sparkle with funk-pop roots. Acoustic sets filled with positivity, warmth and healing energy.

✨Anna Y Diego – A feel-good duo reworking classic pop through live grooves and real-time loops.

✨Uplift – Inspired to create music for the mind and soul. Roots, soul and positive vibes.

✨Gambo – New York drummer-turned-DJ mixing funky, percussive grooves since 2020.

✨Abigail ROSE – Trained in multiple circus disciplines in NZ. Performing on corde lisse, trapeze and more with beauty and strength.

✨Custom Cuts – Electronic music journey from Auckland through Copenhagen and London, now returning to Queenstown with eclectic trance and techno influences.

✨Sangita Ōtepoti – Offering Kirtan in Dunedin for 4 years. Lovers of devotional song, voice and instruments supporting collective practice.

So much talent coming together beside the river 🌿✨

Oh, let me tell you a story…

Once upon a time, in a little village called The Channon, there lived a market nearly 50 years young.

It was not a fancy market with polished floors and a roof over its head. This old market lived on an oval, under the trees, with music in the air, baskets on arms, muddy boots when needed, and real people making, baking and growing real things.

But every good fable needs a character who causes trouble.

In this story, that character is the weather.

The weather has been very busy lately. It has rained and rained, then rained a little more, until the oval pulled its green blanket around itself and said, “I am still a bit soggy, thank you very much.”

So the Market team looked at the sky.
They looked at the ground.
They looked at the forecast.
Then they looked back at the ground, because the ground is very honest about these things.

And they said, “We have seen miracles before.”

Nearly 50 years teaches a market patience. A wet week can turn into a dry morning. Wind and sunshine can do their work. You learn not to give up too early, but also not to ignore what the oval is telling you.

So for now, The Channon Craft Market is still planned for this weekend.

The baskets may yet swing.
The coffee may yet pour.
The makers, bakers and growers may yet gather under the trees.

But the oval has not given its final answer.

So the moral of the story is this:

Plan to come and play in The Channon.

Keep your Sunday basket handy, keep one eye on our updates, and be ready for a relaxed market morning if the weather behaves itself.

And if the rain wins this chapter?

Then perhaps the old market spirit is simply giving you permission to stay snuggled in bed, make another coffee, and let Sunday be soft.

We will keep watching and share any changes here as soon as we know more.

A warning for travellers from Nimbin…

If you are making your way to The Channon Craft Market tomorrow, take heed.

Tuntable Creek Road is closed to through traffic due to the landslip, and Council is asking people to use the signed Pinchin Road detour.

We know there are rumours of other little roads and clever back ways around the closure, but they are not recommended. Some are not suitable for the size of traffic coming to the Market, and with the recent wet weather, road conditions may not be ideal.

So for this journey, please follow the proper route.

From Nimbin, travel south along Nimbin Road, through Coffee Camp and Koonorigan, and continue towards Goolmangar. From there, follow the signed detour onto Pinchin Road and into The Channon.

Allow extra time. Follow the detour signs. Obey the revised speed limits. Check Live Traffic before you leave. And do not trust the little glowing rectangle in your hand if it tries to send you somewhere heroic.

For those coming from other directions, access to The Channon is as normal, but there are roadworks about, so please drive to the conditions and take your time.

Wondering if any of it makes a difference,

And yet the theme of this dance came through @iamlilieve and I ... 
Creative Pulse ✨

A journey to remember that we must continue to create,

Especially when we meet the stories and the doubts, 

Especially when we don't fully know the next step,

Especially when we wonder if any of it matters,

And in these times of uncertainty to remember that we are doing it together.

Something I've been wanting to create for a long time now is a space for women to gather, to move and breathe and remember together, 

So you too can continue to create your life from your Wild Truth 🪶

This something is currently Wild Devotion,

A 6 month journey for women who want to move from deeper embodiment and authentic expression, combining Ceremony and Somatics to welcome the fullness of you,

Where all emotions and expressions have a space, 

Where you can put down the doing and allow yourself to be held,

As you feel and breathe and move and welcome yourself home.

How this will ripple out into your life will be unique to you and the themes you are journeying with over these 6 months, but I know the ripple will be felt.

These experiences touch us on levels deeper than our minds can comprehend.

This is an invitation to join us for Wild Devotion ~ 6 months dedicated to the wildness of YOU

Avui us presentem en Xavi Segura, de @tempsdemeteo , el nostre meteoròleg oficial. Cada dia ens farà arribar la previsió meteorològica actualitzada per seguir de prop com evolucionarà el temps a The Traka 2026.

Aquí us deixem una primera previsió, i a partir de demà a la tarda publicarem cada dia un Instagram Stories amb més detall sobre el temps i les temperatures que tindrem al llarg d’aquest cap de setmana llarg.

Today, while riding the roads of The Traka, we met a local legend.

He didn’t have a race number, but he left us with something more important: a thought that stays with you.

“Experience teaches as much as university.”

And that’s everything.

Because The Traka is not just about the strongest.
It’s about what you live when time passes, when your body speaks and you decide to keep going—sharing the road and facing the unexpected for hours.

We know many of you are ready to be at the front.

Here are some of the favorites, without a doubt, backed by experience.

We’re still dancing in our minds. ✨🌙

As the sun set, the whole landscape of Wellfest transformed.

The trees and earth began to glow.Fires were lit.Costumes got wilder.The music turned up just a little louder… and the dancing never stopped.

The Magic Nursery became a glowing beacon in the night — alive with interactive music games, UV painting, and co-created DJ sets that blurred the line between artist and audience.The late-night rave cave pulsed underground.Fire spinners lit up the darkness.Performers moved like living art against the flames.

Around the fires, smaller circles gathered — singing, drumming, sharing stories, locking eyes in conversations that felt timeless.The saunas carried on into the night, heat and laughter spilling out under the stars.

It was the kind of place where time dissolved.Where you were so deep in connection, rhythm, and presence that you didn’t even think to check the hour…Until you finally glanced at your watch and realised it was 3am.

Wellfest by night was wild and tender all at once.Electric. Elemental. Unforgettable.

caption:
There was something about Wellfest by day that’s hard to put into words… but we’ll try. ✨

First and foremost — it was the human connection.
People arrived exactly as they were. No masks. No performances. Just open hearts.
There was that feeling of being seen, heard, and loved in your wholeness — and offering that same presence to someone else.

By day, Wellfest felt expansive.
The workshops inspired growth, stretched minds, and opened up new perspectives across a wide range of beautiful modalities.

There was yoga beneath open skies.
Breathwork that moved emotion through the body.
Sauna sessions that grounded and reset.
Dance that shook us free.
Singing that opened hearts.
Fire circles that drew us closer.
Bare feet on the earth.
Art unfolding in real time.
Moments of co-creation that reminded us we’re not meant to do this alone.

It was nature. It was the elements. It was depth and play woven together.

There was a special energy in the air all day — something alive, intentional, and deeply human.
A kind of magic that couldn’t quite be matched… only experienced.

💵✨ It’s Market Week at The Channon!

This Sunday the 12th, Coronation Park will once again come alive with handmade creations, delicious food, and that one-of-a-kind Channon community vibe.

💵🌿 49 Years of Cash at The Channon Craft Market 🌿💵

For 49 years, cash has been the lifeblood of The Channon Craft Market. Long before Wi-Fi signals, QR codes, and “tap and go,” our community has been swapping coins and notes for art, food, music, and memories. And guess what? We don’t plan on giving it up anytime soon. ✌️

Here’s why:
✨ Cash is freedom – no machines telling you “transaction declined” because the valley swallowed the signal.
✨ Cash is fair – no banks clipping a fee off your $6 macramé keyring. The whole lot goes straight to the maker.
✨ Cash is tradition – this is a cottage industry market, built on face-to-face exchanges and grassroots creativity.

Of course, many of our stallholders now have EFTPOS too — but cash keeps everyone included and everything flowing the way it has for nearly five decades.

Practical reminders:
👉 Two ATMs on site, but queues can be long.
👉 Car parking is $3 cash only.
👉 Stallholders – don’t forget to bring cash for stall fees.

Bring some notes, some coins, and a smile — and help us keep 49 years of market spirit alive. 🌻🛍️🎶

This morning, the official program of The Traka began.

Thank you all for being here.

See you out there.

That’s how Peggy Byrne describes Bowerbird Market;  South Australia’s original design market and one of the few places where you don’t just buy something… you meet the person who made it.

Bowerbird has been running for 15 years, built on one idea:
handmade over mass-made.
Pieces with a story. Makers who talk to you, not at you. Gifts that don’t come in the millions.

“Every item is made with love — and you can really hear it in the story behind it.”

This weekend brings:
✨ 100+ designers

A edição de 2026 da Feira Miolo(s) traz uma novidade. Neste ano, pela primeira vez, a feira contou com um curador convidado, o pesquisador e artista visual cearense Weaver Lima.

Atuante no meio artístico independente desde a década de 1990, Weaver editou zines de quadrinhos e arte-xerox com o grupo Seres Urbanos. Em 2015, uma seleção de trabalhos do grupo foi reunida no livro “Seres Urbanos - Antologia do Quadrinho Underground Cearense” que ganhou o Prêmio Miolo(s), na categoria HQ, daquele mesmo ano.

No início dos anos 2000, enveredou pelas artes visuais com trabalhos que traziam fortes influências das HQs underground e da contracultura. Foi premiado em salões oficiais de arte e realizou exposições individuais em centros culturais do Brasil, Portugal e Itália. Em 2008, Weaver criou o coletivo MONSTRA com o qual realizou diversas exposições e intervenções urbanas. Como curador, produziu numerosas mostras, entre as quais se destacam as realizadas com o coletivo Monstra, Luiz Sá 100 anos, Desenhomatic LTDA - Jaca e Fabio Zimbres, Arquivo Nirez, O Ordinário Rafael Sica e Subsequência.

Em 2021, desenvolveu uma pesquisa que resultou no documentário Ceará Marginal, que apresenta um recorte de 50 anos da produção gráfica independente cearense (1970-2020). Atualmente, dirige a produtora cultural MONSTRA, com a qual realiza projetos com foco em arte independente.

O convite para Weaver realizar a curadoria reforça o compromisso da Miolo(s) de compor, a cada ano, uma pluralidade de vozes a partir de uma visão descentralizada da produção gráfica latina. Após discussões realizadas com o intuito de se deter com profundidade nos projetos inscritos e diálogos onde não faltaram escolhas difíceis, Weaver chegou à lista final de participantes da edição de 2026 do evento – seleção que pode ser conferida no site oficial (link na bio @feiramiolos). 

Obrigada, Weaver!

Anote na agenda: em 2026, a Feira Miolo(s) acontece nos dias 7 e 8 de novembro!

A décima terceira edição reunirá, mais uma vez, editoras independentes, artistas gráficos, ateliês de impressão e livrarias de rua. Nas próximas semanas, mais novidades sobre as inscrições.

A Miolo(s) é um encontro de cultura gráfica promovido desde 2014 pela Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) e pela editora Lote 42 (@lote42).

#feiramiolos #bibliotecamariodeandrade #lote42

Uma das novidades da 12ª Feira Miolo(s) foi a presença de ateliês de impressão entre os expositores! Consideramos esses espaços fundamentais para a preservação e ventilação de ideias impressas, mantendo vivas as técnicas artesanais e recuperando tecnologias ancestrais frente aos desafios da contemporaneidade.

Nas fotos da Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias) você vê como estavam bonitas as mesas dessa turma durante o evento na Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade)! 

#feiramiolos #miolos #esquentamiolos #lote42 #ateliesdeimpressao

Este ano, a Feira Miolo(s) contou com 241 lançamentos, entre livros, zines, gravuras, livros de artista e fotolivros, todos dos muitos artistas, coletivos, ateliês, editoras e livrarias que ocuparam os espaços da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) – deste número, uma parte compôs a já tradicional mostra de lançamentos no Corredor de Vidro da biblioteca! 

Foram cerca de 80 publicações, todas identificadas com a autoria e o local onde o público podia conhecer melhor aquele trabalho. A realização da mostra também faz lembrar um dos aspectos mais importantes do evento, que é a integração de novas peças para o acervo da instituição: a única contrapartida de participação é a doação, e assim ajudamos a biblioteca a crescer e os trabalhos a circular ✨

As fotos são da Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias) 

#feiramiolos #miolos #bibliotecamariodeandrade #mostra #lançamentos

A Feira Miolo(s) é sobre publicações. Obras literárias, gravuras, prints, zines, livros-objeto, fotolivros, livros de artista e todas essas coisas. Todas essas coisas que são feitas por pessoas. A Feira Miolo(s), então, é sobre pessoas. Por isso, não tem jeito melhor de encerrar a divulgação dos registros da 12ª edição do que com um salve a todas as pessoas que fazem a Miolo(s) acontecer. Fazem a Miolo(s) ser a Miolo(s). Equipes da editora Lote 42 (@lote42) e da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) combinadas com o intuito de promover o melhor evento possível para todo mundo que visita, todo mundo que expõe, sejam os frequentadores das antigas, seja quem está caindo de paraquedas – o trabalho incansável de promover grandes movimentações com a leveza de quem vira uma página. 

Obrigada pessoal! Em 2026 tem mais! 

(ps: faltaram as fotos do Murilo Vieira e Meire Vilas Boas, que estavam sempre em movimento, e da própria Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias), responsável pelo belo registro!)

Em 2025, a Miolo(s) contou com uma estação de serigrafia ao longo dos dois dias de evento. Quem tocou essas impressões foi a Sutto Serigrafia (@suttoserigrafia_caixaseideias), com sua equipe incansável. 

Quem chegasse na Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade), podia fazer uma impressão em serigrafia com a identidade da feira e também com telas dos próprios artistas expositores. 

Aliás, foi a Sutto quem fez a impressão sobre as sacolas que foram entregues aos expositores. A ação foi uma maneira de aprofundar a relação da Miolo(s) com as técnicas artesanais, os ateliês de impressão e o pensamento manual ✨

As fotos são da Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias).

Uma novidade especial da 12ª Feira Miolo(s) foi a gravação ao vivo do Papo Tatuí, podcast sobre cultura gráfica independente da Sala Tatuí (@salatatui), no Auditório da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) 🎙️✨ Foram três mesas por dia, todas mediadas por João Varella (@joaovarella) e com dois convidados atuantes no mundo da cultura gráfica alternativa do Brasil. Dá só uma olhada em quem participou:

Ricardo Rodrigues (Experimentos Impressos - Canoas) [@experimentosimpressos] e Rosinha Disgrassa (Edições Tocaia - Belo Horizonte) [@edicoes.tocaia]

Marceli Mengarda (Burocrata Carimbos - Florianópolis) [@mmengarda] e Pri Ballarin (Lisboa) [@pri_ballarin]

Adriano Melo (La Idea - Belo Horizonte) [@cyco.idea]
Kaetérine Terra (Fudida Silk - Rio de Janeiro) [@fudidasilk]

Buggy (Ateliê de Impressos - Fortaleza) [@buggy_tiposdoacaso] e Tina Merz (Casa Cleber Teixeira, Noa Noa - Florianópolis) [@tinamerz]

Flávia Bomfim (Movimento Contínuo - Salvador) [@flavia_bom_fim] e Thiago Tizzot (Arte&Letra - Curitiba) [@ttizzot]

Charles Zipi (Adaga Verde - Rio de Janeiro) [@adaga.verde] e Tui Boaventura (Bonito, MS) [@tui_boaventura]

Pelas fotos da Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias) dá pra sentir como estava o clima desses papos e fique de olho nas redes da Miolo(s) (@feiramiolos) e da Sala Tatuí (@salatatui) que em breve os episódios vão entrar no ar! Aliás, já começa a seguir o Papo Tatuí na sua plataforma de podcast preferida.

#feiramiolos #miolos #bibliotecamariodeandrade #podcast #papotatui

Quem passou pela Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) durante a 12ª edição da Feira Miolo(s) e nos dias que a sucederam pôde conhecer de perto, ali no Corredor de Vidro, uma parte muito especial do acervo da instituição. Com curadoria de Gustavo Piqueira, (@gustavopiqueira), a mostra “100 EM 10: ARTE IMPRESSA NO ACERVO DA BIBLIOTECA MÁRIO DE ANDRADE” pinçou dez publicações históricas, vinculadas ao pensamento da publicação independente, para esboçar uma espécie de “árvore genealógica” do trabalho dos expositores da feira e também reforçar, no ano em que a biblioteca completa um século, sua vocação para abrigar obras transgressoras, imaginativas – sempre novas. 

As fotos do post são de Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias)

...

10 days to go for THE TRAKA

The Traka 100
Aquí no va de quant recorres, sinó de com el recorres.

Quan estiguis al quilòmetre 70, rebentat, recorda’t dels que han triat la 200 o la 360. Potser això et dona un punt més.

Però no subestimis The Traka 100. Són 100 quilòmetres per viure-ho tot, dels que es llegeixen i es senten: muntanya, plans, singletracks i terreny canviant al voltant de Girona. En un matí, recorres una síntesi real del territori.

És la distància més curta, sí, però no la més fàcil.

The Traka 100 ens defineix. És la porta d’entrada i, per a molts, l’inici d’alguna cosa que es queda. La que ha fet que tants tornin, any rere any, a The Traka.

Al maig, cada dia un raig. I a l’última edició, la Traka 100 es va endur la seva part.
Aquí, un recull d’imatges de la passada edició.

Today, consultation closes on Australia’s new National Cultural Policy. 

Australia is a sporting nation – and that’s by design. Policy settings for culture need to mirror our national commitment to sport, embedding the arts into community life from childhood. 

Currently, the National Cultural Policy’s discussion of children is limited to in-school activities and engagement through digital platforms and television. We need to go further.

The benefits of arts, culture and creativity are far-reaching, delivering social and economic benefit to individuals, communities and the country. Participation in the arts strengthens belonging, identity, education, wellbeing, social cohesion, regional liveability and Australia’s relationship with the world.

Studies show that engaging children builds deep brand loyalty. This happens with sports – and even in banking, where children are given piggy banks to transition them into lifelong clients. 

For children to have the opportunity to engage in arts, culture and creativity, implementation requires adequate funding, and coordination across all jurisdictions and all levels of government. Just as the Australian Government invests heavily in road infrastructure for public safety, cultural investment is essential for public wellbeing. 

Countless studies haves shown that engaging with arts and culture provides profound physical and mental health benefits. This is critically important with the current epidemic of youth mental health challenges. Cultural events and community art programs bring people together, creating robust social support networks that prevent isolation which can lead to mental health challenges.

Durante a realização do Esquenta Miolo(s), o ciclo de atividades de formação que precede a Feira Miolo(s), o terceiro andar da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) se converteu em arena para diversos debates. Um deles foi a roda de conversa LIVRARIAS DE  RUA: QUEM SÃO, COMO VIVEM, DO QUE SE ALIMENTAM? O encontro aberto entre livreiros foi uma oportunidade para conhecer mais de perto as particularidades da cada livraria e quais caminhos são possíveis trilhar para manter estes espaços vivos e pulsantes. 

Feitas pela Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias), as fotos lembram como foi um evento legal, cheio de trocas e debates sobre livros 📚

#feiramiolos #miolos #esquentamiolos #lote42 #livrariasderua

É possível andar por uma rua como quem lê um livro? O que se esconde nos vincos, nas dobras e esquinas de uma região como a da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@mariodeandrade), cuja história se mistura com a da própria cidade? Questionamentos como esses nortearam A CIDADE NA PUBLICAÇÃO, atividade do Esquenta Miolo(s) que começou com uma caminhada pelo centro de São Paulo e terminou no auditório da biblioteca em uma conversa entre os artistas Ángela León (@angelaleon_ilustra), Ricardo Luis Silva (@por.onde.o.homem.anda) e Letícia Lampert (@leticia.lampert) – primeiro em movimento, depois estáticos, o fato é que foi uma conversa cheia de trocas sobre como olhar, pensar e habitar o espaço em que estamos inseridos. 

As fotos da Clara Dias (@clarinhaddias), da Jéssica de Souza Andrade (@jessicadesouzaandrade) e da Cecilia Arboalave (@ceciarbolave) nos levam de volta para lá 💫

#feiramiolos #miolos #esquentamiolos #lote42 #caminhada

Introducing Embodied Sacred Geometry derived from the Esoteric Acupuncture Template, in order to activate the Lightbody, expand consiousness, develop higher sensory perception, and increase coping capacity. 
New Encoding Pattern WorkshopSpirit Path is a guided activation through six gateways of the upper energy centres, awakening a spinning geometry of light that expands awareness while grounding higher frequencies into the body. Second Workshop Lightbody Activation

Drawing on meditation, Qigong, Integral Taoism, and Esoteric Acupuncture, this session teaches participants how to access and refine the octahedral energy field to support clarity, alignment, and energetic coherence. Steven Booth is a qualified Acupuncture Practitioner, senior qigong instructor, and Lightbody Activation facilitator. Trained in Esoteric Acupuncture under Dr Mikio Sankey, he specialises in meridian-based practice, Taoist internal arts, and expanded consciousness work. Perth Design Week extends our heartfelt congratulations to Peter Farmer Senior, Peter Farmer Junior and Miranda-Lee Farmer, following the unveiling of their new Olympic Team artwork yesterday, representing Australia on the world stage.

The Australian Olympic Committee (AOC) together with the AOC Indigenous Advisory Committee yesterday launched its ‘Stretch’ Reconciliation Action Plan and unveiled a powerful new Olympic Team artwork that together represent the next chapter of its commitment to reconciliation through sport.

The new Olympic Team artwork, titled ‘Doonch-doonch, Kaymelan, Together’ is a collaborative piece created by three artists, Peter Farmer Senior and Peter Farmer Junior from Noongar Country in Western Australia and Alick Tipoti from the Torres Strait.  

Meaning ‘coming together’ in Noongar and ‘together’ in Zenadth Kes (Torres Strait) the artwork is woven from these Indigenous visual languages and honours the 66 known Indigenous Olympians, carried together as a wave, an expression of unity across land, sea and sky. Across generations, communities and cultures it represents one shared story. 

The artwork will feature on the Australian Olympic Team uniforms in Los Angeles in 2028 and the French Alps in 2030.

“I’m extremely excited to be part of this project. As an artist for the athletes, I want them to feel proud and strong knowing this artwork was designed with thought and care when it comes to culture,” Peter Farmer Junior said.

An incredible achievement by Peter Farmer Senior, Peter Farmer Junior and Miranda Farmer, and a culmination of 30 years of leadership in art and design.

Image 1: Yesterday, Chair of the AOC Indigenous Advisory Committee, Patrick Johnson OLY, with artists Alick Tipoti from the Torres Strait and Peter Farmer Senior and Peter Farmer Junior from Noongar Country in Western Australia—and their new Olympic team artwork, titled ‘Doonch-doonch, Kaymelan, Together’, a collaborative piece created by the three artists. 
Images 2 and 3: At the launch of “Chirriger Moort: A 30‑Year Retrospective of the Work of Peter Farmer” at Perth Design Week in February 2026.

Thank you to our Major Partner Block Branding whose creative partnership continues to shape the @perthdesignweek identity with clarity and impact. Block Branding has been supporting Perth Design Week since the start in 2022, when all we had was the beautiful logo they created for us and a dream!

For 2026, the identity has been evolved by Block Senior Creative Jack McAuliffe, translating the Design is Everywhere platform into a physical form.

At the centre was a perspex board – a transparent device that captures and refracts the city around it. Photographed by Olivia Pizzale-Bryce across urban Perth, the identity quite literally reflects the built environment. Light, colour and texture are not added – they are revealed. 

As Braddock notes, “from the outset, Perth Design Week has been about making design visible – not as something applied, but as something already present,” with this year’s identity simply reflecting the city back to itself.

@perthdesignweek 2026 concluded last week with our final conversation titled “Designing with Purpose.” This session highlighted individuals who create with intention, emphasizing that design should serve a deeper purpose beyond aesthetics. Design is a process that involves making choices that positively impact the world, focusing on sustainability, social justice, and cultural significance.

Key takeaways from our panelists included:

- Durability over cheap fixes: A preference for steel subframes and reparable, modular products to enhance longevity and reduce waste. (Chris Cooke)
- Social design delivers high value-for-money: Community-led, low-cost, locally sourced solutions yield meaningful outcomes. (Joni Sercombe)
- Climate-responsive housing matters: Simple principles like north-facing orientation and designing according to local sun and wind patterns significantly improve liveability and cost-effectiveness. (Matt Delroy-Carr)
- Market levers shifting: Banks, reporting, and emerging home energy ratings are beginning to reward well-performing designs, potentially disrupting real estate choices. (Karla Fox-Reynolds)
- Design for people, not aesthetics only: ‘Queer design’ framing focuses on creating spaces that support lived experiences rather than adhering to stereotypical aesthetics. (Matthew McGivern)

Thank you to our panellists and our moderator, champion for Perth, Paula Rogers, who expertly guiding this multidisciplinary panel. 

This event was presented by @perthdesignweek with @kingliving 

Thank you to Kahn Morkaya, Tom Acton and King Living. The financial and in-kind support of our sponsors and partners is vital for Perth Design Week to continue to exist and deliver on its primary mission to elevate Perth’s creative and design sector.

It was standing room only for our “Living Large in Small Spaces” conversation at Perth Design Week, with a passionate conversation on apartment design.

- a shift in the Australian Dream, from people seeing apartment living as inferior to a four by two with a big backyard, to changing perceptions on what constitutes amenity

How we can “stretch the day” in Perth, evolving into a city that is vibrant, connected and active around the clock? That was one of the topics we explored at PDW 2026.

Award-winning journalist and architecture and design advocate Claire Tyrrell guided an engaging with panellists James Sutherland (Arcade Agency), Jim Tsagalis (Lease Equity), Kyle Jeavons (Human-Urban), Natalie Busch (Hassell), Samantha Stewart (URBIS) and Sean Henriques (Edith Cowan University). 

The discussion considered the many layers that shape a truly liveable urban environment — from major civic initiatives and education precincts to the everyday experience of retail, dining and well-designed public spaces. Panellists also reflected on Perth’s existing strengths — its climate, lifestyle, natural landscapes and evolving hospitality scene — and the need for greater coordination and critical mass to fully realise the city’s potential.

Thank you to @humanurban and @urbis_au for sponsoring the event enabling this important conversation. PDW is about design at all scales, all working to a common goal to improve how we all live and work here in Western Australia. Because design is everywhere and for everyone.

Perth Design Week 2026 officially wrapped up 10 days ago. While we planned a “smaller” festival this year, the scope of our condensed, curated program ended up being our largest yet. This increased scale required a significant team effort, and I was fortunate to work alongside some very dedicated individuals. I would like to specifically recognise:

 - Eugene Hooks: For establishing PDW Local HQ and securing our 10 exhibitors. Local HQ was a first for PDW and it was great to have a headquarters for the festival. 
 - Amy Clark: For stepping in for Eugene (now travelling for his Churchill Fellowship) and managing the logistics of Local HQ. Amy clocked some serious hours to get HQ up and running - getting ten exhibitors, with many truckloads of furniture, in and out of a theatre was not an easy task.
 - Fiona Kalaf: For joining us this year to write our newsletters and social media posts. Promotion of PDW is primarily via Instagram, which means many posts - this year over 120 in 5 weeks.
 - Amber Sheldon: For taking care of PR for us and faciltating coverage across a broad range of media, from WA Today and ABC Perth, through to national and international design magazines. Amber has been with PDW since the start. 
 - Juliana Torres, Andree McIntyre, and Reinette Roux: For their strategic board leadership and hands-on event coordination.
 - Jason Bo and Tim Stacey: For volunteering their time to assist with coordination at Local HQ.
- And our unofficial PDW team member, Randal Humich, Liberty Theatre building owner: for always being around to lend a hand. 

Thank you everyone!
Sandy Anghie
PDW Chair and Founder

Neste fim de semana, nos dias 8 e 9 de novembro, acontece a 12ª edição da Feira Miolo(s) na Mário! ✨

O evento reúne mais de 280 expositores, entre editores independentes, artistas gráficos, livrarias de rua e ateliês de impressão de diversos cantos do Brasil - além de outros pontos da América Latina - para exporem suas obras e compartilharem experiências da produção gráfica alternativa.

Além da feira de publicações, o evento conta com vivências de impressão em serigrafia, gravação ao vivo de podcast no auditório e performances de leitura. 

No Corredor de Vidro, que conecta as entradas da biblioteca, estarão duas mostras: uma de lançamentos dos participantes e também “100 em 10: Arte impressa no acervo da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade”, coordenada pelo artista Gustavo Piqueira (@gustavopiqueira), que apresenta 10 itens raros e evidenciam a vocação da BMA em abrigar obras e pensamentos de vanguarda.

Produzida pela editora Lote 42 (@lote42), a Feira Miolo(s) acontece na Biblioteca Mário de Andrade desde 2014.

Rhythms of Nature: The creative blueprint for the new paradigm | Saturday, 12pm at the Grove

For 4.5 billion years, life on Earth has evolved through nature’s cyclical rhythms – the cycles of the day, the moon and the seasons. Whether we’re aware of them or not, our ability to survive and thrive depends on how well we align with these rhythms. Join Charlotte @herinnerwilderness in exploring the creative blueprint of the Rhythms of Nature and learn how to work with rather than against them, to create greater wellbeing for yourself, your community, and the planet. 

Charlotte guides you back to your unique rhythm and into alignment with nature’s cycles – drawing on two degrees in psychology and ongoing studies of the nervous system, chronobiology, therapeutic yoga, and a range of energy healing modalities. She has specialised training and 7+ years of experience in supporting women with menstrual or (peri-)menopause challenges.

“Participar da banca de jurados da Tattoo Week sempre foi um grande objetivo, e finalmente poderei estar junto a grandes nomes da tattoo, no maior evento de tatuagem do mundo fazendo a diferença.

É uma grande responsabilidade para com todos os competidores envolvidos e, com certeza, estou muito feliz em poder usar todo o meu conhecimento para trazer um resultado merecido ao pódio. E espero contar com todos para que esse seja mais um ano incrível para o mundo da tattoo”, disse @rafaelsucharski_angeltattoo .

“Fazer parte da bancada de jurados da Tattoo Week é muito mais do que ocupar um lugar diante de grandes trabalhos. É viver um momento que representa anos de dedicação, escolhas, renúncias, aprendizado e amor pela tatuagem.

Estar entre os profissionais escolhidos para avaliar artistas em um dos maiores e mais importantes palcos da tatuagem mundial é uma honra imensurável e uma responsabilidade que recebo com profundo respeito.

A Tattoo Week representa a força da nossa arte. Um evento que atravessa fronteiras, reúne grandes nomes, revela talentos e contribui para elevar a tatuagem ao lugar de reconhecimento e excelência que ela merece.

Minha gratidão a toda a organização pela confiança e pela oportunidade de fazer parte dessa história. Depois de tantos anos dedicados à tatuagem, estar ali, não apenas como artista, mas como jurado, tem um significado muito especial para mim”, disse @verissimotattoo .

É a confirmação de que cada passo valeu a pena.

Passamos o final de semana olhando as publicações que artistas, coletivos e editoras da 12a Miolo(s) mandaram para a mostra de lançamentos. 

Há livros que tratam sobre bairros e cidades. Outros que exploram de forma radical a materialidade. Há também fanzines temáticos. E livros para infâncias, obras de não ficção, quadrinhos, gravuras. Há muita coisa nos lançamentos de 2025.

Aos poucos a mostra vai ganhando forma! 
Ao colocar todos na mesa fomos encontrando relações entre os trabalhos e pensando em como colocá-los nas três mesas expositivas no final de semana da Miolo(s). 

Não se esqueça: a mostra estará no Corredor de Vidro da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) nos dois dias da feira.

#feiramiolos #mostradelancamentos #bibliotecamariodeandrade

Ever gone somewhere alone… and left with a whole new tribe? 👀

That’s the magic of Wellfest ☀️

It’s the festival you can go to solo — and somehow never feel alone. 

In fact, going on your own might be the best way to experience it.

When you arrive open, everything shifts. 

Conversations spark after a yoga class. Strangers smile at you during breathwork. Hugs last a little longer. Eye contact feels deeper. Wholesome connection isn’t awkward — it’s encouraged. ✨

At Wellfest, titles and job descriptions don’t matter. Everyone is there to feel good, grow, move, and reset. The usual barriers soften, and people meet you exactly where you are.

You’ll chat barefoot with someone you’ve known for five minutes like they’re an old friend. Share snacks. Stories. Laugh during workshops. Make sunset plans. And suddenly your “solo” camping weekend has turned into a new group with plans for dinner next week. 

Strangers become besties in no time.

Go alone.
Find your tribe.
Leave more alive and with your cup overflowing 🥰

O que faz o diretor de uma biblioteca pública? E quando essa biblioteca tem um século de vida e uma história que se entrelaça com a história do Brasil? Que futuros são possíveis de imaginar para as bibliotecas brasileiras, e qual o papel dos editores e artistas independentes nisso? Essas são algumas das perguntas que dão o tom do novo episódio do Papo Tatuí com Rodrigo Massi (@massi_rodrigo), atual diretor da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) e Secretário-Adjunto da Secretária Municipal de Cultura e Economia Criativa de São Paulo.

Intitulado A BIBLIOTECA CENTENÁRIA, o episódio ainda traz informações sobre o legado de Mário de Andrade na cidade de São Paulo e – é claro! – novidades sobre a 12ª edição da Feira Miolo(s) (@feiramiolos), parceria entre a Biblioteca Mário de Andrade e a Lote 42 (@lote42) que ocupa a biblioteca nos dias 8 e 9 de novembro, das 11h às 19h, com mais de 280 expositores e diversas atividades em torno da produção gráfica independente. 

O podcast foi gravado na Cabine Tatuí e já está disponível no Spotify e em outras plataformas que você encontra ali no link da bio (@salatatui)

Mediação: João Varella | Coordenação: Cecilia Arbolave (@ceciarbolave) | Produção: Ian Uviedo (@ian_uviedo) e Julia Carvalho (@carva_lia) | Operação técnica, captação e edição de áudio: Ian Uviedo

Ever wondered what lies behind the historic façades of our city? This is your chance to step inside The Liberty Theatre – a hidden Perth landmark reopened especially for @perthdesignweek 

Originally opening on 1 March 1954 as Perth’s first dedicated art house cinema, The Liberty was designed by Krantz & Sheldon to screen foreign-language and European films within an intimate, contemporary setting. While its life as a speciality cinema was relatively brief, the venue continued to evolve, screening diverse film genres until the early 1990s.

Today, thanks to current owner Randal Humich and the Humich Group, the theatre has been carefully reimagined as a live music and cultural venue. Since reopening in 2022 it has hosted events for Perth Fringe Festival and Perth Design Week – once again bringing audiences together to experience creativity in a historic setting.

Where Sound Meets the Cosmos

Tasmanian composer Constantine Koukias returns from Amsterdam with Dutch sound designer Willem van Erven Dorens to unveil a groundbreaking work that transforms the invisible force of Dark Energy into a live sonic spectacle. This site-specific work has been created for Beaker Street Festival and the Theatre Royal.

Forget conventional concerts. Inside a transformed Theatre Royal, a bespoke spatial‑audio system reshapes the room into a 360° universe of sound, where more than 120 recorded voices and 80 instrumentalists break apart into sonic “particles” that swirl, collide, and drift like unstable matter in an invisible field. What you hear depends entirely on where you sit. No two seats share the same journey.

The international ensemble features Australian pianist Gabriella Smart, American soprano Katharine Dain, English tenor Tyrone Landau, Tasmanian musicians Jennifer Owen (violin) and Yoram Levy (trumpet), Celia Craig (Cor Anglais, SA), Greg Gurr (sound supervisor), Jason James (lighting designer), and Donald Bate (live delay operator).

A cada dia que passa a Feira Miolo(s) fica mais perto e nós estamos adorando compartilhar com vocês todas as novidades desta 12ª edição! 

Pela primeira vez na história do evento, em 2025 o auditório da Biblioteca Mário de Andrade (@bibliotecamariodeandrade) sedia a gravação ao vivo de um podcast com participantes da feira. 

O Papo Tatuí é produzido pela Sala Tatuí (@salatatui), um dos projetos da Lote 42 (@lote42), editora que organiza a Miolo(s). Com apresentação do João Varella (@joaovarella), o Papo Tatuí é um podcast dedicado às ideias que movem a cultura gráfica independente. Ou seja: nada mais a fim com o espírito da Miolo(s)! 

São 12 participantes, que apresentamos neste post. As gravações acontecem no Auditório Mário de Andrade, no primeiro andar, às 12h, 15h e 17h do sábado e do domingo. No site você já encontra os detalhes de cada fala. 

Ah! E para acompanhar, só presencialmente! Não haverá transmissão pelas redes, porém os seis episódios serão depois editados e publicados no canal do Papo Tatuí. 

Apareça na feira e acompanhe as falas, entre um zine e um pôster, uma conversa e uma venda, um livro e um outro livro

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #704 | 23 APRIL 2026
Another week of amazing perfect blue skies, almost unheard of. The bananas in the sun-drier are the winners and popular with the MardiGrass volunteers. It’s all go now, getting ready for the big weed weekend. Jingles has both the Indica Arena and Sativa Stadium stages built, and the Hemp Olympix field is in perfect condition.

This favourite event at MardiGrass evolved from the police directing us to get the crowds off the Village’s one main street. Sydney was gearing up for their Olympics and we thought, “Let’s educate everybody who thinks stoners lie around idle all day”.

The Bong Throw and Yell is pretty straightforward but the Growers Ironperson Event is seriously difficult. Sativa Stadium has a steep downhill slope which contestants have to traverse while carrying a bag of fertiliser first, followed by a bucket of water and finally a run to collect the stash. Each run includes crawling through a lantana tunnel laced with leeches and ticks.

That bit’s to educate visitors on the efforts people have to go through to grow them some organic bush weed. Now-a-days the most some do is making sure the light’s working. Times sure have changed. Same with the Speed Roll in the Joint Rolling. Three papers and a filter, who does that anymore? Cultural art forms that are already antiquated.

There are experts speaking (if I dare use this overworked title), on all aspects of cannabis. However, the Hemp Olympix will draw the biggest crowds next weekend—aside from the main events in our main drag—the Rally on the Sunday, and the Saturday 420 Blaze at the end of the Kombi Konvoy!

The endless research looking for some sense of certainty on what cannabis does or doesn’t do to you goes on and on. Yes it helps with cancer and sleep and a zillion other conditions and yes, again, “prenatal cannabis exposure is not associated with negative cognitive outcomes at adolescence”.

Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

2026 is now underway! Thank you to everyone who joined us last night for our Opening Conversation “Designing the Future.” The event began with a Welcome to Country by Dr. Leonard Collard, followed by an address from Hon. Simone McGurk MLA, Minister for Creative Industries, who emphasized the critical role of design and creative industries.

“Designing the Future” was a significant topic, and Ella Loneragan did an excellent job moderating. Here are some key takeaways from the event:

- “AI doesn’t ‘care’. We need humans in the process.” - Julian Bolleter, Director of the Australian Urban Design Research Centre at The University of Western Australia.
- “Creating spaces and experiences that encourage intercultural understanding, build intentional future Australian identity through the truth of its past, despite the discomfort this is where we can grow to understand ourselves as a nation and design for the future.” - Ilona McGuire, multidisciplinary artist.
- “We need to make the tough calls when it comes to sustainability.” - Huia Adkins, GHD Sustainability and Circular Economy Portfolio Lead, and Circular Economy WA Chairperson.
- “Design is expanding beyond making pretty things, and we are now engaging in complex systemic change. Designers need to focus on generating processes, not just objects, that cultivate sustainable change.” - Chris Kueh, Associate Professor of Design at Edith Cowan University.
- “Fostering design practice and creative practice research is a way to reclaim agency in the age of AI. Designers are in a unique position to reimagine the ecologies of the future with and without machines.” - Claudia Westermann, Associate Professor of Creative Practice in the School of Design and the Built Environment at Curtin University.
- “The built environment is uniquely placed, with existing technologies, to move beyond net zero to net positive.” - Simon Blackwell, Associate at HIP V. HYPE.

We look forward to many more great conversations over the next week!

🌿Workshop Announcement: Dr Tonya Cruikshank - The guts of it: where soul meets science 🌿

Join for Tonya an experiential & interactive exploration of the gut as a living ecosystem — where nervous system science, protective parts, and embodied awareness meet to create the conditions for true healing.
Dr. Tonya Cruikshank is a Whole Health Specialist, Emotional Health Expert, and IFS Practitioner working at the intersection of gut science and embodied healing. She explores the gut not simply as a digestive organ, but as a living ecosystem shaped by nervous system rhythms, emotional history, and the protective parts that work tirelessly to keep us safe.

Integrating microbiome research, polyvagal theory, and Internal Family Systems, her work invites people to understand the intelligence behind patterns of control and efforting — recognising that these strategies often protect deeper pain or grief. Rather than overriding them, she guides a grounded, embodied form of self-compassion that creates the safety required for true digestive healing.

Tonya works individually with clients and curates transformative spaces that bridge science and soul — weaving medicine, somatic movement, mindfulness, and neurodiversity-informed care into an integrated approach to whole-person healing.

✨ Second Offering with Chelita Zainey ✨
We’re honoured to share that Chelita will be offering a second workshop at WellFest 2026 — alongside Rua Pick and Michelle Crofts.

Introduction to Māori Healing Arts
An opportunity to explore and deepen your understanding of the Māori healing arts in a grounded, respectful and welcoming space.

Together, Chelita, Rua and Michelle will share insights into: • Mirimiri (traditional bodywork)
• Taonga Pūoro (ancestral sound healing instruments)
• Rongoā Māori (traditional plant medicine)
Rooted in Indigenous wisdom and lived experience, this session invites curiosity, questions, and open-hearted learning. It’s a chance to connect with the wonder and potency of the medicines of Aotearoa, and to better understand the foundations of Māori approaches to healing and wellbeing.

As a Māori healer, mentor and Kai Mirimiri, Kai Rongoā and Kai Pūoro practitioner, Chelita brings deep knowledge, care and integrity to this space — guided by manaakitanga and a commitment to uplifting the mana of others.

We’re grateful to have her sharing not one, but two powerful offerings with us this year 🌿
Join us at WellFest 2026.

Valentine’s Day gets a lot of airtime for romance.
But at WellFest, love starts somewhere closer.

It starts with how we show up for ourselves.
How we listen in quiet moments.
How we rest when we need to.
How we choose ourselves — gently, without performance.

From there, love widens.

It shows up in community — shared meals, honest conversations, moments that linger.
In friendship — dancing barefoot, laughing under open skies.
In family — little hands exploring, big smiles by the fire.
In partnership — moving together, side by side, through music and presence.
In nature — river water, earth under feet, nights that slow us down.

And sometimes, in unexpected connection.

However you arrive, whatever you’re carrying — you’re welcome here.

Happy Valentine’s Day from the WellFest whānau 🌿

✨ Interior Design Case Studies ✨

Join Alona Klaro of @klaro_industrial_design - along with two other panellists - as she explores what happens between design intent and realised outcome, shedding light on the decisions, constraints and trade-offs that shape projects.

A sculptor, interior designer and product designer, Alona draws on her range of unique skills and outlook to create products where design intent captures not only the object's visual language, but the process and locality of manufacture, materials, supply chain, user experience and end of life. 

🎟️ Tickets to Interior Design Case Studies via link in bio or www.perthdesignweek.com includes catering and drinks, and access to Local HQ

At this event, three Western Australian interior design practices will each present a 20-minute case study, covering a completed project from early intent through to delivery. Presentations will delve deeper than polished imagery to examine how ideas were tested, challenged and translated into built outcomes. Speakers will offer insight into how design ambition is negotiated and sustained through the life of a project.

We started with an array of products - tiles, sculptures, and a whole lot of ideas.

Inspired by the Paesaggi concept of abstract landscapes, I began building a series of small sculptural structures - experimenting with form, repetition, and how these pieces could stack, balance, and interact.

This is the FreakHaus way: pulling patterns, textures, and repetition from individual elements to create something bigger, bolder, and a little unexpected.

What started as a few playful experiments quickly evolved into a landscape of shapes, structures, and ceramic moments - not to mention a fun use of materials, with everyday Italian staples reimagined as art. 🍝 🥖 

Design Week officially kicks off today, so if you’re in Perth, swing by the Myaree Ceramics display and see our very fun, very playful collab come to life. ✨

HEMP EMBASSY HEADLINES #703 | 16 APRIL 2026
An amazing cloudless week like I can’t remember in ages and still it’s predicted to continue. Beautiful big blue sky, day after day. I lived on Patmos in Greece for a couple of years and we would have month after month after month of pure blue sky, never a cloud, but it’s rare here at this time of year.

We wrote to our Legalise Cannabis members in the Farrer electorate looking for a candidate for the by-election and we hit the jackpot with Aimee Pearson. She’s a pharmacist whose husband’s Multiple Sclerosis awoke her to the wonders of cannabis for pain relief. She would be using it herself for a spinal arthritis condition but won’t risk losing her licence. 

Honestly I believe hundreds of thousands of other Australians, possibly millions, won’t use ‘mediweed’ in case they lose their licence. And we know the money-god is making all the decisions, so who profits from this? Easy to work out.few plants at home. 

There’s a story below about Americans now worried about pesticides in their pot and wanting to grow their own. There’s been many stories about bad chem’s in legal irradiated weed so no wonder homegrown organic is still so popular, even if it costs twice as much. 

It makes absolute sense in multiple ways to grow our own medicine, and have a relationship with the plants we use. Just like growing our own veggies. Is that still legal?! We’ve lost our connection with the Earth for now, it’s ironic, we’ll all end up in there.

Otherwise my life is being swallowed by MardiGrass, for the next few weeks. Our prime guest, Ethan Nadelman, is attracting great interest. In 1988, Ethan wrote a major critique of US drug policy. Billionaire George Soros read it and realised the ‘war on drugs’ was doing more harm than good. 

The two of them joined forces, and drug law reform moved from the fringe to mainstream, with George investing millions into the movement. Harm reduction became their catch cry as they formed the Drug Policy Alliance and became nationally influential. Here’s hoping he can give us some clues on how to move forward here, Down Under, when he visits.
Love to everyone!
Michael Balderstone
Nimbin HEMP Embassy Head

🇦🇺 🇧🇪 INTERNATIONAL RESIDENCY OPPORTUNITY FOR WA COMIC MAKERS 🇧🇪 🇦🇺

The Perth Comic Arts Festival, in association with the Musée de la Bande Dessinée @comicartmuseumbxl, is very proud to present the first comics-artist residency in Brussels available to Western Australian artists.
Between October and December 2026, for three weeks, the Museum is hosting Belgian and international comic artists in Brussels for an artistic residency. This residency, with the support of PCAF, is available to a Western Australian comics-maker. The residency will bring together artists to share, explore, and inspire one another.

The Museum undertakes to organize the residency with the Artist to enable them to work optimally on their project, following the Artist for the duration of the residency and doing its best to:
🗯️ Provide help and advice on their work
🗯️ Share professional contacts and facilitate meetings
🗯️ Invite the Artist to public or networking events that would happen during its stay
🗯️ Include the Artist in the Museum activities, if the programming allows it
🗯️ The Museum will also provide the artist with 50€ per diem for up to 21 days

PCAF will support the artist by:
🗯️ Assisting the artist with finding accommodation in Brussels for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $3000 AUD towards accommodation costs for the duration of the residency
🗯️ Provide $2000 AUD towards return flight costs to Brussels from Perth

WHO CAN APPLY?
Comic artists meeting all of the following criteria:
🗯️ A practicing comics artist based in Western Australia with a graphic novel or long-form comic currently in process
🗯️ An Australian citizen or Permanent Resident with an up-to-date passport
🗯️ At least 18 years of age

Please head to pcaf.org.au/2026-brussels-residency for full details on the residency and the application guidelines! 

IMPORTANT DATES
🗯️ Applications open: 26th of July, 2026
🗯️ Applications close: 14th of August, 2026
🗯️ Applicants notified: 31st of August, 2026
🗯️ Residency Period: 3 continuous weeks, between the 10th of October and 15th of December (to be decided in consultation with PCAF and the Museum).

📰 💛 2026 Tale Town – Survival of the Friendliest 💛 📰

The publication commissions new works from comics-makers who are asked to engage with the theme of the year’s Festival. One of the recurring compliments PCAF receives each year is about how friendly it is, this is a quality we strive to have but we do at times take it for granted. In actuality friendliness is one of those priceless phenomena that could do with a celebration and acknowledgment of its intangible but important presence.

Our society has long been preoccupied with the myth of the ‘Alpha Wolf’, a dominant, aggressive, masculine figure within social groups that all others submit to. Even the elegant theory of “Survival of the Fittest” is routinely misrepresented as being about a physical, powerful “fitness”, rather than the ability to “fit in.” 

But there is another theory, that of “Survival of the Friendliest”. Which is an idea that organisms throughout history have thrived and succeeded not in domination over each other, but through their ability to collaborate, coordinate and find comrades in life.

The theme for this year’s festival is “Survival of the Friendliest” and we are encouraging artists to reflect on the role of “friendliness” in their communities, in their professional practices and in their personal politics.

Cover Art by Stefanie Palladino 
Curated by Elizabeth Marruffo

⭐ 2026 Poster + Theme Reveal! ⭐

Take a look at the poster for the 2026 festival! Illustrated by the talented Steve Christie with art direction from our creative director Elizabeth Murraffo. The theme for PCAF 2026 is "Survival of the Friendliest".

One of the recurring compliments PCAF receives each year is about how friendly it is, this is a quality we strive to have but we do at times take it for granted. In actuality friendliness is one of those priceless phenomena that could do with a celebration and acknowledgement of its intangible but important presence. 

Our society has long been preoccupied with the myth of the 'Alpha Wolf', a dominant, aggressive, masculine figure within social groups that all others submit to. Even the elegant theory of "Survival of the Fittest" is routinely misrepresented as being about a physical, powerful "fitness", rather than the ability to "fit in."

But there is another theory, that of "Survival of the Friendliest". Which is an  idea that organisms throughout history have thrived and succeeded not in domination over each other, but through their ability to collaborate, coordinate and find comrades in life.

The theme for this year's festival is "Survival of the Friendliest" and we are encouraging artists to reflect on the role of "friendliness" in their communities, in their professional practices and in their personal politics.

If you would like to download a free printable copy of the poster visit to our website at https://pcaf.org.au/poster/

🗡📚 The Killing of Books 📚🗡

Welcome to 2026, where words and books are treated as more dangerous than guns and bombs. Kim Hyun Sook and Ryan Estrada know this better than most. Their award winning (and banned in multiple states across the USA) graphic novel, Banned Book Club, tells the true story of Hyun Sook's experience at college in South Korea where she was part of a secret literary club that read books that had been banned by the state government. 

Hyun Sook and Ryan will join award winning author Sarah Winifred Searle to discuss the power of graphic novels and the threat that book bans pose to our freedoms.
